review_text:
The new restaurant right in the middle of Lincoln Center, from Chef Kwame Onwuachi, as the name obviously indicates.

All the food we tried was great, served in a gorgeous dining room with views of the Revson Fountain and the rest of Lincoln Center surrounding it.

It's obviously not cheap given the location, but well worth it especially for dishes like the Curried Goat Patties ($18 for 3) and the Hamachi Escovitch ($22) to start, followed by the Short Rib Pastrami Suya ($50), a show stopper of an entree.

Don't leave without the Rainbow Cookie Panna Cotta ($16) too, the only dessert currently, with more additions apparently coming soon (I'm going to need to come back for those Truffled Chopped Cheese Buns from all of the opening press that wasn't yet on the menu tonight).

It's going to be very easy to rave about the food  and ambiance and the staff. The flavor choices are bold and exciting, yet the chicken reminded me of a Sunday family dinner but with a dynamic element of a little heat and the acidity of the lime. I really enjoyed the Peri Peri salad. Savory with a kick of heat and then bursts of sweetness with the grapes. The mushrooms were my absolute favorite. Meaty and yet balanced well with the ginger and plum sauce. 

Highly recommend! Kwame Onwuachi has brought a fantastic dining experience to New York that is fresh and new yet the food tastes comforting and familial. We dined at the bar and ended up having fantastic conversations with the staff and the people sitting next to us. From the ambiance to the food to the people - it's a place you want to be. 

Such a great evening out! Everything 5 stars! I only wish I could give it more.

Wedged in the middle of Lincoln Center, literally a stone's throw away from the fountain, Tatiana shouldn't be good.  It should be overpriced and unoriginal food in a sterilized box filled with theatergoers and tourists.

But as his Top Chef devotees and other acolytes know well, Kwame Onwuachi has never been one to adhere to convention.  And so it is fitting that in his first foray into restaurant ownership in his hometown, Chef Kwame has planted a genuinely cool and unique restaurant smack in the middle of a quintessential tourist trap.

The small, dimly lit dining room has a certain energy to it, enclosed in floor-to-ceiling glass windows looking out onto the Center and glowing in ambient light piped in through new-age light fixtures that look like they were taken from outer space.  The space is sleek and stylish, but warm and inviting too.  

But what sets Tatiana apart are the menu and the food.  Noah X is not sure that he has ever had elevated Caribbean before (Miss Lily's doesn't count).  But he left this meal wondering where this cuisine had been all his life.  

As he tucked into his first of several goat patties, he began to contemplate whether he would be satisfied eating these and only these for the rest of his life.  (He would.)  And the piri piri salad was surprisingly delightful, the perfect amalgam of sweet, salt, acid, and heat.  For dinner, the pastrami short rib is a signature dish (though should come with a side of a Lipitor prescription and Tums).  It ate beautifully, as the meat fell off the bone and melded together perfectly with the bright cabbage to cut through the fat.

The drinks are not to be missed, either--brilliantly-crafted and inventive cocktails that arrive to your table quickly.  

In an age where so many new restaurants elevate style over substance, Tatiana proves that you can have both.  Tourists, boomers, millenials, and TikTokers unite:  you will all enjoy this place.

I cannot recommend highly enough. Excellent food and great vibes. Kwame was working the floor - which I loved. He introduced himself to us, and nearly every table. You can just tell this is his passion, dancing and singing to old school Usher with staff. Food rundown:

-Dumplings - 8.5/10, go great w/ house hot sauce
-Truffled Chopped Cheese - 7/10, tbh a little dry
-Mushrooms - 11/10, honestly the best thing ever
-Pastrami Suya - 10.5/10, an absolute must try 

Personally obsessed with the mushrooms. One of the best things I've ever eaten. Mushrooms, scallion pancakes.. plum sauce?! Epic.

Suya was just as good as I had read, short rib fell off the bone. Rolls also 10/10, dead.

TL;DR surprisingly vibrant energy for Lincoln Center - 1000% get either the mushrooms or suya

Kaydene is wonderful. We came here because I have known SOMM Amy from Sons & Daughter Michelin Stared in San Francisco. Saw her post on IG, then realize chef Kwame Onwuachi we met him at James Beard Foundation Award event in Chicago 2021. We were sitting on his table where he spoke!

I love to support minority chef and the kind of food that warm my belly and my heart :-) the server got me the fresh chili , I appreciate it so much!

The style is Afro Caribbean opening at Lincoln Center, at 10 Lincoln Center Plaza, near Columbus Avenue. This is chef Onwuachi's first in New York, is an homage to the chef's roots in Nigeria, Jamaica, Trinidad, New Orleans, and his upbringing in New York. They open for dinner on November in the gorgeous a $550 million newly renovated at the center's David Geffen Hall.

Taking his experience from Michelin-starred Per Se and Eleven Madison Park, chef Onwuachi was also the contestant on Top Chef. He opened with 2 popular spots in Washington D.C.: the Shaw Bijou, a fine dining Kith and Kin, where chef was won a James Beard award in 2019 -- and resigned roughly a year later.

We love everything and every dish we had! The bomb rib. Melt in your mouth, falling apart by itself, oh you are so meaty goodness!

The Goat curry, the rice and peas, the truffle cheese, wish I have a second belly to indulge it all. I look like 6 months Preggo when we are done! HA!

The wine list is so reasonable for this part of town and worldwide list, many bottles under $100, unheard of price point here!

The cocktails is yummy! 

The service is impeccable, genuine, and I love to see faces that represent the food and culture.

Wishing you success chef, I'm a FAN. 

Book your reservation ASAP! Tell them @1MandaBear send you :)

Totally blown away with how amazing our experience was at Tatiana!  The ambiance of the restaurant is absolutely stunning, and we were warmly welcomed & promptly seated.  We ordered a wide variety of the menu & absolutely loved everything we had.  The egusi dumplings were a perfect starter, along with the hamachi, the lamb hummus & the scallops.  Everything was filled with flavor and so creative & innovative.  Another standout was the truffle chopped cheese, a high end take on a NY classic & absolutely divine!  We ordered both the pastrami & shrimps as our mains & loved both.  The pastrami was so tender, definitely the best I've ever tried.  It comes with bread & cabbage, making it the perfect complete dish.  The shrimps are huge & full of flavor from the buttery sauce, delicious.  We finished off with the rainbow cookie panna cotta for desert which was the perfect light way to end our epic meal.  Cocktails were also creative & refreshing.  Service was 10/10, very attentive & gave great recommendations on the menu.  We cannot wait to come back & try kwame's other fantastic dishes.  There is nowhere else like tatiana!

Wow, what a treat dining at Tatiana. We shared the egusi dumplings, truffle chopped cheese, take-out mushrooms, sofrito roasted chicken, rice, and bodega special. We did not have one bad bite all night.

The dumplings were perfectly seared. The truffle chopped cheese paired well with the ribeye and had a nicely balanced flavor. The take-out mushrooms were exceptional. The texture of the mushrooms was perfect with a delightful umami flavor. The chicken was unbelievable - amazingly juicy and moist, perfectly roasted, with a delicious stew around it. The rice was actually one of the best rices I've ever had. The bodega special was good too - a clever take on a nostalgic favorite and creative with the powdered donut ice cream.

I can't wait to coming back. Highly recommend!

First thing to know: you are in for a treat! From the service, to the overall dining experience, and oh yea, the tunes playing in the background (contemporary hip-hop and r&b). I came on a Tuesday night, and needless to say, it was a vibe. 

Now, let's get to the food! Note: the flavors were bold, authentic and simultaneously sophisticated. 

Small Plates: Egusi Dumplings (one of my favs, though egusi isn't something I eat frequently). Each dumpling was packed with flavors and a punch of spice. The Curried Goat Pastries were also incredible  (definitely one of their classic hit). Lastly, the Truffle Chopped Cheese. Now, if you're a person who've had a chopped cheese or grew up eating them (from a corner store), don't expect those same flavors. This is definitely a more refined version, and although different, it was a great bite-- worth trying for sure! 

Entrees: The Mom Dukes Shrimps were off the chain! Perfectly cooked, great size, and o-m-g that sauce! Not to mention the perfectly buttered toast it's paired with.. that thing just melts in your mouth, whew! We also ordered the braised oxtails of course, which were pretty good (don't expect them to be spicy though). 

Highlight of my experience: Chef Kwame calling me out for eating the oxtail with a fork and knife! "What are you doing? Now I know you know how to eat oxtails.... This is home, you better pick it up and eat it!" 

Highly, highly recommend. High-end dining with a twist of home!
What an addition to the area, and all of New York.  Amazing ambiance, upbeat and alive but also refined dining.  Great drinks, too.  Can't wait to come back very very often.

Upscale fine dining and at an affordable price. GOD, Chef Kwame just marry me already! Okay, not me, but I absolutely loved everything about this restaurant.  First, I was floored by the affordability of the menu and wine selection. I am happy that TATIANA is an upscale restaurant that is not exclusive. In its 4th week, the TATIANA staffing provided a professional, warm, fun, and flawless fine dining experience. It was the hostesses for me! The moment I saw these lovely ladies I knew we were going to have a great time. I DID NOT feel as if I was walking into a country club seeking approval. Our server Jake was an awesome guide for the evening, helped us make good selections. The sommelier, Andrew, was pleasant and patient as we talked through wine selections. He even started us off with some bubbles as we finalized our decision (appreciate that). But what made US feel appreciated is that Chef Kwame made his rounds checking in on guest and even stopping for a little conversation. He is charismatic and it made me smile to see this young brotha working his floor. TATIANA is a beautiful space (beautiful and clean bathroom). You can tell that they really do work towards inclusivity and want this to be a restaurant where all can come and enjoy the fire ass food!

THE FOOD - nothing salty, perfectly balanced seasonings and flavors. No condiments needed! Although the scotch bonnet pepper sauce was 

Cucumber Salad: ma'am. What. The flavors bursting in my mouth! These little Pearl radishes and bits of minty to off set some of the spice. Absolutely delicious. 

Egusi Crab Dumplings: perfect. Just perfect. Just...perfect. Perfect crisp. 

Take-Out Mushrooms: laaaawd! Our server was right, definitely a stand out dish that got you thinking about it days later. Never have I had a mushroom dish so tasty, so filling, so impressive. I did not love their spin on the scallion pancake, it was too pancake/waffle batter like for my preference, but best believe I hate a few slices. Just a wonderful dish. 

Brown Stew Snapper: hella good. I'm trying to understand where they found boneless/eyeless whole fish at LOL this was a very tasty fish that I enjoyed with some of the scotch bonnet pepper sauce. I definitely wanted more of the stewed onions that were on top but a perfectly seasoned dish nonetheless. 

Excited to follow Chef Kwame's journey. If y'all got his Spotify profile, please share. He curated a damn a good playlist. I was literally dancing to the bathroom. And may I say, the pumpkin coconut candle burning in the bathroom smelled marvelous!

I came here for my birthday and it was an amazing experience. It was opening weekend and everything was so seamless you would have thought it's been open for awhile. 

Now the food! Amazing! I am Bajan American, but Jamaican, Haitian by association without the accents lol. All of that to say, I know how to appreciate authentic Caribbean food and that was IT! 

The Chef came out and talked to everyone at their table to gauge their experiences which was also a nice touch. 

I went back a few days later, just to grab a drink before the movies and I was able to relax at the bar and enjoy the music and vibe. The drinks were also spot on. 

I will be back

Amazing!! The goat patties was one of the best things I've ever had. Also loved the cosmic brownie, the powdered sugar donut icecream it comes with is soo extremely cool and fun. The hot sauce is fantastic too.

One of the best meals I have ever eaten.  Our server was super friendly and very knowledgeable for a new restaurant.  We has the black bean hummus, curried goat patties, honey nut peri peri salad and hamachi escovitch from the small shares.  We also got the brown stew snapper, take-out mushrooms and short rib pastrami suya. The pastrami dish was amazing - it melted in your mouth.  For dessert we got all three desserts.  The cheese cake was the table favorite but the brownie and rainbow cookie panna cotta were also very good. Kwame was at the restaurant and came over and took a photo with my daughter for her birthday.  I'm hoping that he changes the menu periodically so we can come back and try more delicious items. The room was nicely decorated and we were able to hear each other talk.

We had high expectations despite this restaurant only being about a month old, and still our expectations were exceeded. There was not one flaw to our entire experience. Everything from the cocktails to the small bites to the entrees were complete perfection. The pina pina cocktail in particular was so good, we ordered multiple. We are no stranger to a good crudo, and tend to order one anytime we see it on the menu but somehow Kwame's exceeded any others we've had before. It was like a flavor explosion, but somehow the taste of the hamachi was not overpowered. Fantastic and a must try. The oxtail came with rice and peas and both were also insanely tasty and unique. The oxtail was so tender and delicious I could drink that sauce. The pastrami short rib was the showstopper. The way the meat crisps up around the bone, but there is tender and delicious meat once you break past the exterior... insane. My husband who does not typically like pastrami even agreed it was the best part of the meal. The cabbage and bread it came with were also both so fantastic. It reminded me of a much more flavorful version of the traditional Irish corned beef and cabbage. The meal was on the pricey side but for the location and quality, we feel the pricing is fair. We will certainly be back and will struggle to decide whether or not to order something new or repeat this exact fantastic lineup. Thank you to the team for a great experience!

Just wow! We basically had everything on the menu and it was incredible. Talented young chef, amazing atmosphere with great vibing music. The short rib, chicken, and mushrooms were my favorite! Oh and all the desserts  cookie crumble panna cotta!

Welcome home Chef Kwame!!! It's only been a few weeks but this is already my most anticipated reservation of 2022. 

After his last (incredible) restaurant closed in DC, I knew it was only a matter of time before Chef Kwame came back to NY. He's back and I loved every minute of my visit. 

For the food, I loved the curry goat patties and the steak. Both had lots of flavor and were cooked very well. The egusi dumplings were my least liked dish but it was my first time eating it so no love lost on that item. I also really enjoyed the scallops (but laughed at how tiny they were lol). Thanks to the waitress for warning us about it prior to ordering. For the drinks, I had 2 cocktails that I liked but I was more excited to see that McBride Sisters wine is on the menu :). 

I went opening week so there have been many changes to the menu already that I'm looking forward to. I'm calling it now, this spot will be in heavy rotation for me in 2023.

Our meal at Tatiana was excellent. There was such a variety of flavors across the spectrum of African, Caribbean, and Louisianan. The staff were very attentive, from the host to the servers. Looking forward to going back!

Chef Kwame has put it all together at Tatiana. From the moment you enter, the vibe is high energy with the very sophisticated decor and great music. The food is exceptional. We had the goat meat patties, nicely flavored meat in a crispy pastry. The pastrami, oxtails and mushroom dishes were all bursting with unique flavors. You have to eat the oxtails with your fingers to really enjoy the flavors. The cheesecake and Bodega brownie were outstanding. Service was excellent and very attentive. Chef Kwame is a great young man who has accomplished a lot and I am so happy to have met him at Tatiana. Much success to him and his team. His book tells his story.

My commute was dastardly as it was raining and decided not to drive as you know I most often go for *free* street parking but this culinary experience at the lincoln center made up for it ! The rain however magically stopped when I arrived and though I had to walk around a bit to find the entrance I didnt mind getting caught up in the nostalgia of Lincoln Center on a dewy fall evening (insider tip the entrance to Tatiana is closer to the infamous steps at the lincoln center facing Broadway) .

Upon locating entrance, I was greeted inside a dimly lit restaurant with friendly greeters. And the music, baby, definitely a vibe. Once seated, i had memorized the menu and knew instantly what I wanted; inalso thought i memorized them prices but I guess I was wrong byt this meal was so worth it. Tatiana actually restored my faith in the recently mediocore dining scene in NYC. Like not only was this place running up numbers on the insta side of things, the food, the food also is worthy ... the  instagrammable moment meets fine dining thats actually a success! 

Okay let me get into the food. So if you haven't caught on everything was 10/10 except the oxtails .... 

Curried Goat Patties - yo where have these been my whole life 
Egusi Dumplings - spicy and flavorful; texture of dumpling not gummy and just smooth
Truffle Chopped Cheese - chopped cheese with just the right amount of truffle; nothing overpowering ; the bread was soft and tasty
Salmon Creole - ordered this because it had okra. Okra was bomb. Flavorful in a creole way and not spicy. Salmon was cooked perfect and paired nicely with the tomatoe based sauce and okra
Braised Oxtail  - fall off the bone oxtails but hit my palate with an oily covering that could have been toned down and amped up with  more spices to give it more carribean vibes unless thats not where chef was going and i can respect that... 

i soon realized that the dishes were a play on different cultures and i enjoyed this epcot like experience of the melting pot of NY. The drinks were litisha and our server who was also a manager was just the sweetest. I noticed the chef stopping by a few tables to say hi and i definitely got FOMo when the chef didn't say hi to me but that's cool imma always support next stop the family cookout !

Ooo you may also spot a celebrity or too while dining ... i will keep quiet on who my sis peeped in the crowd. 

My goal is to win Guiness record and try everything off of the menu.

Went to this spot for a ladies night out, the vibe was amazing. Service from the door was very accommodating. The interior design was very elegant. The lighting in the restaurant set a great mood. The drinks were just right. My friend has the Egusi dumplings. She said they were really good. They had to be since she was quiet while eating them lol. I had the takeout mushrooms which were phenomenal. So much flavor in each and every bite. As a plant based eater I was so happy to enjoy a wonderful meal here.

Living in lincoln square We were excited to try Tatania.  The space is sophisticated and hip.  The beaded curtains reminded those of us of a certain age of  the four seasons of ages ago, giving great views of the plaza and people going to the Met and State theater ( as we knew it back in the day) Reception was a bit cool but things warmed up once we met our excellent wait person Beatrice. The food was amazing. 
Hamachi delicious, fragrent of lime  and cilantro. The fried okra was a revelation. We liked it hot and spicy but you can ask for less heat if that's your thing.  Truffled chopped cheese is a must try...have never had anything like it.     Husband's oxtails were savory and the rice seasoned well.  I had the sazon chicken which was accompanied by a soffrito stew with olives  that was bursting with flavor. We were amazed at the balances the chef achieved in each dish.  Spurred by the  inventive use of spice and heat we figured we had to try dessert and that's where things fell flat.  Ugh what a let down.  Dont ask and we won't tell.   Please work on that chef.   Wines by the glass were  very good with generous pours. Beatrice our waitperson was wonderful, the service was great.
The music was good but  a bit loud .
So glad to see a vibrant hip place and talented chef at Geffen.  Wishing Tatania much  success.

Yea baby. It's really like that. No way in the world an Afro-Caribbean inspired, upscale restaurant could come to NYC and not see me. I've been a huge fan of Chef Kwame since Top Chef and as he penned "A Love Letter to NYC" with this menu, I happily dove right in.

First things first, you get your reservations on Resy. Make sure you select "notify" for any cancellations, this is how I snagged my res. Resy gives clear instructions on how to find the golden doors within Lincoln Center's Plaza and upon entering, your met with low purple toned lights with gold decor and accents. Royalty baby.

We basically ordered the entire menu, but the standouts to me were the Curry Goat Patties, Scallops, Truffle Chopped Cheese, Green Caesar, Pastrami and the Cosmic Brownie. Along with my Nutcracker Cocktail. The food is delicious, there's no question about it. But eating with the frame of mind that this is a love letter to NYC, he hit the staples on the head. With each bite came a nostalgic feeling, a story, it evoked feelings and sentiments of home. Not being from the Africas or Caribbean, but growing up in NYC, it was a perfect blend of all that I've been raised in. A 10/10 dining experience. All of my senses were through the roof.

You better go 'head now Chef Kwame

Definitely top 5 dining experiences. Everything was delicious. Service was great, our waitress was very attentive. Ambience adds to the flavors of the food. It's honestly the best of both worlds culturally, atmosphere, music. Definitely will return. 

We also got oxtails (not pictured)

My Gosh. Chef Kwame has got this place down. From the moment you walk in, you are swooped into this soulful swanky atmosphere. That playlist is on point. The staff is incredibly hospitable and professional. We arrived 20 min late for our reservation ( we did contact the restaurant). I was super stressed and upset about it ( it was my fault) but the hostess literally said nothing and greeted us like we were on time. That was so nice. Our server was so helpful. She walked us through the menu and the concept of shared plates. Very knowledgeable.

Drinks: so good that we had 2 rounds! 
Strawberry Margarita- perfectly mix of sweet and tart.
Drink #2: I can't remember the name of this drink for the life of me,  but is was made with Appleton Rum and it also had a sweet tartness in a different way. So divine. 

Food:
Small Plates:
Egusi Dumplings- good amount of spice. The crab paired nice with the red stew sauce. The dumpling exterior had that good crunch followed by chewy balance.
Curried Goat Patties- MUST TRY-let me tell you about this!!! Nice spicy bite, perfect amount of heat complimented by the side sauces...AND THAT CRUST! The ideal vehicle for the goat filling. Perfect crunch- the texture and taste. I could eat the crust alone all day. 
Scallops- well cooked. The combination of the confit made for a tasty bite.
Large Plates:
Brown Stew Red Snapper: MUST TRY- well prepared snapper with brown stew. Rice and beans were a nice touch. I would come back and order this again!
Short Rib Pastrami Suya- this dish is not all presentation. An upscale deconstructed pastrami sandwich- the meat is so tender it falls off the bone. I had my partner fix his own plate so he could experience the satisfaction of shredding the juicy tender meat off the bone as I did: The cocoa bread was warm with a glazed exterior and a nice chew. I was in heaven. It indeed felt like a warm hug. 

We ended the meal with the bodega special. Shout out to our server who fulfilled our request for us to take it to go. She even brought it out unpacked so we could take a look at it! Happy to report we reached our hotel with the ice cream intact! The brownie is one childhood dreams are made out of. And that powdered donut ice cream? I was taken straight back to my days of binging bodega powdered donuts. Talk about an infusion.

It was so perfect for our anniversary dinner. I'm coming back with the whole fam. Too good to not enjoy multiple times. I hope we get to meet Chef Kwame one day at the restaurant. Would be icing on the cake! 5

Not easy to find at Lincoln Center. Staff is very friendly and made good suggestions. Although I enjoyed the Afrobeat/R&B playlist, it was a bit loud. The ambiance was great though the lighting is a bit too dim if you care to see your food. I would highly recommend the black bean hummus dish (ask for extra bread -they gave us exactly 5 so we each had one dollar size piece). Not a lot for dessert choices and the drinks were not great.. all in all, an experience worth having.

I've never had African inspired food and this blew any expectations I had out of the water. All the food was unique and delicious. The lamb and chicken were my favorites but everything on the menu was amazing. Service makes you feel right at home and ambiance might be the best part of the whole place. Congrats to Kwame and his team on a real winner. Will be back to try the rest of the menu.

We get so many cute places with big prices and small plates that are sub par that my expectations weren't super high for Tatiana. I was so WRONG. Everything from the FOOD, to the SERVICE, to the atmosphere!! Amazing. This review is worded so extra because that's really how much I loved dining at Tatiana. The attention to detail, the attentiveness of the staff, the menu! There is nothing not to love. 

I celebrated my best friends birthday here and we're definitely coming back!  

You have to try the okra, the oxtail, the empanadas, the arroz con guandules, the fish, the hamachi! Everything was so so good. Worth every dollar you spend and you'll be more than satisfied with the amount of food you get.

I waited an entire month for my reservation and it was worth it! 

Ambiance: Upon arrival you're greeted by the hostess who were friendly and sat me right away although I was the first one there. The place is dimly lit but not overwhelming to me where you have to squint to see what you're eating, lol. 

Service: Service here is superb. When I say swift I mean swift. Our waitress was amazing she was constantly in the area, refilling our water cups and keeping an eye out to see if at any moment we needed her

Drinks/Food: I started with the Pog Nutcracker which was decent, not my fave but worth a try if you must. Now, the strawberry margarita was the star of the evening. 10/10. For starters we got the curry goat patties and the egusi dumplings. Patties are a 10/10. Zero debating there. It came with an aioli sauce and a mango salsa which wasn't even needed but complimented it so well. They also place their signature pepper sauce on the table when you arrive which was amazing. I'm not someone who enjoys spicy food yet I still heavily enjoyed that. The dumplings were good but in my opinion needed more crab. I'd love to see lump crab meat in those. The red snapper was perfectly cooked. Crispy on the outside and soft on the inside and the best part is they debone it. The oxtail was an 8/10 for me. It was good but I think it can use just a tad bit more flavor. The rice and peas can enter a competition lol.

I actually have a dinner party to attend here on Saturday so I'm happy I'm able to go back so soon and try more dishes!

Best meal I had in 2022. No joke. No exaggeration. Kwame is a world class chef. The vibes are immaculate. I've been back twice since november. Going again soon. Can't over hype the goat curry dumplings. Or the oxtail. Slamming.

Me and my boo been waiting for a month to get a reservation and best believe it was worth the wait! 

First off the decor and aesthetic of Tatiana fits in with Lincoln Center yet feels more approachable and friendlier than most places in the area. I love seeing all these beautiful faces celebrating and eating good things in a safe and welcoming environment. 

Now to the food: they were able to accommodate the fact that my partner has a gluten allergy so the gluten items in the dishes we had were separated and I gladly ate those. 

Small Plates: 

Honeynut Piri Piri Salad: delicious, light and fresh

Scallops Pinchos: not spicy but lightly sweet

Black Bean Hummus: I don't have enough words to describe it, it was oh so good! And the m'semen was good and oily to complement thd hummus

Large Plates: Short Rib Pastrami Suya!!! We loved it! The meat was super tender and the taste was on par with any old school NY deli

We even gave the scrapes to our pups when we got home and they devoured it haha

To sum it up Kwame is doing his thing and I hope this place becomes a mainstay in the years to come

Resy, Resy, Resy... alert Tatiana how bad we would like to go! Resy answered. Thursday night right Afterwork? 

We'll make it work. Nyc Free parking did not disappoint. Right in front of LGA high school. Arrived at 5pm for our 5:45pm res and were seated right away. 

Server introduce herself and made us aware she was fully at our service and did not disappoint. Small shares: euhsi dumpling, scallops okra and goat empanadas for starters please. Small shares all delicious and wonderful-pause skip the okra. Server shared the pina pina as her favorite, however when would a Bronx native, such as myself ever get the opportunity to say in tangent, " I had a "Nutcracker" while dinning at Lincoln Center??  

For our large share: the braised oxtail and short rib pastrami. Every dish which hit the table was explained beautifully, even over the sounds of afrobeats and even Biggy Smalls playing. Yes, not one dinning patron looked surprised... "must be these succulent braised oxtails" I said. 

My Jamaican hubby; who self proclaimed, he makes a mean oxtail dish and reluctantly scoffed"who is going to make great oxtails below 125th in Manhattan?"
 
 He's now a believer and we CAN'T wait for Resy to grant us our wish again!!

Eating at TATIANA was the best dining experience of my entire life, and I don't even know if I have the words to do it justice. The decor? Beautiful. The vibes? Unmatched. THE FOOD? EXQUISITE!

To be honest, I went into this restaurant with very high hopes and extreme excitement because I have been a fan of Chef Kwame since he competed on Top Chef. I knew this was going to be a restaurant that spoke to my soul. I booked my reservation on a whim with no idea who was going to accompany me or what that day would bring, but all I knew was that I was going to eat at TATIANA one way or another.

To say this experience exceeded my expectations is an understatement. We decided to order the Egusi Dumplings, Curried Goat Patties, Takeout Mushrooms, and Braised Oxtails. The Egusi Dumplings were the first to come out and set the tone nicely. They were savory and spicy, and served with a sauce that added a very mild sweetness that rounded out the flavors. Next out were the Curried Goat Patties, which were served with a chutney, a green aioli and a scotch bonnet pepper sauce. Our waitress encouraged us to use all three sauces with each bite, and we were amazed at how beautifully all three worked together with the spicy and flavorful patties. To our surprise, Crispy Okra also came out with our Curried Goat Patties. Ironically, I told my friend we could not order the okra because I hate okra, but then it came out as a complementary dish from the chef! I was reluctant, but after trying it, my jaw was on the floor. This okra wasn't your typical slimy okra. This was crispy and spicy and sweet heaven! I ate nearly the whole plate. 

Moving on to the large plates: the Takeout Mushrooms and the Braised Oxtails. The Takeout Mushrooms were two different kinds of mushrooms in a delicious sticky glaze, served with the most heavenly and fluffy scallion pancakes i've ever had, plum sauce, and picked ginger. DELICIOUS! The Braised Oxtails were huge pieces of tender, fall-off-the-bone oxtails served with a yummy side of rice and peas. 

By this point, we were full but could not leave with out dessert. We ultimately went with the Bodega Special because of the nostalgia it brought us as native New Yorkers. This dish was a decadent, rich chocolate brownie inspired by the Cosmic Brownie, served with an unbelievable powdered donut ice cream on top of brown crumbs. I have been thinking about that ice cream every day since I've had it. Honestly, I've been thinking about this entire meal everyday. I don't even know why you're still reading this. Go make your reservation!

Food was exceptional, atmosphere is fantastic and comfortable (if you don't mind the music bumpin more than your typical fine dining establishment), and service was above and beyond. HIGHLY recommended. Dumplings and goat patties are must-haves.

Sorry to break away from the pack but this restaurant is NO 5 stars. Maybe it was a bad day but not excuses when paying a $70 for a entree. But first things first!  The Strawberry Margarita came highly recommended by the staff, it was good not great. For $18 my Margarita was served in a Low ball glass that means 4-6 oz not even in this case as it was served with 2 extra large cocktail ice cubes which means; I received less than 4-6 ounces! The appetizers okra and egusi dumplings were satisfactory the goat patties were very good. I ordered the Short Rib pastrami it was beautifully plated but less than lukewarm closer to cold on the other hand the rolls were hot. My dining partner ordered the same thing but they brought out oxtails.??? 

This restaurant is beautiful and in a great location but I believe the overall delivery of food, drinks and prices are part of being swept up in new found fame and exposure. Be careful overexposure and momentary celebrity recognition without true substance can detrimental.

Vibes were great. Food was absolutely phenomenal. The truffle chopped cheese and the short rib pastrami suya were the stand-outs. We also tried the mom dukes shrimp which had the best toast I've ever had in my entire life (yes, just toasted bread but it was soooooo good) and the oxtails. Oxtails were meh, probably wouldn't order again. 

Drinks were also pretty  good. The old fashioned and strawberry margarita are both great choices.

It was a busy Friday night so service was kind of slow but the staff was great and very friendly.

4.5 stars ! 

Somehow managed to score prime time dinner reservations at this new hot happening trendy spot! It's a really cute spot inside David Geffen hall at Lincoln Center. We did have to wait 30 mins past our dinner reservation . I guess cause it's such a happening spot. Not sure if they kick you out after a certain time . 

They did made up for it by bringing us two glasses of sparkling wine! Was absolutely delicious and a really nice touch. We ended up ordering a whole bunch of things off their menu. The only annoying thing was they wanted us to place the entire order at once. 

Small plates wise , we got the curried goat patties. It came with a green seasoning aioli which was outstanding . Then we got the honey nut Piri Piri salad which was phenomenal. It was gorgeously presented, I didn't care for the dressing but the cucumber avocado and gooseberry combination was so crisp and refreshing! They then brought out the egusi dumplings which my husband enjoyed. Finally we got the truffle chopped cheese which was by far my favorite small plate. It's funny cause our server said she wouldn't recommend it compared to the other dishes and I almost didn't get it!  I guess it is little on the pricier side and we did get quite a few plates. I'd definitely recommend this and the salad as must tries. 

For our mains we got the braised oxtails which came with a nice sauce and huge portion size and the short rib pastrami suya (which is priced at $70). The rub on it was to die for but the melted red cabbage and caraway coco bread fell a little short. I guess you're mostly paying for the cut of meat. But it was still a little overpriced in my opinion . I did want to try the chicken which sounded delicious and maybe more reasonably priced. 

The music all night was just on point . The chef came out and chatted with us which was a super nice touch! Honestly the sparkling wine , the chef coming out to talk to us were such nice added touches and the food is overall very very good. But it's not my favorite spot and not sure I'll really go back but I highly highly recommend you try it atleast once for sure!

I can't comment on the food because we didn't get that far but the staff needs to be rehired or retrained. Hopefully this review can drive some improvements. 

I live around the corner so stopped by at 10pm to try their late night menu because it was fully booked on Resy and the website says they take no reservations for late night. We had no issue with waiting a while but, apparently the website is incorrect because the host said were fully booked until close. So maybe you can book for late night or the hostess didn't know what to do? 

We asked her if we could eat at the bar. She said we could talk to the bartender to see if something would open up. We stood in the corner of the bar because it's a cramped space and didn't want to obstruct the wait staff traffic or lurk around the diners at the bar. Well, before we could even ask the bartender, he yelled at us to clear the area. So really, there's no way to talk to the bartender because there's no space. There's only 6 seats at the bar and everyone is eating a full meal so there needs to be some system to manage the wait. Seems like the hostess should do it if the bartender has no time or desire to do it. 

After that experience, we decided to just leave. I would have given it another shot but on our way out, one of the hostesses yelled at us about keeping the door open behind us. Yes, it was a cold night but we were only in the restaurant for a few minutes so were not aware the door didn't automatically shut. We weren't intentionally trying to be uncourteous to the diners, we had no idea it didn't automatically shut. 

I know inflation has been high but at this price point you'd at least expect politeness from the staff.

I had heard about this place on social media so I opted to go while looking for a good final dinner while in NYC. I came at about 5:15pm (they open at 5pm) on a Saturday evening. I didnt have a reservation but it was just me so I figured I would sit at the bar. However, when I arrived, the bar was already full and there was a waitlist. There were only 6seats at the bar and I wasnt sure how long they would take so I got a drink while waiting. The bartender Nick was really nice and even though he was super busy, he still was attentive to each customer. He proactively had me try a wine before ordering to make sure it was to my liking and later on made me a few other really good cocktails.

While waiting, I spoke with a regular who said he loves the food an recommended a few dishes. After about an hour and a half, there was one seat available. The guy who is a regular was next but he let me sit down before him since he knew it was my first time. I ordered the curry goat pies, the truffle chop cheese and the oxtails. Everything was good and Nick checked with me regularly to make sure I enjoyed the food. I thought my oxtails were salty but wasnt going to send them back since the overall experience was so good. Nick proactively took 2 of my drinks off my bill which was super nice of him.

This was a great experience and I would defintely come back but I wold come right at 5pm and I would try a few more apps.

I was in New York for New Year's Eve weekend and was able to get reservations for Tatiana while there. Instead of ordering individual items, our party decided to try multiple items and share. I think this is the best experience, since most of the entrees are made for sharing. These were the dishes we tried:
Crispy Okra - 9/10
Egusi Dumplings - 8/10
Curried Goat Patties - 10/10
Truffled Chop Cheese - 5/10
Mom Dukes Shrimp - 12/10 (My favorite)
Mushrooms - 9/10
Brown Stew Red Snapper - 9/10

Pros: The restaurant and location are beautiful. The food was delicious and the dishes were timed and delivered perfectly. Service was great and the chef was nice enough to send over a few extra dishes for us to try. 
Cons: Music was too loud and could be a more diverse mix of genres.

One thousand percent recommended. Don't walk, RUN. Quality of food, creative presentation, ambiance, service is impeccable. The fried Okra is slamming. And don't sleep on the crab cakes. You're welcome.

4.5 stars

There are certain restaurants in New York City that are impossible to get into [i.e you have to stay up until midnight to make a reservation via Resy and probably still won't get a reservation] and/or don't take reservations for one. Tatiana By Kwame Onwuachi is the epitome of those both things. 

After reading a previous Yelp review about having to wait an hour and half to sit at the bar, I got to Tatiana at around 4:30PM and waited until they started to let people in around 4:57PM. There were already four people ahead of me, but I got the 5th bar seat [there are only 6 bar seats]. A meal also does take around an hour and half so be prepared to wait if you arrive post-5PM.

Upon entering, I realized the restaurant is pretty small so no wonder it books up fast. I feel like the restaurant wasn't initially designed to be as popular as it has turned out to be. There are no bar hooks and you're essentially below eye level when receiving drinks across the bar so you don't necessarily see your drink waiting for you.

That being said: what a meal, indeed. It was great but do I need to wait a half hour for a restaurant to open to get a seat? Maybe. 

I started with the Smokey Piri Piri Paloma [$18], it wasn't really my cup of tea. It was nice and fizzy, I like piri piri spice but this drink didn't excite me. I ordered the Strawberry Margarita [$18] next and found this to be much more my speed. It was very refreshing and fruity. 

The bartender was very nice and attentive, which was surprising because after 10 minutes the place really started to fill up. 

I ordered the Truffle Chopped Cheese, it was good but it didn't blow me away like the rest of the meal. There were three "sandwiches" stacked next to each other and filled with beefy beef, tomato, and shredded lettuce. The sauce on the side was nice and the toasted bread it was on was buttery and delicious. I don't know that I needed all that shaved truffle on top though, I guess it was a bit of earthy but it didn't make an impression on me. 

The Braised Oxtails [$50] with rice and beans though. Lord. That is a special dish. I don't typically order oxtails on a menu or really know what they should taste like, but after having these, the bar is set very high. They were so tender and fell off the bone. There's about 5 or 6 of them in a sticky sweet sauce. It was perfection. I loved the carrots and other veg, they were crunchy and delicious. The rice and beans were also fantastic. I didn't know how much I needed this dish in my life. 

The Rainbow Cookie Panna Cotta [$16]. I can't even with this dessert. I don't love rainbow cookies but I love this panna cotta. It legit tasted like a rainbow cookie. I loved the nuts and the crunchy topping. It was a rainbow cookie but reimagined as a fancy dessert. The whole thing was a party in my mouth, it was perfectly sweet and creamy. I would come back just for this.  

I left feeling very full. Tatiana is definitely a place you come to with friends, if you can get a reservation and have a very thick wallet. It is not cheap. I ended up spending $140 before tip.

The food was great (we had: fried okra (delicious & on point), egusi dumplings (yummy but not crab forward), brown stewed snapper & coconut rice (totally dreamy), bodega special dessert (great brownie, ice cream silky but needed more flavour). Great vibe - although the music is a tad loud for dining (but I am way past 30). Luscious decor. Attentive hosts - but pacing between ordering and bringing courses over needs to be sharpened.  Overall a great experience. When we can afford it again - and am able to get a reservation - we will return to try other dishes on the menu. Proud of this young NY chef!

The Ambiance- welcoming and relaxed. Mellow

The honeynut Piri Piri  Salad and the Scallion pancake Take out mushroom dish were our favorites. 

Okra and wagyu short rib were also really really  good. 

Our waitress was Shae. Our waters were never empty.

Sadly sold out of cheesecake but the cosmic brownie was delicious
Let the pictures of the food speak for itself.

Super disappointing. High prices and poor quality. The food either had zero taste or was super salty. Service was decent but I would not return nor would I recommend this place. In a city filled with quality dining options, this place falls far short in every way.

This just was not a good experience at all, which makes me sad because I loved the chef's former restaurant in DC, Kith/Kin.

I'll start with the ambiance: the music was way too loud and the restaurant decor was extremely minimal. I think it was the first time in my life that I was disappointed to hear 2005 top 100 hip hop. I guess I was expecting a more elevated experience from a celebrity chef.

The food service: The serving plates were curved which led to our servers unintentionally putting their fingers in the dishes and touching our food as they were delivered to our table. However, our primary server was very nice and attentive.

The food: we ordered egusi dumplings, goat patties and oxtail. The dumplings were burned and the meat inside was undistinguishable with very little flavor. I've had better frozen dumplings from Whole Foods.

The goat patties were doughy and mushy on the inside with about a tsp of goat meat as filling, which again was under seasoned.

The oxtail was the most disappointing. It was served with about one cup of rice, it was lukewarm, and it was 99% fat and ligament. What's worse is that it was $50 and when the dish came to our table, there was a lid on it, but no drama. Meaning, there wasn't any steam billowing out of the lid or a beautiful display of vegetables and meat inside. Just some lukewarm oxtails with super syruppy sauce and about one quarter of a carrot and one cut up fingerling potato.

Lastly, the drinks were just... meh. I ordered a Riesling because until yesterday, I haven't had a bad Riesling. It was terrible - it smelled bad and the notes were just off. My partner ordered a cocktail that was basically a spiked Arnold Palmer. The drink selection was just so disappointing because I'm sure Kwame has some celebrity sommelier and mixologist friends that could have elevated his menu.

This restaurant would be way better as a bar with food. They should redesign it with a huge bar in the middle, some standing tables, and just make it a vibey place to listen to good music and get mid- food and drink after a show. Drop the prices by $10-15 across the board.

Exceptional experience. Really good food. Loved the piri piri salad, dumplings, shrimp, pastrami short ribs, etc. The only thing I didn't love were the mushrooms. Skipped dessert, just didn't have room left. But overall a yummy meal.

5 out of 5! Hands down some of the best food I've ever had. Finally was able to get a reservation after months of waiting. And it was totally worth it . Everything was top notch including the service. The decorum was wonderful and the vibes! I ordered the nutcracker to start and that was nice and sweet but had a kick to it. Started with the dumplings as an appetizer and the oxtail as the main course. My friend has the scallops and fish. Everything was immaculately prepared and I'll be visiting again.

I saw this place on lists of hardest reservations to get in NYC, so I secured a reservation and was super excited to go with a friend who has also been curious about it. Once we entered, we both immediately fell in love with the vibe, as it was super chic and urban but also so so modern and stylish. We were greeted by our server who was super nice and explained the menu to us, and once we pondered, we ordered drinks and food and were ready to eat:

Drinks:
Piña Piña Piña and Tatiana Tonic - first round of drinks; I got the former and my friend got the latter. Both were AMAZING. So so sweet and light and fruity and yummy. Just we both wanted. Literally the perfect cocktails to begin our dinner.

Half & Half and POG Nutcracker - second round of drinks; again, I got the former, and my friend got the latter. My drink was WAYYYYY more spirit-forward this time, but I really appreciated the black tea flavor from the black tea infused bourbon. My friend's drink was again super fruity and sweet; more of my cup of tea, but I still liked mine.

Food
Crispy Okra - the first appetizer to arrive at our table. This was definitely the most unique okra I've ever had, and I appreciated their courage to play with various flavors for this dish. However, I feel like a lot was going on, since it was salty but also spicy but also sweet but also sour, so I think my palate slowly started to get overwhelmed by everything. Definitely not bad, but I wish it was a little lighter in the flavor department. Texture was interesting and nice though.

Evian Dumplings - the second appetizer we received and the one I preferred. I really liked the crab flavor of the filling of the dumpling as well as the egusi stew based sauce (very tomatoey and acidic). We only received three dumplings though, and I wish we could have had more since I really liked the flavors of this one.

Take-Out Mushrooms - the first entree we received. I think I can appreciate what they were trying to do here, but again, like the okra, I think they were trying to do a bit too much here. The mushrooms were very potent with a specific spice (we thought it was allspice/five spice), and they were really sticky and stuck to my teeth pretty easily. The scallion pancake that came with it was my favorite part though, as it helped with the potent flavor of the mushroom as well as with the texture. The plum sauce and ginger were okay, but I think if they toned down on the flavors more on the mushrooms, I would have liked it a lot more.

Short Rib Pastrami Suya - the second entree of the night and probably my favorite of the evening! The pastrami was so so tender and flavorful, and I really enjoyed the pairing with the pickled onions and mustard that were provided. The bread was good, but I wish it were more airy and soft on the inside, and it was somewhat hard to eat with all the components in one bite. Still highly recommend, though it is a bit pricey (70 dollars).

Dessert
Rainbow Cookie Panna Cotta - probably my favorite dish of the entire night. It was so light and smooth and went so nicely with the finely shaved chocolate and whole almonds. Tasted just like a rainbow cookie but in panna cotta form. Excellent.

Overall - the vibes were amazing and the service was really good. Drinks were immaculate, but I feel that the food just fell a bit short of my expectations and was a bit on the expensive side. Still a great spot for a date or a night out with friends, so I would for sure try it at least once!

FINALLY snagged a res at Chef Kwame Onwuachi's new restaurant and safe to safe that I am in love - definitely adding this one to my favorites!

[VIBE] Upon entering, the restaurant was exactly what I hoped it would be - sleek, sexy, with the music bumpin - but not so much that you can't carry a conversation. Every staff member greeted us with smiles, and their team worked like a fine tuned orchestra- water was always full, plates were cleared often, and dishes were fired at appropriate intervals to allow enjoyment and conversation.

[FOOD] All the plates are meant to share, which was perfect for me because I easily wanted to try everything on the menu. It was hard to eat with my jaw wide open as I both oohed and ahhed over every plate and morsel. The highlights -

The CURRIED GOAT PATTIES I could eat EVERY.DAY. They were light and flaky, while the filling is savory and flavor packed.

EGUSI DUMPLINGS were a treat to eat - we were instructed by our server to take a bite of the crab dumpling first, then dip it into the red stew below for another bite. This reminded us of soup dumplings, but on a richer, heartier level. Freakin amazing.

TRUFFLE CHOPPED CHEESE - Yes, it IS possible to elevate this bodega sammie. Ribeye + taleggio on brioche, with loads of truffles on top - I mean GTFOH it was amazing. I even had it for leftovers the next day and I was still happy with it.

MOM DUKES SHRIMP - I had seen pics of this on IG and knew I had to try it. What I was not prepared for was the SIZE of these dang shrimp! My homegirl named them baby lobsters, and we each devoured these plump, meaty thangs which were served on a bowl of spicy creole butter with yes, more brioche 

BRAISED OXTAILS - This is my go to whenever I see it on a menu. I cannot describe the happiness I felt when I barely touched my piece with my fork- the meat properly fell off the bone. My only complaint was that I wanted a triple serving of this. Tears of happiness.

BODEGA SPECIAL - I was hellbent on finishing my meal with the cosmic brownie. Y'all know I'm a sucker for anything fun, nostalgic, and with rainbow sprinkles. This dessert was the perfect size to share, yet I demolished it on my own  

[COCKTAILS] Not pictured: her Tatiana Tonic done with gin + elderflower cordial, and my POG Nutcracker, with Appleton rum  + passion fruit + orange + guava. My drank was sweet, light, and waaaaay to easy to wanna kickback to, as a proper nutcracker should 

Bigups to our server Kaydene and the entire team there this past Wednesday night! I am making it my mission to eat there again and again until I've had the whole menu. And then again and again and again. Best of luck to Chef Kwame - I hope you're at Lincoln Center for a long, long time!

TLDR: beautiful venue, amazing vibes, friendly and affable staff.. but none of the food convinced us that we needed to return any time soon.

Came on a Friday night with a friend. It was pretty busy; it took us over 20 minutes after our reservation time to be seated. We were told to wait in the waiting area/lobby of the David Geffen Hall until our table was ready. Once seated, our server was super fun and friendly and told us that the small plates were extremely small while large plates were meant to be shared between two. 

We ordered the okra and egusi dumplings for small plates and for large, we got the take-out mushrooms and wagyu pastrami. The okra was larger than we expected and were unexpectedly crisp! They were reminiscent of crispy Brussels sprouts and they were sweet, salty, and even spicy. There was so much going on we weren't sure if we liked it or not. The egusi dumplings were as small as we expected. There were three small crab and egusi filled dumplings. Pretty solid. The take-out mushroom dish was kind of all over the place. The sauce was sticky and flavored with five spice, which was reminiscent of Hong shao rou, but it was so overwhelmingly five spice that we didn't taste the nuts that were sprinkled on top and we didn't even realize that there was shiso until we finished the dish and saw there were leaves leftover. The scallion pancakes were good - a little bit on the cakey side but I quite enjoyed them. The mushrooms were a little difficult to eat with the pancakes because of how sticky they were and how they were cut and I don't believe the ginger or plum sauce was necessary because how flavorful the sauce already was. I really wanted to like this dish more. The wagyu pastrami was our favorite dish of the night. It was extremely decadent though - if I hadn't come with a meat loving freak I don't think I would have finished this with another person. I believe it was a deconstructed pastrami sandwich. The only thing I wish it had was a more neutral side like a rice or a less fatty bread. The bread was nice, but it was buttery and oily and that paired with wagyu wasn't very pleasant. The cabbage and mustard were great and I loved the wagyu even more with the scotch bonnet sauce! 

For dessert, we got the rainbow cookie panna cotta.  It was unexpectedly light and we liked it more with every bite. Exactly what was needed after what we thought was a very heavily flavored meal. We also ordered four drinks. If you like fruity/can't taste the alcohol type drinks like I do, get the piña piña piña or the POG Nutcracker. 

Overall, would come back for the vibes (legit sang all the r&b music while eating) but not the biggest fan of our meal. Perhaps it was an off day or we ordered the wrong things. I think next time I'd order all new dishes except for the wagyu pastrami.

The venue at Lincoln Center is stunning as is the atmosphere. This is one of the top dining experiences I have had after years of travel and visits to restaurants that stretch coast to coast, to Europe, Asia and Latin America.  The Afro-Carribean creations offer a taste journey with amazing richness that will lead you to table conversation contemplating not only the presentation but diversity of flavor. We had the black bean humus (wow!), the mushrooms, (these are not to be missed), and the chicken, which is just so delicious!  I recommend, however, you try anything - it all looks great!  Bravo!

https://www.tatiananyc.com/

Snagged a resy over a month ago and trooped it here on the coldest day of the winter this past Friday, 
Was it worth it ? 100 percent yes!

It's been a while since I've sat at a restaurant and been pleasantly surprised by the food. 

We had the truffle chopped cheese, hummus, fried okra and the short rib pastrami and all the flavors were amazing. The presentation was beautiful. 

The vibe in the restaurant was dope. 

My only complaint is that it's going to so hard to get another reservation

I was really looking forward to trying this restaurant out. I am so happy I did. 
Service - great, no complaints
Ambiance - nice setting, music was hittin. I would come here for date night
Food- We ordered the curried goat patties, the take out mushrooms, the egusi dumplings, truffle chopped cheese, the short ribs pastrami suya, and Bodega special.
The curried goat patties were delicious. Every jamaican patty should have that crust. 
The take-out mushrooms I would only order again for the scallion pancakes. It didn't taste like mushrooms to me because of the Seasoning/ spice they used, and it kept getting stuck in my teeth. 
The egusi dumplings were delicious. Perfect size and portion.
Truffle chopped cheese was good and tasty. 
The short ribs pastrami suya was so well done and our favorite dish. A fall off the bone, tasty, melt in your mouth goodness. Definitely order this. And the portion is perfect for two people. 
The Bodega special is the best brownie I have had at a restaurant. I was shocked. It was a piece of chocolate heaven. Get it! 
The dishes come with different sauces and Insiggest you try all of them. They really compliment the dishes. If you want some heat, please ask for their hot sauce. It has a good kick to it. 
Drinks- I enjoyed every drink I had. Well concocted. 
Price - This meal was not cheap. Definitely in the fine dining price range.

Absolutely amazing. As soon as you walk in, you are immersed in such a contemporary yet cozy space. The restaurant is intimate but you have plenty of space to comfortably eat and sit with your party, which feels so rare these days in the city. The ambiance and music was fantastic and service was also great. Food came quickly and was really great portions. 

The black bean hummus was my favorite -- the bread was so buttery and hummus extremely flavorful. You can even get the lamb off/on the side if a vegetarian is in the party. Breads were clearly a standout at the restaurant because the TakeOut Mushrooms were so flavorful and the scallion pancakes were such a good compliment to the plum sauce, ginger and mushrooms. The mushrooms were a bit heavy on the caramelization but with the ginger and plum, it had great balance. The scallion pancakes were more bread than a traditional, flaky pancake but it worked well for this dish. 

The highlight of my night was Chef Kwame coming over to speak with our table. He is so kind and humble, absolutely a pleasure and honor to have eaten here. I cannot wait to come back.

10/10 highly recommended, the epitome of cultural excellence in the heart of lincoln center.  Flavor and culture intersect fine dining and elegance. I see a michelin star in this restaurants future.

Do not pass on the curry goat patties, oxtail, and bodega special.

Everything about Tatiana was amazing. The decor is understated but gives a sexy vibe. The staff is attentive while not overly so. The food & wine suggestions were on point. The food was absolutely delectable. Next visit I'll have to remember to take pictures because the plating was superb. We had curry goat patties, truffled chopped cheese, & crispy okra for appetizers, then braised oxtail for our main course. Every morsel was delicious. We'll definitely be back. Well done Chef Kwame.

We absolutely loved eating here!!! We were able to snag a reservation about a month in advance and looked forward to it for weeks. The menu was so creative and I loved the fusion of the diversity of New York flavors. My favorites were the goat curry patties, the truffle chopped cheese, and the rainbow cookie panna cotta. We also got the shortrib pastrami, which was melt in your mouth tender. If you're a fan of bourbon, I strongly recommend the half and half cocktail. If you're able to snag a reservation here, go for it!!!

Tatiana by Chef Kwame is a true culinary experience. I had the scallop dish and oxtails and neither disappointed me. The oxtails were tender and fell off the bone. Everything was seasoned to perfection and was a true delight. The service and ambiance were exceptional and I can't wait to try more dishes in the future.

A bit disappointing since this was *the* place a friend of mine in town wanted to go to. 

We're big fans of Kwame and really loved the sound of the menu. We were thrilled to get a reservation on a Saturday night but unfortunately I think it was let down by the service. It could have been the night because they seemed to have a party in the other room (which was mentioned three times) but we did feel pretty neglected with empty glasses and long waits with our server mostly off the floor. It was clear that at least one item (the scallops) had sat for awhile because it was lukewarm to cold when it arrived and a drink had suffered the same fate as the ice had melted to the point where the drink no longer tasted as it was meant to. Sauces and items were taken away before we were finished without being asked, things were forgotten when requested, and the general / floor manager (who was attentive and seemed to be looking out quite a bit) had to cover a few times. 

We ordered the scallop pinchos, egusi dumplings, curried goat patties, mom dukes shrimp, and take out mushrooms so I think we got a pretty good sense of the menu. If the scallops were served how they were meant they would have probably been amazing. My companion said the goat patties were great; they are a big goat fan. Egusi dumplings I liked the best of what we received. I think the mushrooms are skippable--none of us were that impressed and it was the dish we left the most of. Honestly, with the way it was served it was hard to even tell they were mushrooms.

Most oddly, the server kept constantly referring to us as 'ladies' every time they came over despite my mother (after about the 10th time which I think would be excessive for actual ladies) pointedly referring to me as her son. Restrooms are nicely gender neutral and private. Ambience is great in the restaurant--beautiful fashionable people, beautifully fashionable place, great music at the right sound level. Not a great opening set up with two entrances and no controlling for showing up for bar seating. 

I do wish Kwame and his team all the best; I'd come back in a year or two after they work out new restaurant issues. At the moment, everything isn't on the same level and it is not worth the price point.

Ok, Tatiana is it. The food was great but the staff really made it 5 stars for me. I'll jump into the food and then give some backstory if you're interested lol

FOOD: 4/5

Small Share
    Scallop Pinchos - Tiny delicious scallops! "Pinchos" is apparently a small     snack so this was definitely that. It was really good. Would definitely recommend. 
   
 Egusi Dumplings - These were good but there were only 3 and it definitly felt like more dumpling than filling, if that makes sense. I would order it to experience it but wouldn't order it a second time. 
   
 Green Ceasar - Amazing. Might be weird to brag on a salad but it was GOOD. You can taste the anchovy in it which is my favorite thing in a ceasar. 
 
   Hamachi Escovitch - I love raw fish so this gets love from me. It's good but nothing to write home about. 
 
   Truffle Chopped Cheese - This was a fun one. A little elevated chopped cheese lol Just get it.   

Large Share
    Brown Stew Red Snapper - Great! I can't really describe it because I have a fish sensitivity (it's complicated) but my friends said it was amazing. 

    Sofrito Roasted Chicken - I wanted to love this but couldn't. The flavors were there, the tomato stew was great. I just have a thing against chicken breasts lol Parts of it were thicker and I felt like the great flavor on the outside didn't make it all the way through. The stew definitely helped supplement that but chicken breasts are why I almost never order chicken when I'm out. 

AMBIANCE: 10/10
The music was EVVVVVUHREETHANG!! Loved the music. Loved that the restaurant is lit in a way where it's dim but still light enough to see everything. Gold utensils?? Yes, ma'am. Love those. 

SERVICE: 10/10
Our situation was different because we pulled up off the humble with no reservation. So I was hoping for a miracle and got one lol The hostess told us they were fully committed on tables but could get on the bar waiting list, so we did. It was going to be up to a 3hr wait and my hungry ass said, 'Bet' lol. We sat at the bar in the theater waiting area next door and waited. After 2hrs, a table became available. 

We were welcomed with champagne. Idk if it's that standard or that's the 'damn y'all waited a long time' special. 

Our server was sweet and made sure all of our food made it to us.

After waiting on a table for 2hrs and then finally getting one, we got to talk to a lot of the staff. Everyone was kind and energetic. I can't wait to come back here
Absolutely off the charts amazing! The space, the food, the service, the crowd, the drinks were all amazing. Don't miss the pastrami or the oxtail!

Definitely lived up to the hype. Got a reservation a month out at noon. Arrived on time and were seated a few minutes later. The restaurant has a really good vibe, kind of a combination between a trendy bar and modern fine dining, but definitely more on the trendy side. Service was great the whole time, our waiter especially. On to the food, the goat Patties were great, many levels of flavor presented on a light puff pastry. The lamb hummus was also quite good, decent size portion, served with hot flat bread. Egusi dumplings I would avoid. Tasted like something you could get an order of 4 in Chinatown for $1. Nothing special. For mains we got the chicken and the short rib. The chicken was super solid, it was not anything crazy, but super tasty and the portion was huge. The short rib was great though. Fall off the bone tender. The place is a bit pricy for sure, but overall for the vibe, especially the music, and the innovative food I would definitely come back for a special occasion.

Do not understand the hype. At. All. To be fair the food is ok, good even at times. However the prices are giving fine dining while the service and ambience are not. It simply lacks the polish I would expect for what I assume is meant to be a destination for theater goers. First there is the hip hop music blasting at club level volumes. Now I'm far from a Karen complaining about rap music at restaurants... I in fact loved the playlist. But the volume made it impossible to hear my dining mates. And that felt disjointed for what I thought would be an elevated experience. As the night wore on, they even turned the volume UP at one point. Service was very spotty throughout the evening. We were never really checked in on.  

Some interesting flavors happening with the food. The curried goat patties were delicious. The truffle chopped cheese was skippable. Portions were on the small to very small side. The mom dukes shrimp being under the large share portion of the menu is laughable. You get TWO shrimp... be so for real. While they are very large shrimp, it does not a large share make. Unfortunately, didn't get to try the short rib pastrami suya as it was sold out.

The final nail in the coffin was that we saw chef Kwame in the room and mentioned we would love to say hi and congratulate him. We watched our server deliver this message, which chef proceeded to ignore, instead choosing to spend almost the entire evening at one table with a couple of ladies. While his time is his own to spend as he likes, it's certainly disappointing when you are trying to express support and also a bit unsettling to see him not spend any time in the kitchen. It's too soon for the restaurant to be in running-itself mode. He finally ventured over at the very end of the night but by then our moods had soured due to our throbbing heads and hoarse voices from shouting.

Service was horrendous. For where this restaurant is and the quality dining it tries to exude (price of items on menu/location/etc), there was a lot lacking in the service. Prime example was a sommelier choosing to sit in the bench to talk to the table next to us. They were ordering wine so talking to them is fine, but without asking, he chose to sit in the gap on the bench meant to be just enough for the two people sitting on either side to make their way in or out of their seat. The person I was with and the lady at the table he was speaking to both had their jackets there. HE SAT ON THE COATS. Again, excusing one self, I wouldn't have thought much of it, but to just sit down without consideration of diners around you, when you are representing the restaurant is unacceptable. Outside of that, our waitress was fairly aggressive. They pushed dishes and drinks we made sure to say we had no interest in as well as constantly try to suggest how to eat/enjoy a dish.

The score is not solely on the sub-par service. I had high hopes on the menu, but the food was lacking. The best dish was the peri peri salad. Amazing flavors, texture, and even presentation. That's where it goes downhill after.

The mushrooms were overly-oily and chewy. The "scallion pancakes" barely resembled such and probably would have worked well with the dish if it was actually a scallion pancake. 

We also ordered the dumplings (not pictured). The stew served with it was VERY flavorful and balanced. I almost wish they had more of it in the serving as the dumplings themselves were pretty bad. The casing was chewy and soggy up top and a little burnt on the bottom. This may have been simply due to the wrapper being a little too thick for the filling. Also, the filling tasted closer to imitation crab rather than actual crab meat.

I'd go back for a drink or to give 1-2 dishes we didn't have a try but overall not worth the price and wait.

I'm a huge Top Chef fan and when my friend scored a reservation to Kwame's restaurant it was an immediate yes from me. 

I can't begin to tell you how incredible the food is. It's the best of NYC staples with a modern spin that keeps getting better with every bite. You must get the chopped cheese (even consider x2 it was so good), fried okra (if you're into spicy this is for you!) and the wagyu (how he makes this taste like butter I do not know), cosmic brownie (ask for an extra scoop of the powdered donut ice cream, trust me) and then that rainbow cookie panna cotta (it tasted identical to my all time favorite cookie)! 

The only thing that I would change is the volume of the music. Great jams but it's so loud/clubby that you can't really converse without yelling. 

I'll be back 10x over...if I can get another resy!

The food was phenomenal! I strongly suggest you plan ahead and get a reservation, but if you don't... get there early to snag 1 off the 6 bar seats. Doors open at 5 and we were able to be the first seated at the bar by getting there and in line by 4:30pm. The staff was great, especially the bartenders. The environment feels very open, not too crowded and the bar seats were comfortable. 

We ordered a lot! My favorites were from the small plate menu: the scallops... perfectly cooked and seasoned, I just wish it was a larger portion. The okra was also a fav. I'm a big okra fan, but I was eating with some people who do not like okra at all, and they even enjoyed it. The okra seems dehydrated, and then fried without breading so it's much different from traditional okra dishes. We also got the goat patties, the breading was so good and I liked the sauces with them. As for large plates: we got the oxtail and the pastrami rib. Both were good and I'm usually always team oxtail, but I have to say the pastrami was so so so good. We cut it with a spoon so that tells you just how tender it was. And they give you pickled onions and bread on the side so you can make a little sandwich. Again so so so good. The bread tasted like 5 pounds of butter was mixed in it and if that's true, it's totally worth the cholesterol. I wish the pickled onions had a little bit more flavor but overall everything was so great!

I'm a Kwame fan and have been wanting to come here since spotting it on my walk home. I haven't been able to get a reservation but my friend and I heading over to see if we can grab a seat at the bar. Turned out, they had a lot of cancellations that day due to the snow and we could sit at the table as long as we could finish in 90 minutes which was plenty of time. We ordered drinks along with the curried goat patties, egusi dumplings, and braised oxtail. The patties were flakey and came with tasty sauces. This was my favorite dish. Then 15ish minutes later we got the egusi dumplings which were okay and I found them to be a little salty, then another 20 minutes later, the oxtails arrived covered. The server lifted the lid to a big pot to reveal oxtails on one side of the pot. The oxtails were very tender and flavorful. They had a nice sweet and salty flavor with sticky consistency. Rice and peas were served in a small bowl. I would have liked a little more to eat with the oxtail. Overall a good meal with fantastic service. There were long waits between dishes which I noticed was common at all the surrounding tables. Music was too loud for my liking but glad I finally got to come.

O M G . The food here is literally heaven on earth. I don't even know where to start. Every aspect of this establishment from the food to the staff , to the drinks , to the ambiance is complete excellence. I guess I'll have to talk about the food first. I have never experienced the vision of a chef, so perfectly executed. First dish, I experienced was the Piri piri salad, I was mid conversation, when I tasted the first bite. I was shocked by the burst of refreshing flavors. This salad set the tone for the night. Right then and there I knew this establishment IS special. Then I went on an adventure of flavors, I had the scallops , the curry goat pattie and dumplings. Every dish was hitting. The consistency of the flavors, was incredibly impressive. Then the chopped cheese came out ..... I took a bite , and , I'm pretty sure , a tear ran down my face. This chopped cheese was not only out of this world good but it was telling a life story on a plate. This dish is everything. The explosion of flavors brought out so many emotions. I could talk about this chopped cheese all day, it is the definition of deliciousness. It might be the perfect dish. It is a gift for our tastebuds , that I'm truly grateful for. I also had the sofrito chicken. This chicken was cooked perfectly down to the second. Succulent is an understatement.  This chicken is juicy AF.  The drinks compliment the food perfectly. You can not go wrong with the nutcracker, it's a must have .The strawberry margarita is great as well. Omg , I forgot about the okra. We had the pleasure of meeting Chrissy , the hospitality director. Chrissy recommended the okra, and again , we were blown away. It was so good. Thank you Chrissy for all the love and making an incredible experience, even more incredible, you truly are a GEM. Chrissy is as incredible as the food here, thank you Chrissy. We also had an amazing server named Beatriz. Beatriz is wonderful, just amazing . Beatriz is everything you can want as a server. Knows the menu and is sooooo personable. Thank you Beatriz. We also had the pleasure of speaking with mikayla. Mikayla is such a people person, thank you mikayla, for making our dining experience even better. We also had the humbling pleasure of meeting chef Kwame and his sister Tatiana. Such a honor to meet both of you. Your family is the definition of black excellence in every sense of the word , thank you for your kindness and your vision. Truly an honor. Our desserts were incredible. Overall, I'm blown away. I'm so proud of my Bronx brother kwame. You put your life on a plate and I thank you for that. The food here is made for royalty by royalty and I will forever be a supporter of your visions. Every person here is as beautiful as the food. Dining here is a journey through perfection, excellence and love. My favorite establishments, hands down.
