Okay y'all know I'm % foodie all day everyday and when I tell the experience here was above board STELLAR from the walk in.....thank you to the algorithm gods for putting this on my radar and my friend for being a foodie and persistent...... because they are Booked Booked!!!!!! (Call daily for cancellations).

The staff is super polite attentive pleasant informative and accommodating. The cocktails and each dish was just amazingly eruptive in flavoring......the overall simplicity and nods of the Caribbean Indian and African spicing/herbs just pure magic......each bite enhancing the next with sauces that exploded to the next level. There was no wrong choice or moment that a dish was just okay......the entire experience mind-blowing .

Culinary Delights had:

CURRIED GOAT PATTIES
Green Seasoning Aioli, Mango Chutney

SCALLOP PINCHOS
Jerk BBQ, Spiced Oregano, Onion Confit

CRISPY OKRA
Honey, Mustard, Peppa Sauce

TAKE-OUT MUSHROOMS
Scallion Pancake, Plum Sauce, Pickled Ginger

Dessert:

HARLEM CHOCOLATE FACTORY WHITE CHOCOLATE CHEESECAKE
French Vanilla Mousse, Chocolate Ganache, Brown Butter Graham Crumble

If you're in New York and the area this is definitely a must have experience......I look forward to going back and future expansions of the menu.

We had SUCH a fantastic time at Tatiana (or "Tatiana's" for the fam ).  From the time we arrived the energy was top tier! We were quickly greeted and escorted to our table (sans any pretentious nagging about being slightly late). Before we even sat down two team members complimented our outfits which, I know, has nothing to do with the meal but really put us in a fantastic mood.

As for the food! I mean, like be for real! I was FANTASIZING about the okra for DAYS! OKRA!!! We shared the curry goat patties, scallops, crab eguisi, crispy okra and, of course, the pastrami short rib. The flavors were so well balanced and everything was perfectly prepared, so I won't go into detail, I'll just make a few highlights.

1. I'm Caribbean so goat is like a food group, I never realized until reading these reviews and eating with my homegirl (who had NEVER had it) that it really is uncommon for Americans. With that said, this is a PERFECT intro item the curry is perfectly flavorful and the goat is prepped well so the meat is tender. Highly recommend!

2. Did I mention the okra? I didn't even know you could cook okra that way. It was giving crispy Brussels sprouts sexy older sister. MUST TRY!

3. Sonnets have been written about the Pastrami short rib, everything they say is true. But for those with dogs at home, and to give a sense of the portion, my aggressive chewing English Bulldog is still happily working away at the bone 10 days later! 

After our meal Chef Kamat (Chef Kwame was traveling that day) graciously stopped by our table so we could sing her praise.  We love the upscale yet homey environment, Burna Boy playlist and exquisitely black diaspora energy of this place.

We will be back as soon as we snag another reservation...may the odds be ever in our favor!

Hands down, this is the absolute best dining experience I've ever had. Ever.

Let's start with wait time for the table. My friends and I arrived right before our reservation. The moment we gave the hostess our name she introduced us to our table. The total interaction took less than 30 seconds. How efficient!

Our waitress, Shay, was so beautifully pleasant! She's down to earth to make sure we enjoyed every part of our experience. She recommended the best dishes and not a single part of the meal disappointed us.

The appetizers, truffle chop cheese, hamachi escovitch, and curry goat empanadas were love at first bite. I fell in love with each bite and even deeper in love the closer to the end I got. The paired pepper sauce to the Pattie's were 10/10. We were even happier to find out that it's Chef Kwame's grandfathers recipe. Definitely tasted like home. The main entrees, Short Rib Suya, oxtails and Sofrito Suya had us eating in silence. It was hands down the best meal to date.

To place the icing on the cake, the man himself Chef Kwame Onwuachi made him way around the dining area to greet each and every client. Now I've been to thousands of restaurants and I've never been greeted by the Chef/Owner before. Not only did he come by to say hi once, but 3 times total. Our party chit chatted with him, asked him a few questions and thanked him numerous times for his culinary vision.

From the cuisine, to the vibe, to the outstanding customer service. Tatiana embodies what it means to embrace your culture, and putting your own twist to it. This place deserves as much press and publication as it can get.

It's going to blow your mind and exceed every expectation. 100/10 experience.

10/10! Everything about this restaurant is fabulous from the food to the service, to the ambiance and even the bathroom is a vibe! We started with Hamachi Escovitch, Curried Goat Patties, Egusi Dumplings and the Honeynut Puri Piri Salad. I could go on and on about how good every dish was because it really was that good. The salad is so fresh and light so it was a nice mix with some of the other heavier dishes we ate. And I LOVED the goat patties. I could have eaten several orders of them. I love sauces and all the sauces with the dishes are wonderful additions to the food. For our main dishes, we shared the Take-Out Mushrooms and the Short Rib Pastrami Suya. The pastrami is so, so, so good! It's perfectly cooked and seasoned and the warm caraway coco bread it comes with is so soft and fluffy. All of it is just yum! The mushrooms and scallion pancake were also very good, but I definitely would have ordered another meat dish had I not been with someone who jumped to order the mushrooms before I could get another order in (lol). We finished with the Rainbow Cookie Panna Cotta and the Harlem Choclate Factory White Chocolate Cheesecake. Both desserts are good, but the cheesecake is a standout. That is very good! To accompany my food, I had the watermelon margarita which was perfect for me, not too strong but didn't take like I was drinking juice. 

The restaurant has a very chill and hip vibe with the best Hip Hop/R&B music playing. The staff are very attentive and all so pleasant. I can't wait to go back and I will be back (whenever I can get another reservation)!

Note: I forgot to get a pic of the piri piri salad, egusi dumpling and desserts before we started eating.

I can see why it's hard to get a table. I ordered the curry goat patties & oxtail. Everything was delicious!
Nutcrackers were amazing as well. I loved the ambiance & music selection! Service was amazing!
I can't wait to come back!

Great experience. Very cozy atmosphere with a with a splash of sophistication. Dimly lit to stimulate conversation and string drinks to help move things along. The food was excellent despite the portions being a bit small for the price tag! The Wagyu Short Rib was was a stand out .. it will leave you wanting more! Reservations are hard to get here so plan ahead!

The Afro-Caribbean restaurant located in the heart of Lincoln center had my palette experiencing fireworks all night long. From the minute you walk in to the time that you leave the music was a vibe from reggae to hip hop. the dim lighting sets the mood. The story behind the restaurant being named after the chefs sister is a story in itself. I was beyond excited to finally be able to reservations to try out this place. I waited 28 days and it was worth the countdown. 
Every appetizer, entree, and dessert was beautifully plated & was filled with so many unique flavors! I will definitely be returning because there are many dishes on that menu I need to try, the scallop pinchos being one of them !! My mom loves oxtail and goat, we were not diss appointed at all. I'm a sucker for a good dessert the rainbow cookie pannacotta was absolutely delicious top 5 favorite desserts. Now let me tell you the little Debbie cosmic brownie "bodega special" took me back to my childhood. It reminded me so much of when i use to eat them. The powdered donut that's served along side, replicates the taste as if you're physically biting into a donut. Chef Kwame understood and killed the assignment.

This was a truly exquisite dining experience. A+ service from the moment we came to the moment we left. The menu is divided into main plates and small plates to share. We had:
- Braised oxtail (a must try)
- Curried goat patties (I liked the crispy shell more than the filling but overall it was yummy) 
- Egusi dumplings (favorite small plate) 
- Crispy okra (not a fan of okra usually but this was really flavorful, and had a spicy kick) 

We thoroughly enjoyed the house-made chili oil and it paired well with almost all the dishes. The restaurant is located near the Lincoln center which makes it a convenient place to eat before/after shows if you have a reservation. Great service, food and experience. Highly recommend.

After visiting Kwame's restaurant Kith & Kin in DC back in 2018, I was excited to check out his latest Lincoln Center endeavor. The menu was different of course but the vibes were still the same. A fusion of Afro-Carribbean in his own modern take that draws flavors from New York City and the culture here. Egusi dumplings and black bean hummus tells this story perfectly. Blending flavors and spinning classics into new favorites the menu features a selection of large plates and small. We focused on trying things we've never had before and started with the scallops pinchos that had a jerk bbq sauce on top. Smokey and a bit sweet, the scallops were cooked perfectly. We also ordered the black bean hummus, truffle chopped cheese, and crispy okra along with the dumplings and hummus. All of which I recommend. The berber spiced lamb on the hummus was so delicious, especially when dipped with the crisp flat bread it comes with. The okra is dry-fried, not 100% sure what that means but it translates to very light and crispy. Not slimy at all and covered in a spice rub. I know these were all the small plates but as a party of two, I wish there was just a tad bit more. Groups of 3+ should definitely order a large plate in addition to a few small. This is the kind of place where the flavor and ingredients are the star of the show. Not a huge portions fill up kind of place, quality over quantity and giving you flavors to savor kind of place. Make a reservation and try the cosmic brownie dessert.

Mediocre experience. Came to celebrate my birthday and was really excited to be able to secure a reservation the day before. I wanted to add an additional family member to my reservation so I called and left a message (they were closed on Monday). I made sure to call as early as I could day-of, to request the addition, and did not have high expectations, but figured it was worth a shot. The host who answered was very nice, and assured me that she could add a third to the party, but would need push the reservation time to 15 minutes later. I told her that was absolutely fine and thanked her. I got an email notification from resy that the time was changed, but didn't actually read the email because I trusted that all would be as discussed. I also noted that it was a birthday - not only in the voicemail, but on resy.

Fast forward to arriving at the restaurant: two members of our three-person party arrived ~15 minutes early, and checked in, but were told the party needed to be complete to be seated. The hosts surprisingly had no knowledge of the change from two to three people... when I heard this and checked the email, sure enough, it still said two people. This was disappointing because it seemed to impact where we were able to sit in the restaurant. I was a few minutes late. I don't think more than 6 or 7 minutes - if that much - and we ended up seated in the less-appealing area of the restaurant - not the main dining area. I asked the host who sat us if there was a possibility we could be seated elsewhere, even if there was a wait, and the manager (not sure if this was the host manager or manager of the restaurant) stated that everyone had just been seated, but didn't really seem apologetic about it. Throughout the couple of hours we spent there, I also saw a six-top that had the luxury of being seated as an incomplete party (only half had been at the table within the first hour were were there), so I found that interesting.

There is no uniformity in the restaurant in terms of dress. While it's fantastic that there's no dress code for patrons - the staff dress code is disjointed. All of the servers and runners had a clear dress code. Dark slacks/shirts. I think some may have even had half-aprons. Of what felt like the five or six hosts milling about at the stand: there were two in dark slacks and blazers, some with sneakers and dresses, one with an oversized sweatshirt on....the person who was introduced as the manager was dressed just as casually with a crop top and short skirt. It was giving confusion... why have a clear dress code for some staff but not others?

Out server was okay in the beginning. We couldn't hear her, and she couldn't hear us due to the volume of the music (which was very good, by the way!) but we eventually got our orders in. No ask about us celebrating or anything. The main food arrived hot and I can't complain about the taste at all, but it was pricey for the portions. We didn't see our server again or have her ask if all was okay until we were just about scraping the last bits off of our plates. No desire to make the dining experience special. Dessert was the least exciting taste-wise and although I shouldn't have been - based on the service prior to dessert - I was surprised that there wasn't even a candle in the cosmic brownie or the extra order (tiny - half scoop?) of ice cream.

Maybe it was an off night all-around. The food was solid, albeit pricey, but after that experience I wouldn't give high marks for service outside of the incredibly prompt and polite food runners. I'm really disappointed that the experience wasn't a special one for my birthday.

I cannot say enough about the quality and excellent experience my wife and I had at this restaurant in NYC. The food was simply superb and the drinks were amazing. I mean... amazing! I highly recommend this spot though it is expensive. That being said, one item I thought was great was that their dishes can be shared between individuals so that despite the expense, it was not over what we may have otherwise spent at other fancy places we have gone to in recent times, where the PPP was through the roof! All I can say is that fine dining is not without a cost and the reality is that great food is worth every dollar when you walk out with a smile from side to side.

Likewise, the ambiance and friendliness of the staff are also details that have to be brought into view because it wasn't that the food was, Aline, great, but the experience was wonderful.

Try that pastrami ditch... OMG! What a delight. If you get a chance, check'm out!

I was super excited to try Tatiana, and it did not disappoint.  My first time here was with two friends and my mom, and I knew I had to show my boyfriend. I came back with him on Tuesday, and we immediately made a reservation the next day for one month from now. We are devastated we have to wait a whole month to come back, so we might try to walk in for bar seating sometime sooner.

Dishes (in order of my favorite to least favorite) 

1. Goat Patties: MUST TRY. My mom's favorite. My two friends' favorite. My favorite. I would eat 6 of these myself.

2. Chopped Cheese: Worth trying if you like patty melts. This was my boyfriend's favorite dish. 

3. Black bean hummus: everyone is skeptical when I say this dish slaps because they're thinking "how can hummus be that good?" It is. There's some chili oil for spice and the ground lamb bits are so good. 

4. Oxtail: very tender and the coconut rice that it is served with is so good too.

5. Wagyu pastrami: very rich. It was a good dish but I was so full at this point.

6. Hamachi: a very light dish but nothing particularly special

7. Egusi dumplings: thought this was just ok.

OMG after finally getting a reservation I must say it was worth the hassle . Me and two of my friends decided. To eat here one night while he was in the city from DC . The atmosphere , food and service was the bomb . We tried a the coco bread , Honeynut Piri Piri salad, Egusi dumplings, Truffle chop cheese , the braised oxtail and the snapper. I enjoyed every single item we ordered my favorite was the oxtails and the truffle chop cheese . If you can get a reservation you will not be disappointed.

Tatiana - Wow - Chef Kwame has a style of his own serving classic food like Red Snapper, Oxtail with a new twist nicely done. The restaurant itself is a glorified cafeteria - nightclub atmosphere! The music is to loud making it hard to have a pleasant conversation. It's very dark making it hard to read the menu, no candle on my table.The service was slow and they seem to be inexperienced for the quality of the food being served. If your one of the lucky ones to get a reservation - please remember it's all about chef Kwame FOOD.
Chef Kwame Red Snapper with the head please Caribbean way

I was so excited to visit Tatiana. I made a huge effort to secure a reservation for my Sister's birthday and I was really looking forward to the night. Unfortunately, I experienced one of the worst experiences with a server that I can recall ever having. 

The food was immaculate. The patty, the oxtails, the suya the dumplings - we enjoyed every morsel. As Nigerians it was a great sensory experience to see our traditional flavors prepared in a new and innovative way.

Our server literally ruined our night. I have worked in the service industry and I know that late reservations after a long night can be especially difficult but our experience was exceptionally off putting. She was rude, nonchalant, visibly irritated and unpleasant. It really put a damper on the energy of our evening. I was especially discouraged after I witnessed a blatantly rude/disrespectful interaction between her and my friend who inquired about placing an order and instead of being acknowledged was on the receiving end of a single finger raised in her face as if to say - stop talking. It was shocking. She made shallow attempts to blame her mood on other things (ranging  from how busy she was to another customer's allergies) but to have her somewhat acknowledge that she was treating us badly while continuing to do so was so confusing...

It's sad that I walk away from this night primarily remembering the negative energy my party and I were on the receiving end of and not the delicious food.

Ambiance is amazing but food overall was decent and not spectacular. I expected more surrounding all of the hype. The sofrito chicken wasn't as seasoned as expected. Yes, lots of sauce, but the chicken itself didn't have much flavor. I was told it's cooked to order, so maybe it's not properly marinated for that reason. The brown stew red snapper I expected it to be stewed as its title says, however it was fried. Wasn't great, but wasn't bad. I did enjoy the okra, as I'm not a fan of okra but I enjoyed the way it was prepared here. The curried goat patties were good, but I wasn't wowed about them. The truffle chopped cheese was interesting and I enjoyed the presentation of it. The black bean hummus was tasty and different than the average hummus, so enjoyable. Personally, the biggest disappointment was the bodega special. Maybe it's just me because I read a lot of great reviews about it and expected it to be over the top, but I didn't find it to be able to stand apart from any other rich chocolate brownie type dessert. 
The prices I feel were high for the quality of the food, but I guess it compensates for the location. A sprite which comes in a small 8 oz glass bottle was $8 just to put things into perspective. 
Overall, great experience but I probably wouldn't return unless the menu changes here and there. I am also glad to support a black owned business.

This place is amazing! I was just there tonight and am already craving to go back. Staff are accommodating  and  kind. The vibe is sexy dark with good music.  The food !!!!!!  Every dish was just WOW. HIGHLY RECOMMEND !

I have been waiting for months to get reservations here. I've been on the resy website and waiting list and called american express for their reservation services, no luck. A friend told me she just walked in and was lucky enough to get a seat at the bar, so I tried the same tactic. It wasn't as successful, but I did get a table for two the next day

The ambiance is incredible, perfect spot for a date night. There is a blue/purple mood light throughout the restaurant. The staff was just as poised and attentive as you'd expect at a restaurant you have to get lucky to get in. And the best part? Trap and twerk music the whole time. Waka Flocka Flame, Travis Porter, Meg the Stallion, Pop Smoke, Lil Wayne. You name a guilty pleasure, they played it. Definitely not the environment to dance in, but so therapeutic to be fine dining to music that feels so familiar

Now for the star of the show, the food. We ordered a sprinkling of everything to get a taste of as much of their menu as we could. The portions of the appetizers ranged from small portion to shareable but the entrees were definitely enough to fill us alone. 
- egusi dumplings: they were okay. I tasted more of the crab filling than egusi but the red stew it sat ontop of was really nice and i wouldve enjoyed it by itself 
- crispy okra: GET THIS!! I have a pack of okra in my fridge right now waiting for me to recreate this dish. Because it was roasted, it doesn't have the slimy okra texture but crispy like a chip instead. The description in the menu listed mustard and honey as part of the components giving this dish its flavor. The sweetness of the honey was a lot more pronounced than any mustard-y tang but the heat was silent and deadly, building up in intensity with each bite. This was a shareable appetizer but it was so good, we inhaled it down to a clean plate in no time
- chopped cheese: another must have. The upscale rendition on a deli favorite was incredible. The bread alone would've satisfied me. It was so light and almost melted away in your mouth. The beef was definitely a good cut, there were no chewy pieces. The truffle wasn't overbearing. I did a little dance for each bite
- scallop pinchos: my friend ordered this and i tried a couple, wasn't crazy about it. The scallops were well made, the presentation was nice, and they were cute bite size pieces but the jerk sauce didn't taste anything like jerk nor did whatever that sauce was complement the scallops in any way
- brown stew red snapper with rice and peas: my friend ordered this as well. She reported that the fish was nice and moist, however, the brown sauce on it was just sweet. Not exactly brown stewed. She also wasn't impressed with the rice and peas
- short rib pastrami suya: this came with melted cabbage, fresh bread with carraway seeds and sauce on the side. The short rib was incredibly tender it fell off the bone. The suya spice ontop was a great accompaniment to the tender meat. The melted cabbage was sweet and the cabbage was a little softer that I'd go for, but that didn't stop us from cleaning the plate. The bread, I wasnt a fan of, the caraway seeds were overbearing to me so it sat in my plate and i wasn't quite sure what to do with it
- rainbow panacotti: the streusel on top was my favorite, the rest of it was average
- bodega special: up until now, I have no idea what role the sorrel played in this dessert. I did not taste it at all and I'm really not a dessert person but I love sorrel so that was disappointing. The warm brownie and ice cream went well together though 

Overall, I would come again. The things they did good was AMAZING and the things they didn't do so great was probably based on our biases but was good enough. Like I really enjoyed the atmosphere and the crispy okra and chopped cheese were enough for me to wait on a waiting list for but their attempts at traditionally jamaican dishes (jerk sauce, rice and peas, brown stew fish) missed the mark for our expectations but were still prepared well. Considering that, i would try something like their curried goat patties out of curiosity because I know it won't be awful but I also know it won't be my mom and grandma's curried goat in the patties. I left feeling stuffed and satisfied. Enjoyed my night there

**there is one single bathroom that there's often a line to so don't wait til the very last minute to go or plan a 20min bathroom trip

Reservations are hard to come by & I see why. I really enjoyed this place. From the decor to the music to the food to the service. We had a reservation for 9:15 and did have to wait about 15mins to be seated. They were busy on a Wednesday evening.

Once we were seated the waitress checked in. We like to order starters and then the entrees but we had to order all at once-- but no worries it comes out 1 by 1!

We tried the truffle chopped cheese, curry goat empanadas, crispy okra, egusi dumplings (only thing I did not enjoy) and the pastrami short rib. I had the birthday martini first, which I didn't really enjoy & the pina pina after which was delicious!
Believe the HYPE! Money will worth it. Definitely will be back. Very flavorful. Don't worry about the price you will leave satisfied.
It was Perfect! Flavor, food and vibes. Don't wait. Make a reservation asap!!!!!!!!!!

Hey hey! Let's hear it for the young brother Kwame doin his thang in the MIDDLE OF LINCOLN CENTER!! 
Food: Def felt and tasted like fine dining. GET THE HUMMUS 

Service: We had a dude who looked like he lived in Williamsburg with 9 other dudes or like Shaggy from Scooby Doo. He was in training and tried to turn it on...but he just looked like he didn't want to be there. The main waitress (I think her name was Kaydene) came to sub him out or check on us and it was like a breath of fresh air during our time there. 
Shoutout to the hostess stand too, my wife was running about 15 minutes behind and they were hella accommodating. 

Ambiance: Beautiful decor, artwork and flowers. Black opulence! And don't forget to visit the handicap bathroom it's SEXY! Oh and I love Drizzy Drake but turn down the volume!

Took a while to get a ressy but finally made it on an early Tuesday evening.

Loved just about everything about my experience.  We were a party of two with a 5pm ressy and finally got up from the table at 7:30pm.  I LOVE a restaurant that doesn't push you out the door.

I don't know what more I can say about the food that hasn't already been said but here goes:

Standout:  
Curry Goat Empanadas- we had to order a second plate of these they were that good

Oxtail- fall off the bone soft and perfectly sticky.  The sauce was divine- i could take a straw and slurp it up

Really Good:
Black bean Hummus - wow the texture was incredibly smooth but that lamb ragú gives all the feels you need.  The 'bread' was named after someone I forget but were very much like thin fried 'bake' (if you are familiar with Caribbean food you know what I mean) 

Strawberry Margarita- very tasty but light on the strawberry flavor.  Not much drink due to the huge ice though

Jell-O shot- the presentation is gorgeous with the gold flecks and the marbling & complexity of the shot but 2 for $12 seems like highway robbery.

The okay:
Egusi dumplings - my husband really enjoyed this but I was underwhelmed.  The red Nigerian stew included was pretty good however 

Cheesecake - pretty & sweet but not very special tasting in the NY cheesecake scene

Best:  the Service!  My server was Wogey and she was A1!  We want her to go work at our regular fine dining restaurant just so we could see her more often.  She guided and curated our experience expertly.  She was engaging and knowledgeable and professional with a bright smile- it gets no better.

- food was good
- I managed to get an easier reservation when going in person
- I also called and made an easy adjustment on my reservation
- environment is hip
- hip music is playing
- they have walk in opportunity available at bar
- alcohol gummies were night thing to try
  I didn't get lit or anything
- cocktails tasted very good
- chopped cheese, patties, and dumplings were good
- short rib was good, 
  enough to feed to people to perfect satiation
  all the ingredients complemented each other  in a way I never thought possible
  I really liked the mustard
- the cosmic brownie and powdered doughnut ice cream were good
  I really hope I didn't pay all that money for a cosmic brownie, I could get from the store for 50 cents
- I didn't feel as blown away by the experience as I thought i'd be

Tatiana has been everywhere, so I was excited when I snagged a reservation. Now with lots of hype comes lots of expectations.

The ambiance was really nice. The chairs were comfortable and the lighting was soft. The service was fine. The waitress may not have noticed but her face was very judgmental.

Overall, the food was great! I really really liked it. My issue is that for the price, it's almost not worth it, and I don't care. My Asian ancestors are rolling over in their grave knowing I just paid $30 for 3 dumplings. It's WILD. A lot of the menu feels like expensive versions of things you can get for cheap that are still really good. 

The food also came out staggered so we didn't get our entrees together there was a big gap. The food also never tasted piping hot but always lukewarm, which threw me off.

Crab Dumpling: 8.5/10

The filling of these dumplings is so unique. The crab tastes so fresh. I also like the sauce.

Curried Goat Patties: 9.5/10

This was my favorite dish! The Pattie's were so flakey and soft. It was shaped like a typical patty but the texture reminded me of a croissant with how light it was. The sauce and chutney with the curried goat were fabulous. I wish I could've had more!

Short Rib Pastrami Suya: 9/10

The short rib fell off the bone immediately. The meat was so soft. It was so buttery you didn't have to chew at all. It tasted exactly like pastrami but better.

The bread was a bit dry and dull, but I loved the take on mustard and the sweet onions. Overall this dish was incredible, but given the price, I almost would have preferred to get something else where I could try something that is unlike anything I've ever tasted. This tasted like pastrami but with elite meat.

Oxtail: 9/10

I really enjoyed the rice that came with this dish and had a subtle hint of coconut. It was perfect with the sweet sauce from this dish. The oxtail fell right off the bone. The meat was tender and soft. It melted in my mouth. Overall the flavor was great too. Not too sweet and a little spicy.
Am still waiting for a day to visit this place . The waiting list is long . I have to post 5 stars because you got to be a star to get in it seems

There is little to say here that hasn't already been said. The food is, in fact, delicious, the service was smooth, and the ambiance is fitting for the restaurant's vibe. 

I am mostly here to attest that the food is not hype. It is a coming-home-sigh-of-deliciousness on your palate. It is what many Michelin star restaurants pretend to be, but aren't. It is utter, wouldn't-change-a-thing satisfaction.
The food was delicious, and the ambiance was perfect for a nice dinner for two. There wasn't one "miss" on the cohesive menu -and we tried 6 dishes. Highly recommend!

Although the prices are expensive, food, drinks, and service are outstanding. It's a beautiful venue, smaller than I thought but still has a great vibe. Highly recommend. Wish I had more pics of the food

From the food presentation to specific details esthetically of the footprint down to the menu and saucer exhibit upon arrival, most important the amazing flavors of each item that were very well balanced  it was an overall amazing experience (my apologies for the run-on sentence). To top it off our server was very personable and flat out amazing..... great vibes as soon as you enter as well.
Tatiana's was on the small side but the private room we occupied along with the food and service Exceeded my expectations!

Let me start by saying we had a good experience and importantly loved the food, ambiance and location of Tatiana's. Right next to the Met there is a buzz and energy to the place and the diversity of staff and patrons is wonderful. 
Food was uniformly excellent - the two of us shared 4 smalls and one large along with one dessert and five drinks. About $300 all- in so not inexpensive. 
Why the removal of one star. 
Our server was very nice but despite discussing we wanted to be there two hours pre- opera and pace the food and drinks in a order, everything came out in a 10 minute interval. That's a problem at a place charging these prices. We had to send back the large plate ( fish) that they were nice about and brought us a fresh one 30 minutes later but we had to do all the smalls together. 
For food our rankings at 9/10 go to 4 of the 5 and surprisingly not to the restaurants most popular item- the curried goat patties that were great but too doughy for our taste. We had the okra, Egusi dumplings, the new jerk cod/ cornbread and the brown stew Red Snapper - each of these was terrific. The bordega brownie was excellent as well. 

We had the Margarita ( beautiful presentation but so so), Benton's old fashioned( excellent) and a  Chablis- our server was good enough to allow us to taste a few wines before choosing. 
So overall great- just fix the glitch in the kitchen of not pacing orders.

Chef Kwame is a mastermind. Putting together a menu that personifies his West African and Caribbean roots and sprinkling New York Culture to create a culinary masterpiece. He even stopped by our table to check in on our experience. 

The concepts is tapas that are intended to be shared. At first glance they look small and delicate but they are actually rich and filling. Also my partner who is vegan had a ton of options as well.

Some of my favorites was the curry goat patties, the truffle chopped cheese, egusi dumplings, and the takeout mushrooms. The restaurant esthetics is nice as well - good music, hip and modern. 

Great places if you want impress a date or grab a few friends and fam to share some dishes. Really good for all occasions. Reservation come out daily for a 30 day window. Keep refreshing and be comfortable with going anytime to get a seat at hottest restaurant right now.

5 stars from a reviewer who ordinarily shares 4 star restaurants worth an outing for food alone.  You get that and more for a terrific dining experience at Tatiana.  All are welcome, if you can afford the tab.  Expect lively atmosphere in an amazing setting and warm and friendly service from everyone on board.  If you've never tried oxtails but are intrigued, go for their take and be prepared for heavenly bites.  I have never had a salad without greens that had all the best things about a salad before our server recommended the Peri Peri Salad, a dish I won't forget that pairs so well with their must get curry goat patties.
Amazing! Delicious! Worth the wait and price! Ver creative! In a wonderful setting! Need I say more...!

Tatiana, located within the adored David Geffen Hall- gorgeous location with tamed sophisticated interiors.
The hosts were all so lovely, waited about 2min after our actual reservation time. 

Was seated by the window which was lovely, our waitress Beatriz was helpful and v accommodating. 

Ordered the famous spicy margarita- ok, smoothest margarita I've ever had in New York- and it's my go to drink! 

We got the PeriPeri Salad- the sauce or dressing explodes in your mouth, alright. Beautifully made. 

For mains; oxtail and the wagyu ribs. 
Oxtail  was delish! Although it's was a staple take- it was def made very very well, melt in your mouth and v flavorful. 

Ribs was screaming quality, nothing too outstanding besides how well it was done! Take the cabbage, meat and mustard on your bread and take it all in one is the perfect bite *chef'a kiss*


A commendation for the service- our appetizer came before my drink and the manger noticed and because of it, we were treated with an appetizer on the house- the crab dumplings- which was good. 

The cheesecake was a unique take- don't skip on it. It's worth the sugar.

Overall- a lovely night with delicious food. 
Will I go back again, Definitely. 
Is it just a hype- perhaps. But it's worth the hype.

My dining experience at Tatiana was phenomenal!
First I was to say the staff was so lovely and kind and made a really good impression. The ambiance inside the restaurant was a nice vibe they were playing good music but I ended up eating outside.

For drinks i got the POG. Nutcracker and the Strawberry Field Margarita. The nutcracker was  pretty strong and gave me a nice buzz. The margarita has a basic presentation but it was smooth and really nice. I would order it again

For small plates I had the curry  patties, the cod and cornbread and the egusi dumplings. I really enjoyed everything but the goat patties were on another level. I couldn't get enough of the green aioli and the mango chutney. It also comes with a habanero sauce if you want to add some spice. The cod and cornbread is really underrated I would definitely give that a try!!

For my large plate I had the Mom Duke shrimp which had really great flavors and the brioche bread was perfect toasted and delicious to help sop up that yummy sauce!

The true star of the show was the bodega special. The brownie was moist and delicious but that ice cream? SO good! You would think powdered donut flavored ice cream would be to sweet but it wasn't, it was perfect. 

All in All it was a great experience and I can't wait to go back. I'm really proud of Chef Kwame!

Very poor service and treatmet. 

Earlier this week, Tatiana expanded to outdoor dining, effectively doubling to twice its capacity of the enclosed restuarant.  On Wednesday (5/10/23) and Thursday (5/11/23), I inquired as to reservations for this Friday and was told for outdoor dining there was none.  Essentially, show up, if space is available, you will be seated.

When I returnd  on Friday (5/12/23) at 6:45 pm, I learned that the outdoor dining was closed, despite having open tables both in the dining room and outdoors, since the kitchen could not prepare the meals due to the expansion of the outdoor dining. The waiting time was two hour.  When my girlfriend arrived at 6:55 pm, she began to make inquiries, largely getting the same answers (i.e., run-a-round).  The big difference was that there was now a waiting list that had opened up at 4:45 pm and we could put our name on that list. (There was no mention of a waiting list on either Thursday or Friday).

Obviously, the story kept changing the longer we waited and asked more questions.   To summarize, when popular, you can treat your potential patrons like dirt.  You can lie to them, mislead them, look down on them.  However, in a city where 2 out of 3 restuarants fail in two years of opening, No restuarant can treat the public like this and survive.

My advice is steer clear of Tatiana until they can accommodate their patrons in all of their seating and learn some manners.

Bill Short

Thoroughly impressed with the food and staff. Cheers to chef Kwame! The suya pastrami, snow crab and oxtails are must haves. I suggest attending as a group, good is served in large portions family style fine dining.

It is no wonder that this place was raved by The NY Times. The menu is limiting, yes, BUT everything single item on their menu looked delicious and you can't go wrong with any of them. We got the egusi dumplings, curried goat patties (my favorite), the short rib pastrami, and the bodega special. The only problem I had was that I thought a ridiculous amount of meat was provided with the pastrami and I had so little bread to eat it with. Definitely on purpose, but I just personally prefer a larger bread to meat ratio. Everything was absolutely delicious and I was so sad that I couldn't take anything order to go. Considering how difficult it was for me to get a reservation, I was very lucky to have a taste of what Kwame Onwyachi had to offer. I would love to come again if I had the chance to try the oxtail.

Having been to Tatiana twice now I can ensure you that you are in for a delicious meal and a good vibe/night out. The ambiance of Lincoln Center speaks for itself, then you add the fantastic meals by Kwame and team and THAT'S IT. I've enjoyed the HUGE oxtails, curried goat patties (twice and I'm not ashamed), the egusi dumplings, to name a few things. Every dish is flavorful, thoughtful, and just DELICIOUS.

Tatiana's drinks are delicious as well. They're carefully made so YOU be careful not to have too many. They don't have a strong alcoholic taste but it's definitely present.

Everything else about Tatiana: the location, the music, the open kitchen... makes me very very proud of this team and thankful for it's addition to the NYC specifically Manhattan scene. Reservations are strongly recommended via Resy and I hope you enjoy as much as I did (:

For honesty and transparency - during my first visit the service was extremely slow, I am guessing since my group was one of the later reservations of the night. Our waiter removed 20% for the inconvience which I thought also spoke to the hospitality. We put that right back toward tip, but still it set the tone for my perception of the experience. Thank YALLL

Very meh. Disappointing! Was there on a Monday night. The hamachi appetizer was tasteless - hard, not buttery and soft. The king crab dish was also tasteless/bitter. The service was awful. Had 3 different servers as each one seemed to disappear. Waited forever for our main courses and the restaurant was not crowded. They did apologize and bought us a dessert. But for over 100$ a person none of this should have been acceptable. 
The red snapper was delicious - but everything else was not.
Very disappointing!!!
Food was great, atmosphere was amazing I would definitely recommend this to family and friends, and I won't be returning. All of the staff was nice and polite and professional.

I will never stop talking about this food and 10 out of 10 experience. OMG! Each dish was so delicious. I savored each and every bite. From the goat patty with mango chutney and the other sauce i'm not sure what it was but so very good. The patty was flakey and golden to perfection. I adored the mango chutney (i'm biased because i'm a mango stan)! The caesar salad was yummy and the radish was the star in this dish to me. 

The suya pastrami deserves its own paragraph because how?! This is a masterful dish. I don't consume meat often so I am a hard critic when it comes to the quality and when I tell you, it literally fell off the bone. I wish I took a photo when I cut into it. The pickled cabbage was also so good to pair with it. And that salted buttery bread - nomnomnom. So filling but didn't make me feel too heavy. The mustard sauce was also yum but you don't need it at all. 

We also enjoyed a glass of their sauvignon blanc which was quite nice and they had an awesome pour. 

Aside from the bomb food, the service was wonderful. The host was super sweet. When she sat us, she was full of compliments and delight. Our server asked how each bite was and my sister made sure to let her know the ancestors were present in each dish. 

The restaurant is gorgeous inside and they played some of the classics and my personal favorites like Future's "March Madness" and Juvenile's "Slow Motion." Gayle King also made an appearance so we knew we were in the right place because we trust Aunty. 

Absolutely will come back! Very difficult to get a resy here so be sure to book well in advance.
I dream about the food. 10/10! Service and Ambiance are also very solid. My current favorite place in the city

The NYT was absolutely right.  The food was amazing.  The flavors are exotic and work well together. The large to share is enough for at least 3 people.   We had the short rib pastrami.  Loved it. The red snapper had no bones and was superb.  The oxtail to die for-fell off the bone.  We had the chicken shwarma which came with lamb and rice which was a meal in and of itself.   Definitely will be back if we can get a reservation.

I would give this place 6 stars if I could. I officially have a new favorite restaurant. Kwame is a master on all levels. Beautiful restaurant. Awesome staff. The food? Unbelievable. Inventive, artful, delicious and oh so different. You will never taste anything like it again. I give it all available thumbs up!

I damn near sold my unborn baby to get this reservation. No, seriously getting a resy here is next level impossible. I logged on so many days and within seconds (no exaggerating) they are gone. Needless to say, I've gone on every day and put the "notify" button on. I randomly logged onto resy yesterday and BAM a 9:15 reservation was available. The resy God's were with me and I said through hell or high water, whether someone was able to go, I was making it to my reservation! I threw on a cute outfit and heels and went dining solo. As I have mentioned in previous reviews, I like to make note of this when talking about a dining experience. Solo diners tend (not always) get subpar service. 

I was running 10 min late and called but no answer. Located right in Lincoln center, you past the fountain and enter into the restaurant to your right. This is on the smaller side for a restaurant. I entered and was not greeted by anyone. Awkwardly stood there for a few minutes until the white gentleman came up and asked if I was being helped. Small things such as this while dining are why michelin stars are given and places are held at a higher standard. Let me mind you, I still have no clue who the hostess was. I let him know I was alone, and it wasn't an issue. I was sat at table 63 which actually gave me a nice view of the place (open kitchen to the left w/tables and all of the tables ahead). 

The decor is dark, sexy, and modern. The dishes are a matte black and silverware is antique gold. Love the vibe! As I mentioned earlier, I came for a late reservation. The tunes were on POINT...all the awesome old school jams. The music may have been slightly louder or different than other comparable places but not to the point you are screaming over the music. I believe they change it to these vibes later on. 

I had two cocktails. The nutcracker and the pina pina. Both were very good, got me buzzed but wasn't one of my favorite cocktails I have had as of late. I'm so upset I came alone because I couldn't try as many things as I wanted. I guess I will have to make it back again if I am lucky! lol. I took the suggestion from the reviews and got the curried goat patties. That first bite....MY GOD...the flavors were everything with the mango chutney. Now, they do NOT do to-go orders buuuuut if you just so happen to order an extra order to the table and just so happen not to eat it then you can take it home. Do with that information with what you will. lol! Then I ordered the hummus which was bangin as well! Next is where things went south for me...I ordered the oxtails for my main dish. I was SO upset when she came back saying it was sold out. Oxtails are not a special on the menu and I was really bummed about them being out. I read mixed reviews about the stewed fish and would've gotten the pastrami if I were with someone. I randomly went with the mushrooms...WHY is beyond me? I am not a vegetarian or vegan (although I do like veg dishes). They came with scallian pancakes and some nuts on top. Listen, it was good but I do regret getting that dish...$48 for mushrooms and I eat meat?! Never again. I took some home since I was full and couldn't fit dessert. 

The waitress took my number down and supposedly I would be called to get a reservation to come back. I don't think I will be called but we will see. The service was pretty great! She was patient, explained everything, and when I accidently got sauce on my silverware she came and replaced it immediately. Loved that! 

Very random thing to add.... the bathroom wasn't as fabulous as the rest of the place. Nothing majorly wrong but not exactly Instagram worthy place for pics either. I will post pics to this review when I get a chance. 

While leaving, I was blessed to meet the chef himself! Great guy, very down to earth and took a selfie with me. I did mention running out of the oxtails lol. It really is always a pleasure to meet the chef. I'm hoping to come back with someone next time to try other dishes and see if I can add to the other 5-star reviews. I WILL BE BACK!

Beautiful food that dives into African diaspora cuisine! The braised oxtails were perhaps the most memorable oxtail dish I've ever had. It is a must! I also had the dumplings, but alas, 3 dumplings for $21 was not worth the price point. I should have gone for either the goat patties or the beautiful looking (and I hear quite tasteful) piri salad.

incredible. food and cocktails are next level. the Okra appetizer is a must try. the red snapper, cheesecake for dessert. amazing cocktails. lots of the menu was able to be gluten free. inventive, delicious. we loved it.

If you can get a reservation at Tatiana, Go! It is that simple. I'm more than a little skeptical when the NY Times proclaims someplace the best new restaurant in town, but for once I agree with Pete Wells. While typically restaurants in concert halls and museums are simply there for a decent meal or a quick bite before or after an event, Tatiana is a destination. Kwame Onwuachi is a gifted chef who has created an awesome new spot and is destined to be a great chef for decades.

We went here on a Sunday night and it was a really weird vibe. Half empty, but they weren't letting in anyone who wanted to sit?

Anyway, the food was amazing, for 4 people the waiter told us to do 4 small plates and 2 large plates. We were not even close to full. While each bite was delicious, it was just that... a bite! For $300 tab (without drinks) we were still SO hungry after and ended up going to get pizza. 

Very disappointed for what is supposedly NYC's best restaurant. Won't be returning.

A friend and I waited in line for about 20 minutes before opening and snagged a seat at the bar.

Bartender was very personable, vibe was on 10, and the food was really good! Oxtails we're wonderful and the waiter did a very good job of explaining the food is Afro Caribbean inspired (so no, it's not going to taste just like your Jamaican grandmother's oxtail, but yes, it's still good)

Would definitely come here again, but the way those reservations are (not) set up, maybe next year

This place has been on my radar for awhile now and I'm so glad my boyfriend and I finally went. Reservations book out a month in advance and it's highly recommended to have one in order to dine at this establishment. They do have a bar area but the dining room is a lot more pleasant and not as loud. 

Of course we wanted to try everything so we got a myriad of dishes. From the small plates we had the plantains, crispy okra, patties, and dumplings. We opted for more small plates so we could try more and were even able to order the coco bread as a side. Everything was absolutely delicious but my favorites were the dumplings and crispy okra (and I don't even like vegetables!). 

For our main we chose the oxtail which was definitely the star dish of the night. Absolutely succulent, delicious, and fall off the bone tender. The braised sauce is amazing drizzled over the rice - make sure to ask for it if you have leftovers! We finished our lovely dinner with the strawberry shortcake dessert which was the perfect ending to an amazing meal. 

Overall fantastic spot and well deserved as the number one restaurant on The NY Times list for 2023!

4.5 stars. Am I terrible for not giving Tatiana 5? I'm low key a little bummed that I came here as part of a planned event (we were in the private dining room) instead of having a fun yet methodical night out here. These are two very different dining experiences. In the first, the restaurant mainly serves as the setting at which an event is held. The food is talked about some and hopefully enjoyed, but it is not the focus. The second type of experience is one in which I would be very mindful about ordering and the night would be all about being taken on a culinary journey. I wish the latter was reflective on my experience, but alas, that was not in the cards for me. And considering how hard it is to get a reservation here, it's unlikely I'll make it back here anytime soon. So, my review is my review. We had some outstanding dishes and we had some very good dishes. The service was a little wacky. I enjoyed just about everything, I just would have ordered differently had I gone here without a large group.

We came here at around 5:45 as a party of 15 on a Tuesday. I tend to eat around 8:30, so things already felt weird. Eating dinner in daylight? I guess people do such things. As soon as we walked in, a server asked me for my drink order. I was ambushed with the drink menu but luckily I was able to decide quickly. I got the Negroni, which was excellent. I also got to try the orange wine, which was great. They told me it was on the sweeter side but there was no sweetness at all, just a fair warning in case you don't like dry orange wine (I loved it anyway). The pours were obscenely heavy. Sadly I was not looking to get drunk on this night, so I didn't take advantage. 

Food-wise, we had a preset menu. I figure that's always the case for large parties. My sense was that one of our party members communicated our desired menu to the staff beforehand, so I'm guessing you can design the preset menu yourself when booking a private room (as opposed to them having a standard one that all parties must use) I wish I would've had a say, though, because I did not get to try the oxtail nor the snow crab. I would've swapped those two for two of the three entrees we did try (the short rib and red snapper, ideally). Still, the food was mostly excellent. Innovative, delicious, spiced and spicy, diverse, unique, eclectic, and many other adjectives. The flavors here are just something else. Eats, below:

Crispy Okra w/ Honey, Mustard, Peppa Sauce: A-
I rarely eat okra so this was a treat. Not the most outstanding dish of the evening but still delicious. Sweet and spicy (too spicy for some, but not for me!)

Egusi Dumplings w/ Jonah Crab, Nigerian Red Stew, Pickled Pearl Onion: A+
A star of the night, the juicy crab meat pairing beautifully with the flavors of the stew.

Ceasar w/ Baby Mizuna, Green Seasoning, Cashew: A
I'd heard mixed reviews about this salad but I loved it. The lettuces were different than those you typically get in a Caesar, fresh and slightly bitter, holding the dressing nicely. As elevated as a Caesar can get. 

Black Bean Hummus w/ Berbere Spiced Lamb, Sweet Pickled Sultana, M'semen: A+
One of the standouts of the evening. It comes with pita, but you could easily eat this straight as a whole meal. Very rich, super creative, insanely delicious. And presentation was great too. 

Curried Goat Patties w/ Green Seasoning Aioli, Mango Chutney: A
One of the standouts in all reviews, for good reason. This is something I will probably never have again so I'm glad to have had the experience in fine dining. The meat was seasoned so well, and the salty-rich-sweet combo with the chutney was just divine. 

Honeynut Piri Piri Salad w/ Persian Cucumber, Seasonal Grapes, Crispy Quinoa: A-
Solid salad, a nice use of seasonal and fresh produce, creative but still approachable. Beautifully presented. 

Take-out Mushrooms w/ Scallion Pancake, Plum Sauce, Pickled Ginger: A+
My favorite main of the evening. A Chinese-inspired mushroom dish that were a total umami bomb. The mushrooms themselves were delicious, the texture perfect, with an absolutely incredible plum sauce (I could douse anything in that) that elevated them even more) that elevated the dish even more. 

Short Rib Pastrami Suya w/ Caraway Coco Bread, Melted Red Cabbage: A
Not a red meat person but I can appreciate how well this was done. Melt in your mouth meat with (once again) and accompaniment (in this case, the cabbage) that made the dish even better. The way many of these dishes are conceptualized is just next-level.

Red Snapper w/ Rice & Peas, Cilantro, Onion: A
Another solid protein dish, a whole fried fish seasoned and cooked beautifully. Rice served on the side, which I didn't try. 

Overall, the food was brought out so quickly and devoured with such haste that I feel like I didn't have time to truly consider and savor the food. It's a shame, because I honestly think my review would've been a five-star one if the cadence of the night was different.

Everything. Is. Fantastic. The egusi dumplings, the curry goat patties, the black bean & lamb hummus, the oxtails, everything. Finally got a reservation and I'm dreaming of how fast I can go back to try more dishes.

Had a 9:15 reservation here and was sat at exactly 9:15 which I appreciate considering the effort that went into getting this reservation! Upon walking into the restaurant, it is very intimate lighting. There are decorative blue cloud like lights hanging from the ceiling. The tables were big enough to house the family style plates and the chairs were comfy! 
Now moving onto the reason for being there: the food. We started with drinks, I had the strawberry fields I believe it was called which reminded me of a strawberry margarita. Nothing fancy, good, tasted the liquor. 
The waitress, named Shay recommended that for a party of two we should do 2-4 small plates and 1-2 large plates depending on our appetites. She was very knowledgeable and shared crowd favorites as well as her own personal favorites. 
Upon her suggestions we started with the egusi dumplings, curried goat patties, black bean hummus and crispy okra. I'll break down each one. 
Egusi dumplings: good flavors but nothing like authentic egusi stew. The crab tasted fresh! Would have preferred if these came out hotter. 
Curried goat patties: reminded me less of a patty and more of an empanada which I get is a patty but I really would have liked the flaky component of a patty. It was good alone as well as with the mango chutney and garlic aioli
Black bean hummus: this was my absolute favorite of the night! We only ordered it because there weren't anymore hot pockets and I'm so glad for that! The hummus and lamb combo with the bread reminded me of a ground beef taco but elevated! Would recommend!
Crispy okra: it was good! But there was too much honey on some pieces compared to others. 
For our main we ordered the curried snow crab and my goodness that crab and curry paired so well together! It was my second favorite. It was savory. It was delicious! 
We closed with dessert of course. We had to get the bodega special: the cosmic brownie and powdered donut flavored ice cream. When I tell you that ice cream tasted exactly as such!!! The brown was also fudgy and decadent. I just wish the ice cream wasn't so hard or frosty but the flavor makes up for it!

Overall I greatly enjoyed this restaurant! I'm glad I fell for the hype and got a reservation!

Literally everything was excellent. My fav - the hot pocket and the bodega special desert which is literally entenmans powdered donuts turned into ice cream with a warm chocolate brownie yum. Wife's favorite: oxtail: Also terrific: empanadas, fried okra, ribeye. We didn't love the strawberry shortcake or the crab dumplings!

This is a very hard review for me to write. Tatiana is now at the time of this writing the hottest restaurant in NYC. I used the Well known hack of getting there before they opened and got on a about 20 people line. At this time it was unclear if these people had reservations or not. At some point the hostesses came out and told us we could be seated at the Bar (that has 6 ) chairs if there were seats left. (There was not) or we can stand and eat in the bar area. So my partner asked what was on the menu. She was allowed into the bar and decided the menu was the same. We decided to do the standing thing but we were told we had to wait 15 min so people could be seated. After 10 min she asked a different hostess if they had any cancellations? We were told that we could have a table till 8:00 we said that was fine. We were ushered into a practically empty dining room (remained that way till 7:30) we had plenty of time to eat. The wait staff seemed very inexperienced and in the course of the evening we had 2 wait persons the second seemed competent. Everyone was very nice. We started with cocktails. Tasty but small. We opened with the Egusti dumplings. Tasty! Next the Mom Dukes Shrimp. These were Huge (both of them) (hidden message here) this might be thel first time I had to slice up my shrimp! These were served with Brioche. The sauce was fantastic. Finally we had the cheese cake they forgot to mention that the pecans were gilded very good. It was a memorable night out and dinner. However I do not think we will be regulars.

We enjoyed the food - egusi dumplings (very good) and hot pocket (okay) to start, followed by brown stew branzino (delicious). It was just the right amount of food for the two of us.

The big disappointment was the service, and -one instance, in particular. We ordered cocktails, and then one of us ordered a glass of wine to go with the branzino. The fish had already been brought to the table, and even the glass for the wine. But the glass sat unfilled, even though we were well into the fish. 

Finally, we got our server's attention. He poured the wine and explained the delay, saying something about wanting to have a new bottle of wine opened, as there was only a little left in the prior bottle. Okay. Then, to our utter surprise within a few minutes he brought out the dessert menu - as we continued to eat our "large share" dish and one of us still had an almost full glass of wine. 

We should have said the obvious at the time - we are STILL eating dinner and the server had only FINALLY poured our wine two minutes earlier.

Not sure we will return. If we do, we will be more outspoken if service is lacking.

While it's in demand, the staff are first class professionals, the drinks and food are delicious, but that is expected. Seating is certainly an issue here. While I get people make reservations, what I'm trying to come to terms with are the empty seats I see for hours while I'm grabbing a quick drink and a bite. I'm actually on-site - a seat would be nice, perhaps I would even purchase more than I would standing. Oh you have no seats available for 3 hours. Then what are those empty, currently unoccupied seats called? Oh - unavailable- I see, our definitions do not align, but thank you for the service.

We were lucky enough to get a reservation here for a Wednesday night. The setting is gorgeous and the chairs are so comfortable. Service was friendly but not warm. Drinks were great (spicy marg and negroni). The mushroom and oxtail dishes are DELICIOUS and I could not stop smiling when I ate them. The only miss food-wise were the eguzi dumplings. They are just okay - pricy for a small serving, texturally not super interesting, and the crab flavor gets lost.

All the wonderful reviews are accurate! The food was delicious. I don't normally like oxtail but the meat was so tender it fell off the bone and melted in my mouth. The crispy okra, curry goat patties and the take out mushrooms were also incredible. Definitely recommend going here!
Food was amazing, service was exceptional and ambiance was great! Definitely recommend this place if you are looking to have a nice night.

As a lover of Top Chef, Black Chefs, and Afro-Caribbean food, I just knew I had to come here. After fighting for months for a reservation, I was finally able to snag one (shout out to Amex) on a Saturday evening. We got there a few minutes after 8:15 for our reservation and waited 5 minutes to be seated. Understandably so because the restaurant does not have many tables, but the space is used well. It is dimly lit and they have an open kitchen concept so you can see the chefs cooking as you eat. I loved the vibes here! They played Afrobeats music the entire time so it really feels like a celebration of Black culture in Lincoln Center. We ordered a few drinks and they were delicious. The Pina Pina is sweet and tastes a lot like a pina colada but stronger. We had another drink which was more like a rum punch which I found had the right balance between it's sweetness and how strong it was. They also give a house-made pepper sauce for the meal and while I don't eat spicy food, my partner thoroughly enjoyed it, evidence by the empty bowl at the end o the meal.

Our server explained that the dishes are served family style and that we should order 2-3 small plates and 1-2 large plates so we did just that. Here's what we ordered:
Egusi Dumplings- Having had everything else, this honestly paled in comparison. While I did enjoy the crab mixture, I felt like something was missing from this dish. Everything felt like the same texture and umami is really the only flavor you get here. Not bad but wouldn't order again.
Curried Goat Patties: This was my favorite small plate. As many other reviews have mentioned, these are more like empanadas than patties but they are so flavorful that you don't really care! The mango chutney that comes on the side pairs perfectly with the goat meat. I would order these again and again.
Black Bean Hummus: The spiced lamb was really tasty and went well the hummus. It came topped with a pickled vegetable (not sure which) but that was the perfect bite each time. Wish it came with more pita but delicious.
Braised Oxtails: As a frequent oxtail eater, I have to say this was some of the best I've ever had. The oxtails were tender and falling off the bone, the stew was sweet and savory and they give you more than enough to pour over the accompanying rice and peas. While it only comes with 3 pieces, that is more than enough to share!
Grilled Ribeye: Was disappointed to see the Pastrami Short Rib is no longer on the menu but this did not disappoint as a substitute. They only cook this to two temperatures (medium-rare and well-done) so sorry to those who like their steak cooked otherwise. The seasoning was perfect and it comes with stewed peppers and pickled onions on the side for pops of acid. They don't offer any sides but something to go with this if you pick it for your entree would be great.
Bodega Special: I grew up eating cosmic brownies and powdered donuts, so this really brought me back to my childhood and they taste exactly the same. While the donut is made of ice cream, it really does capture the taste of a powdered donut. Though I will note, this is SUPER SWEET, I really loved this as a finish to the meal!

Some people will say this place isn't worth the hype, but I disagree. I loved every minute of my experience here and the food was awesome. If you can get a reservation- go!Rating: 5/5!

Great customer service (Neo) and the food was on point. This is a must visit location if you are in NYC. We ordering the following 

1. Curried Goat Patties 8/10
2. Tequila Jello Shots 7/10
3. Oxtail with Rice & Peas (small portion so I recommend ordering 1 per person) 10/10
4. Dessert #1: Strawberry Shortcake 6/10
5. Dessert #2: Bodega Special 8/10
6. Drink #1: Benton Old Fashioned 9/10
7. Drink #2: Piña Piña Piña 9/10

The oxtail was very tender and seasoned to perfection ( don't forget to cover your rice & peas with the oxtail sauce ). The curried goat patties were nice and flaky and the curry filling had a decent flavor as well especially when mixed with the toppings that came with the dish (the mango chutney was my personal favorite). The tequila Jell-O shots were just okay as you didn't taste much of the tequila but were a nice addition to the meal and something new to try outside of the drink menu. For drinks we ordered the Benton old fashioned and Piña Piña Piña which were both refreshing and a great way to end the work week on a Friday evening.

*Most importantly if you are like most people who are unable to secure a reservation ~28 days in advance, I highly recommend arriving prior to opening time (5pm) around 4:20 to secure a reservation on the waitlist. We were able to secure dining outside and were seated within 30 min of opening time!

TL;DR: A sleek family-style Afro-Carib restaurant transforming comfort foods like bodega cookies or goat patties into whimsical fine dining dishes. Very good, but can be hit or miss.  

I was thrilled when I managed to secure a reservation at Tatiana, considering its widespread popularity. The food was indeed very good, but while the flavors were rich, nothing was risque or innovative enough to consider mind-boggling. The prices were also questionable--$30 for 3 dumplings for example. On one hand, sure you are getting an elevated experience, but dumplings from the takeout are just as good (albeit in a different, more homey way). 

Dishes are meant to be shared family-style, recommending 2-3 small plates and 1-2 large plates. Following their suggestion, here's what we ordered:

Egusi Dumplings: Compared to everything else we tried, this dish fell short. The textures were homogeneous and it was incredibly* oily. Voila Afrique would satisfy standard egusi cravings better. I could not finish the dumplings due to the oil. 

Curried Goat Patties: The best thing we tried! As other reviews have noted, these are more akin to empanadas than traditional patties, but the abundance of flavor and the perfect balance of turmeric makes this nothing short of amazing. This is what a high-end goat patty would taste like for sure. 

Braised Oxtails: As someone who frequently indulges in oxtail dishes, I must admit that this was some of the best I've ever had. The oxtails were incredibly tender, nearly falling off the bone, and the stew boasted a delightful blend of sweetness and savoriness. The best value dish we had--comes with a lot of sauce for the super tasty pea rice side.  

Overall, this is an excellent culinary experience for those looking to experience African/Carib cuisine esp. at an elevated angle. Personally, I grew up eating Somali & Trini food and it was amazing to see that professional twist, but I didn't leave super amazed aside from the goat patties.

So I finally got a reservation at a reasonable hour after months of inconsistent trying. We waited about five minutes for our table to be ready. All the plates are shareables. It was a Wednesday night and the vibe was nice, good music playing, upbeat crowd not stuffy at all. We enjoyed all our food. It was all really savory and hearty and we ended up having to take a doggy bag home. My favorite might have been the goat Patties. But I definitely would like to go back and try more of the menu. I was STUFFED.  The chicken shawarma was so good. I rarely order chicken at restaurants because: boring. But it was so juicy and tender. Amazing with a lovely savory lamb rice. The owner Kwame was present and talking with most of the tables and told us 'Welcome Home' which really resonated with my partner. I would definitely come back and bring others!

My only one tip is to customize your doggy bag or maybe add a sticker so that when guests leave they are a walking advertisement. But I know this place doesn't need any extra promotion but still worth mentioning.

I'm sorry but for such a high price point the food was not good. 

To begin I'll start with the positive. Now food aside, the environment is great and the wait staff is incredibly attentive. 

Now for the food? Much to be desired. My friend and I went on a Friday night and ordered the following:

-curry goat patties (3/5) 

-egusi dumplings (3/5)

-peri peri salad (4/5) tbh the best thing we had all evening

-hamachi escovitch (1/5) the flavor was good but when I order escovitch I'm not expecting sashimi. 

-oxtail (1/5) this was the WORST oxtail I've ever had in my life. It was over $50 for 4 pieces of meat that was incredibly burnt and UNDER SEASONED. As a proud Jamaican-American, this oxtail would make my God-fearing grandmother curse up a storm. 

-cosmic brownie and ice cream (2/5) cute concept but $18 for a cosmic brownie is WILD

The jelly shots to begin were cute. For a $300 bill (tip included) the food could have and should have been much better.

Worth the hype. Service was so lovely thank you Monique and Kaydene for your warm welcome and service. The goat Pattie's (empanadas) and humous were fabulous. But the piece de la resistance was the shrimp entree. They give you 2 pieces of shrimp that were the size of 2 mini lobsters and just as flavorful. A fantastic night all in all.

Tatiana has mastered the elements of a superb restaurant from the flavorful food, excellent customer service and awe-inspiring atmosphere.  I loved everything about this establishment and my experience.

There is a reason this is the best restaurant in NYC and it comes down to the incredible food. I will say, our server was fantastic, and the chic interior was great, and you really can't beat the location. The drinks were good - my negroni was a great execution and I really enjoyed. BUT OMG THE FOOD. Had some inside knowledge from the soux chef and glad we took the recs: Mamas Shrimp and the Lamb Hummus were out of this world!! The lamb humus was made with black beans and it was such a savory and tasty dish with the right amount of spice. I could've eaten 4 plates of that dish. The haddock with the corn bread was outstanding as well. Loved the sauce it came with and the fish was perfectly cooked. Those massive prawns with Mama's shrimp was just amazing. The curry wasnt crazy spicy but had such a delicious tang and we were practically licking it off the plate. The prawns were HUGE and SO meaty. This place really is something special and get ready to split some dishes! Honestly, the price wasn't crazy or expected so feel free to spend a little to get one of the best meals around and certainly the best meal I've had this year.
I enjoyed the food, ambience and service. The decor is amazing. I had the curried goat patties, oxtail Rangoon, black bean hummus. All delicious. The dessert was great as well. Highly recommend!!!

Welcome home.

Tbh, felt underdressed and out of place when I first stepped into the chic, upscale interiors of Tatiana. But despite the gold heavy-set utensils, the cool vibes with R&B playing in the background felt home-y to me. 

A homage to Chef Kwame's sister, Tatiana by Kwame Onwuachi is the blended experience of Chef's childhood and prestigious training background. Ordered half the menu, and there wasn't a single miss. The flavor profiles are rich, powerful, and spicy... just the way I like it! It's no wonder everyone raves about this place from Pete Wells to the James Beard Foundation. The restaurant just received accolades at the recent Worlds 50 Best Restaurants awards for the "Resy One to Watch". Honestly, my only gripe was I wish I had more bread, rice, roti to scoop up all the chutney, puree, and sauce on those plates! 

Highly recommend a visit, even if you have to wait in line before open because reservations are impossible to get! Can't wait to visit home again...

Worth all the hype! Very pricey for the portion size but completely worth it. Every dish is delicious and executed to perfection. The presentation is innovative and edgy. The service is top tier and the crowd is chill. If you can get a reservation, go!

Mom Duke's Shrimp is one of the best food items I have ever eaten in my life. The flavors of the sauce are so complex and deliciously savory. It is a must order. The wagyu pastrami was good, but forgettable. Skip the caesar salad and beef patties. The weak link here is definitely the service. Staff was friendly, but did not seem knowledgeable about what they were serving when presenting dishes.

Every aspect of our dinner at Tatiana was delightful and memorable. We had different food preferences and needs within our party (vegetarian, vegan, shellfish allergy) and our waitress guided us through selecting sharable dishes that would be appropriate and combine well to tease our palates. Her service was fun and engaging. The food was unique, with great attention to flavor and texture. The presentation and color of the food on the dark crockery was beautiful. The wine and cocktails felt generous and tasty. Attention to detail was impeccable, down to the soap in the restroom which was decadent. Thank you for a memorable experience.

Impossible hype and yet still very much worth it and more. First visit, we ordered way too much food (we were both uncomfortable after) but every bite was outstanding. We got the goat patties, the egusi dumplings, the okra, the black bean hummus, the shrimp, the oxtail, and the bodega special for dessert, and yet there were still so many items that I still want to try. 

I honestly don't know how we would choose what to sub out next time (every single item was outstanding), other than the dessert, which was great, but I'd love to try the white chocolate cheesecake next time.

I finally got a reservation at Tatiana. The place is way over hyped. The best dish was the black hummus...the only dish that's not overly sweet. The crispy okra was so sweet like sweet and sour chicken from a bad Chinese Takeout. While the oxtail was super tender, it too had a heavy sweet taste. Brown sauce Bronzino was decent. 
My Tatiana tonic was good but nothing special that would bear the Name. 

At these prices, I expected much better.
There are a lot of other places in Nyc to get better Oxtails.

Excellent playlist...Afrobeat R & B Playlist

I waited months to get this reservation. Everyone has been raving about how amazing the food is and I just knew I had to try it, only to to be disappointed. I went with a friend for dinner on a Friday night and was first shocked how small the restaurant is. The furniture and aesthetics were so blah. My drink was actually really good, but my friend did not feel the same about hers. The waiter took forever to take our order and still ended up getting it wrong. The curry goat patties were just ok and they were oily. The oxtail and crab Rangoon did not give what it was supposed to give at all. The oxtail was gammy which was surprising and lacked seasoning but wasn't terrible. The chicken was a 7 out of 10. Overall, we were dissatisfied, but maybe it's just our palette. I don't think it was worth the hype or the wait honestly.

I personally heard about this restaurant through my homegirl who wanted to check it out the reservations are hard to come by. We walked in on a Monday about 8 and the place was indeed packed so I can see how reservations are hard to get. By chance 2 seats at the bar opened up and we just so happened to be there . It is located in the Lincoln center and has signs around to help guide you which was nice. The restaurant itself is really nice and well put together, loved the decor. The bartenders were very nice especially Pierre! He was so fun and a great person to speak with. Now onto the food , we ordered so much food ! I'm glad we ordered in the way we did because as we went down the scale. The curried goat Pattie's were so GOOD ! Omg ! Loved it , the dumplings were amazing ! The large share chicken was amazingggg ! But the lamb rice was a little on the sweet side for me.
