The oxtail large share I wasn't a fan of the flavor it was missing that real oxtail flavor but the pieces you got were amazing in cut and great meat , it was fall off the bone, I just wish it had more of that oxtail seasoning, and less broiled, but the rice and peas it came with was to die for! Then to finish we ordered the large share was the short rib pastrami and I thought it would have been more served whole and can use our forks to shred it but it was served sliced as steak and just didn't make much sense with the bread and we didn't eat more than a tasting bite. Over all there are so many amazing things on the menu. We spent about 350$ but keep in mind the plates are meant to share so you can order less food than we did and be full, everything was just well described on the menu so we had to try lol. Overall I say check it out and go during the week for bar seating

Everything was delicious and I feel so fortunate that I got the opportunity to eat here. 

I couldn't get a reservation for the life of me, so I went to line at at 3:50, and there was already someone in front of me. I brought me a book, and sat down and waited, knowing that my place in line was secured. With such a long waiting time, the camaraderie between the first few people was palpable, so much so that, me and the guy behind me decided to share our dining experience and split the check!!! So I got the opportunity to try twice as many dishes as expected. 

The service was excellent, and I loved that they did not discriminate based on appearence and dress (cuz I showed up casual af).

The food was amazing! Everything was amazing. I did not have not one bad dish! I would have never ordered the piri piri salad myself, but so glad that I did. It was so good, that we had to order an additional side of roti to sop of the residual juices! 

And y'all that roti! Sooooo delicious! It's absolutely warm, buttery, flakey with the perfect amount of salt rocks. Just divine!

Both the curry snow crab and the mom dukes shrimp had me also scrubbing the plate with roti. Every single morsel was gobbled up. Each dish was plate licking good, and I'm not exagerating. 

The desert wasn't any less spectacular. We got the bodgea special which was so such an elegant twist on one of my childhood  favorites. That brownie was absolitely sinful. Rich, thick, chocolately, fudgey and completely decadent.

I can't rave enough about how much I enjoyed my time, and hope to come back soon.

After a few attempts at trying to get a reservation, I ended up snagging a 5pm one on a Thursday. However, if you find yourself struggling to book a table, you might be able to walk-in if you arrive right when it opens. There were a few parties that were able to be seated. 

Started with a Tatiana tonic which was light and refreshing. Sweet but not overly sweet. A good accompaniment to the dinner, especially on a hot day. Egusi dumplings were okay. I didn't think they were too special. The amount of filling is good, but there wasn't a prominent crab flavor. Definitely get the curried goat patties. The mango chutney was such a great pairing to it. It didn't taste too gamy either. The aioli was very mild. The meal came with a house made habanero sauce which was extremely spicy. The waitress was right telling us a little goes a long way for it. 

The cornbread and cod was my favorite thing on the menu. The cornbread was moist, had a crispy grilled crust, and was super buttery. Probably the best bite of the night for me. The cod melted in your mouth. The buttermilk soubise was creamy. A good balance of sweet and savory, crunchy and soft. Tatiana is renowned for the short rib pastrami suya, but I wasn't amazed by it. The texture really reminded me of pastrami, but I missed eating the tenderness of wagyu. It shredded like pastrami and had a really good crust, but it wasn't for me. The caraway coco bread was like a parker roll but insanely better. 

The bodega special would be nostalgic if I grew up on the desserts they were based off of. However, because I didn't it was just underwhelming. The appearance of the brownie was very much like the brownies you can find in Kid Cuisines. Although it was moist, in the end, it was just chocolate cake to me. Powered donut ice cream, really was a powdered donut. The ice cream itself had a texture like a donut and the exterior coating was a bit hard. An elevated powdered donut, which I didn't really care for. 

The inside is decorated beautifully. I was sat in an area with dimmer lighting, but the front of the restaurant has a good amount of natural lighting perfect for photos. They recommend dressing smart casual, but they won't turn you away if you dress casually. I saw a few people in casual attire. 

Tatiana was good, but I wasn't blown away by the meal especially after hearing so many praises.
The food was absolutely delicious. The service is unmatched. It had a great vibe and great music. I'll definitely be back.

I'd try everyday to get a reservation here until I could get one! The NYTimes knew what they were doing when they ranked Tatiana as #1!! The oxtail & crab Rangoons are a must try, so crispy & full of flavor with a little kick of spice. The pastrami was quite literally the best I've ever had. It was incredibly seasoned, so tender & the pickled onions were perfect to create your own little slider using the buns. The buns were the perfect addition as well. The shrimp are HUGE, the creole sauce was so delicious with salty notes. Now the dessert!!! The cosmic brownie was the perfect balance of moist, not too dense & warm chocolate on top. It was the most elevated kind of cosmic brownie and tasted 100/10. I've been raving for weeks about the powdered donut ice cream that yes, also looks like a donut! The ice cream tastes EXACTLY like a powdered donut in the bag from the bodega, down to the aromas in your mouth after you finish. It was delectable. Service was incredible, helped us choose what to order & gave us some back story into the dishes and the ambiance was great. The restaurant was absolutely stunning!!

I could not get a reservation so we decided to stand in line at 4:20pm. There were three people ahead of us in the line on this rainy evening. We were able to secure seats at the bar. The bar only has 6 seats. To my surprise the bar seating was very comfortable. I ordered the Tatiana tonic ( very refreshing). Next the curried goat Patties( devoured them 10/10). Then we ordered the branzino and cod /corn bread dishes. Both options were good. The branzino was a larger portion size than the cod. For dessert we ordered the bodega brownie. I will definitely visit again and will do my best to try to get a reservation so I can enjoy sitting In the main restaurant area.

Upscale restaurant with an eclectic menu inside the Lincoln Plaza. I'm assuming this spot will receive a Michelin star once they've been around long enough. 

Restaurant is beautifully elegant. Tables have gorgeous countertops. Seats were large and comfy. Small yet sleek bar. There were two gender neutral restrooms. One was handicap accessible and had a changing tables. Even given the conveniences, it was one of the most romantic restrooms with its dim lighting and lovely aroma.

We were fortunate to grab a table for four as walk ins on a Saturday night. I'd recommend going with a similar sized group so that you could share as many items. Most items are meant to be shared for three people, so I'd recommend coming as a group of three or six. 

We ordered four small plates, four large plates, desserts, and drinks. It came out to approximately $115 per person before accounting for tip. I thought it was surprisingly reasonable given the atmosphere, location, and that it adds up to a nine course meal plus drinks. 

Service was super attentive. Water glasses were consistently refilled. Our waitress come around frequently to check up on us and see if we needed anything. She was very bubbly and I'm glad her personality came through which is indicative of a good work culture. She also made some helpful recommendations. 

Food was superb. We started with the curried goat patties. Not only were they the most expensive patties that I've had but they were also the best I can remember having. Filling was great but the dough was phenomenal. Hot and crispy. More similar to a fresh empanada than to the flakier style of pastry that I typical associate with a patty. Parties are a must order.

Next were the dumplings. They were a gyoza style dumpling with a mildly spicy sauce. They had a nice crisp to them and a delicious filling.

We also had the crispy okra and the black bean hummus. I believe okra was seared in a pan or stove top and had a sweet glaze to it. I dipped a few pieces in their house hot sauce which added a little zing to it. Hummus has minced lamb in it and was on the savory side. 

First large plate that was served was the braised oxtail. Meat was tender and fell off the bone without being over cooked or mushy. Perfect cook time. Came in a sweet sauce with carrots, squash, and a side of rice and peas. Rice and peas were on point. I've been working on my own rice and pea dish, so the chef's provides some great inspiration to me. Great dish but NYC has some fantastic Caribbean spots where you could find a similar caliber dish for a quarter of the price. 

Next came the curried snow crab. This was my favorite dish and another must order. Crab was cooked on point and already pre-cracked making it super easy to eat. This was served with roti. The curry and roti were outstanding. I ended up ordering seconds of roti to completely mop up every bit of curry. Curry was rich and flavorful with a thick gravy texture. Anything would have been delicious in the curry.

Up next we're the takeout mushrooms. These were massive (I believe Honshimeji) mushrooms served in a sweet sauce along with nuts. These giant mushrooms were ultra juicy. Would love to see them utilized more often as a meat substitute given how meaty and juicy they were. Shrooms were served alongside scallion pancakes. Pancakes were thin and extra crispy. Nice saltiness to them.

Last main course, was the wagyu pastrami. Also one of my favorites of the evening. It's ultra fatty cut but it's rendered so nicely. Maybe not great for my cholesterol but it was delicious. Super savory. Bold seasoning as expected with pastrami. They came with smaller Parker house style bread rolls and some sautéed red cabbage. I made a mini sandwich topped with their house made Russian dressing. Absolutely glorious bite. 

I was beyond stuffed but my group insisted on dessert. They selected the bodega special high was a cosmic little Debbie style brownie with what I believe to be a powdered doughnut inspired ring of coconut ice cream. Fun and nostalgic finish to a tremendous meal.

Tatiana deserves all the hype and accolades that they've received (and will receive). Love that the menu draws on many different cuisines and experiences. Love the hospitality. Love that it's a fine dining experience that leaves you full and , most importantly, happy.

The food is good, but it's hard not to make good food with these flavor profiles. If you had decent Indian food and/or Thai food, the flavors here do not deviate too far. In short, dipping roti into good coconut based curry means just good eating.

I had a few of the appetizers like the goat patties and dumplings. They were not bad but not great. Again, it's hard to make this type of flavor profiles not work.

The mains of pastrami and snow crabs were better. Pastrami is their signature dish, and the tender slices of beef do justify that status. The sauce was also unique. This was the highlight of the meal. Snowcrab is not bad, but the curry based sauce is the star of the dish.

Now on to the finer aspects of the meal: service. It's not good at all. If the main large plates require use of hands (unavoidable since you make your own sandwiches or dip the pieces of roti into the curry) any competent high-end restaurant would serve a wet towel before and after the meal. Obviously, this place doesn't.

There is no wiping down of the tables, though there are pieces of roti or sauce on it. Wines are served in wrong glasses for the type. If you order another glass of the same type of wine, it's poured in the same glass. While that's not a big deal, if you are sensitive to different flavors, you want the change of glasses. And I assure you some of these dishes are heavily spiced and flavored, so you might want to switch glasses between courses.

The service is also very slow. For instance, the meal lasted 2 hrs total for my party, and the timeline went like this. Apps about 25 mins after sitting down. Mains another 30 mins or so after finishing the apps. The final main is another 30 mins after the second main. 

Overall apps are aprund $20 to 28 and mains are around 50 to 85. Having said that, you'd expect seemless and professional service throughout. It's obvious the chef knows his ingredients but not the customer base and the front end of restaurant management.

No wine list. Mediocre drinks. All in all this is a professional chef not a restaurateur running the place. Won't go back.

If you can score a reservation here it's worth the visit! 

Highlights:
- goat patties 
- oxtail 
- crab curry 

Wine selection was great. We also tried the black bean hummus with the lamb as well as the shrimp dumplings. Both were good apps but not as strong as the other dishes. 

The ambiance and music gives lounge vibes and all the wait staff were funny and nice.

Delicious food and great ambiance. 
Unique Caribbean food in the heart of Lincoln Center. Great service too!
The food and cocktails were delicious, the service was impressive and the ambiance was amazing. I will definitely be back!

Top notch meals and service. Would definitely recommend. The vibe was nice for a 5pm dinner - not too loud, not too quiet. Our server, Neo, was the best. Super attentive and nice. Helped us answer any questions we had!! Will definitely be returning!!!

The food is 10/10 as you would expect and more. The food was exceptional and everything was cooked to perfection! Unfortunately, The service was horrendous. It definitely left a bad taste in my mouth after waiting over a month for the reservation and spending over $800. I will start off with mentioning that we waited over 46 minuets to just sit down,  although we had a reservation for 8pm and we arrived 15 minutes prior the reservation. After we waited the host mentioned they unfortunately made a mistake and if it's ok to sit in the outside patio ( we didn't have an issue with that part).  Once seated, the host mentioned that we have a 2 hour limit and that it's only 2 hours. The waitress was the icing on the cake though, she  never mentioned her name and gave us attitude the whole night. I honestly don't understand how you have a service job and can't even be nice nonetheless say her name. She never checked if we were ok through out the dining experience. She ended service by mentioning the tip was included in the bill as if we didn't already know that. I would have loved to tell her a life tip and to be nicer than actual to  tip due to lack of service ( We did leave her 18% tip and that was way to much in my opinion due to lack of service). She literally didn't even say bye or thank you for coming.The ambience was honestly not same as the inside and it wasn't a vibe. This place got the 4 stars due to the food but the service is the true definition of trash !

Came with no expectations.
I don't care for celebrity chefs and winners 
Of "who the F**k care" food network show .
I care for great food , service and if the place is happening it's a nice extra .
The food was very good specifically very nice done fried branzino ,real impressive.
The chicken was flavorable and tender and those (for both entrees) rice with beans sides were excellent and you want to add that fantastic hot sauce (which eventually they will sell at fine groceries around the country) 
The hummus texture was good though I wasn't impressed with the taste , chickpeas (nothing else) are for hummus . Period .
Excellent desert with the chocolate covered cheese cake with caramel.
Fantastic service and very cool space that even with big celebrated table next to us (probably due very rare great acoustic - after all it's Lincoln Center....:) it was pleasure to sit and have food conversation.

Highly recommended!!!!

Definitely A destination!!!!

Absolutely delicious with an ambiance to match. The waitstaff was knowledgeable and attentive. Chef Kwame even came over and introduced himself to us, which I thought was a special touch to the evening. This is fine dining, a place to go for a special occasion. This is not the type of place you come to more than once or twice per year. If I can snag a reservation again sometime in the future - I'll absolutely return.

This place is great - Atmosphere is chill and cool but the staff is also really knowledgeable about their menus. They know what they're doing and what they're talking about, and you can tell making the customers happy is main priority. When Kwame is around the restaurant he stops by to interact with guests. 

Our Menu: EGUSI DUMPLINGS, HAMACHI ESCOVITCH, CURRIED GOAT PATTIES, CURRY SNOW CRAB, SHORT RIB PASTRAMI SUYA

Each dish is an array of spices, flavors, and takes on traditional Caribbean and African dishes. Prices are 100% worth it.

Anything less than 5/5 is a lie. You get the experience you've anticipated. Everyone is super friendly. The food is super delicious. The drinks are exactly what you need. This is some of the best food I've had in a long time and I'm very happy to have spent my birthday here. Special mention to how authentic the curry goat patties tasted.

Birthday Tour Dinner #2!

Me being able to snag a reservation here for my birthday was a gift in itself! My friends and I came to Tatiana on a cool Saturday summer night. Upon arrival we checked in with the hostess and moved over to the bar area as we awaited the rest of our party. The entire party must be present in order to be seated. 

I loved the vibe here.... Dim lighting, gorgeous light fixtures, bomb playlist, indoor and outdoor seating AND strong drinks! We started off with champagne for a bday toast then moved on to cocktails once the rest of my party arrived and we were seated. 

Our waitress was an absolute pleasure. Giving several recommendations for food and drinks. We decided to order a spread to share. We had plaintains, dumplings, fried okra, oxtails, brown stew branzino and curry snow crab. The showstopper for me was the curry crab BUT everything was good. Drinks were flowing for the entire night, the playlist was spot on and had us singing along. 

When we were done the waitress gave me a strawberry shortcake and the girls sang happy birthday to me. We really had an amazing night! Fingers crossed I can snag another reservation soon.

Mmm Mmm 
Mmm is all kept saying because I finally got a reservations to Chef Kwame's Tatiana's restaurant in NYC. The ambiance is absolutely beautiful ! We kicked it off  with drinks . We got the POG Nutcracker and the Spicy Margarita. We then jumped into sharable small plates &  we got the crispy okra which was seasoned to perfection , egusi dumplings & let me say that crab and red stew was delicious & I had never heard of oxtail crab Rangoon , but it was unique and so delicious. Now we shared our large plate & approve of the oxtails. They get a 10/10. 

The flavors in all dishes came together perfectly & are a Perfect example of chef Kwame using his Afro Caribbean influences on traditional dishes nailing it . This place was Amazing ! 

If you're in NYC & get a reservation it is definitely worth it!

This is based off of 2 visits, and one non-visit. The food is good to great. The cocktails are solid if not spectacular. The vegetarian options are basically non-existent, and the one veggie main they have (takeout mushrooms) is bar-none the worst thing on their menu, and they shouldn't be serving it. 
Is it worth going here? Sure, if you have a reservation. Don't wait for it though. That basically covers my first two visits. 

My non-visit, consists of me not having a reservation. I rocked up at around 8 on a Wednesday night and honestly didn't expect to be seated. It's close to my place however and didn't require a train journey, so I thought I might as well check it out before heading to a further destination. Well, what do you know? I put my name in, and they said they'll have a bar seat around 9:30. Fantastic! They have a cocktail garden where you can have a drink, and I figured I could easily kill one and a 1/2 hours. Long story short, I def killed those hours, annnnnd never got a seat. The restaurant closes at 10 so I never made it off the waitlist. Listen, if you have a waitlist, then you need to be up front and tell people they have no chance of getting in that night or that it's very low likelihood. Don't tell people the wait is an hour and a half and "we'll text you." I wasted an entire night and could have gone elsewhere easily. And I wouldn't have held it against them! Great that you're popular! Now figure out how to manage that popularity and don't mess people around.
I went there for my birthday & loved it. Since his days on Project Runway, I have been a fan of Chef Kwame

I came here a while back and I still remember the meal. So first this place is delicious and worth all the attention it is receiving. I loved my meal, the restaurant, the service and the playlist. I want to go back and I am going to make it my business to go back before the year ends. So let's get to the food, first we ordered three appetizers the Hamachi Escovitch, the goat patties and the wontons. So my favorite was the Hamachi Escovitch which was a special that day.  The Hamachi was fresh and the carrot nage added a wonderful flavor to this dish. I was informed they have a lot of returners so they make specials to offer variety. I was disappointed they didn't have the chopped cheese I wanted. The goat patties' dough was very fresh and soft. The sauce that comes with the patty was so good, we kept it. The wontons were good. My main course was the curry crab legs and I loved it. I did order extra roti because the sauce was so good. My favorite part of the dish was the crab legs were already cut so I did not have to work to get the crab meat out. The roti was the right thickness and texture. My friend ordered the oxtails and that was very good. We also ordered the okra wow that dish was so good, it was crispy yet it had a taste of citrus. The okra is a must try, I still think about that okra. For dessert we ordered the brownie and ice cream. The ice cream was really good and I liked the flavor and creaminess of it. I did have three drinks and my favorite was the Pina Pina. The service was amazing we were never rushed and she was very nice. Also the amount of detail makes this restaurant a must visit. All the employees were in sync they all were friendly and I loved it. Now I like to go to all types of restaurants but this restaurant was my favorite because the music was great and it was lively. The volume of the music was just right, I did not have to yell to communicate with my friend. Some restaurants of this level are unwelcoming but this place was different the food, the employees and the music were all great. I felt like I belonged and it was wonderful and the manager is very friendly she came to ask us about our meal. This is a great place to go and I look forward to going back. We did not make reservations but we waited outside before it opened, it was only two of us and it was raining.

Worth it just for the experience! 

 I would say that the food is overhyped but it is decent and served family style. I am not sure if it lives up to the hype. 

We found the dessert to be way too sweet. The best thing was the hot sauce, they should bottle it up and sell it. 

The service is top notch and the restaurant ambience is amazing.
Amazing everything is amazing  The ambience, the food, the drinks, and the music was top tier!!! Can't wait to try the nightlife!!!

I'm not a professional food critic but I got some things to say!

- overall innovative dining experience based on Afro Caribbean staples with an homage to nyc 
-  main dishes are the main attractions ! Short rib and Branzino can't miss - the coconut rice and peas was killer! Order anything here that calls to you and go lighter on the apps 
-  the Patties, Rangoons, and dumplings are all a bit too similar so don't order them all at once 
- appetizer plating could be improved, something about the tiny plates had me feeling jacked 
- desserts are a no for me
- tea was a definite yes 
- cocktails were flavorful and fun 
- please turn the ac down

xx

The food was worth the wait. This restaurant had the best food selection. The pastrami and oxtails were delicious the drinks were so delicious.  The service was great. The ambiance was beautiful right inside of the Lincoln center.

The food, staff, & service were exceptional! The drinks, appetizers, & entrees were absolutely delicious. I've dined there several times and it gets better every time. Your time, money, & energy spent here will definitely be worth it!

A disappointing place esp for NYC,  which had the most astounding restaurants, in the world, next to Paris. 
The menu " c'est non intéressant "  rarely  worthwhile but it's a typical fad place. 
I'll save my $ for the greats without the Hollywood riffraff.
Addendum : Can anyone play some decent music understated and sublime during dining? 
This is a time to relax. It is Lincoln Center after all. Please consult a Marsalis and keep us posted on the improvements. Has potential.

Fantastic food! I'd give it 3.5 if I could. Not sure if it lives up to the hype as a whole, but the food was delicious. I had been trying to get a reservation for a while and got lucky. A day later, they called me saying they had a private event scheduled for the day I had booked and needed to change my reservation. Luckily, there were no issues finding a new date/time based on their availability. There are 6 seats at the bar for walk ins, but I would get there right when it opens to try to snag one of those. 

We were seated in the main dining room which was dimly lit and had a great playlist. They also have outdoor seating and a private dining room for parties/corporate gatherings. We were quickly greeted by our waitress who explained that the restaurant was family style and recommended two small plates and two large plates for two people. 

We ordered the goat patties and dumplings for an app. When they arrived, there were 3 patties and 3 dumplings on the plate so I would consider this more tapas style, NOT family style. I'm Italian and family style in my mind is large portions for everyone to share and get more than one item on the plate. We ordered the oxtail and the crab dish for entrees. Skip the crab dish; while the crab was pre cracked and made it easy to eat, they only gave you one piece of roti to soak up the curry. The oxtail was the highlight for us; fell off the bone and was tasty! 

The service was average and inconsistent throughout the meal. I think if they are trying to go for a Michelin star, this is the area they need to significantly improve on! Our food took a while to come out at 9pm on a Friday evening. We were there for over two hours, not by choice (and there's a two hour table limit which the waitress reminded us when we sat down). The bus staff would clear our plates without asking if we were finished and would just reach across the table as we were eating. 

Overall, I'm glad I went and tried it but I'm not sure if I'd be back or recommend it. Prices are high for the amount of food that you get. The food is good but the service doesn't live up to a fine dining experience. And it's definitely not family style!!

Without question- the BEST meal I had while visiting NYC.  

This is the only restaurant I wanted to check out while in the city. I attempted to make a reservation 2 weeks in advance with no luck.  

Reservation information: 
1. Reservations are through Resy 
2. Reservations  via Resy are for parties of 6 or less if you have more than 6 in your party you will need to e-mail the restaurant at the following address:  info@tatiananyc.com. 
3. Reservations are available 28 days in advance at 12pm. ( I really don't understand this rule and have not tried it out. However, tomorrow is 09/15 so I assume at 12pm tomorrow  you can make a reservation for 11/12). 

Since I did not follow the reservation instructions I  told myself that I would arrive when they opened at 5pm and hope to get one of the 6 seats at the bar. When I walked up about 20 minutes prior to opening there was already a line forming. There were approximately 8-10 people in front of me!!! How could I let this happen???! Lol . I struck up a conversation with the young lady in front  of me who said  she was actually trying to secure reservations for a party of 6 for the following day! This was great news! One less person in front of me! !  As we waited in line ( it was raining) the staff walked around and offered everyone in line a fresh juice. I don't recall what they told us it was, but it was very tasty!  At around 4:50pm a staff came around and took names and obtain phone numbers to put us on the waitlist. I was 1 of 2 in my party. The staff advised it would take about 30 minutes.  We went next door and sat down to wait for our table. I received a text at around 5:20 pm that our table was ready! 

I have to say that my impression of this spot started in the line. The nice gesture of the complimentary drink as well as the friendly demeanor of the staff had a positive impact on my first impression. 

When we were seated our wait staff came over to greet us! She also had an amazing personality and provided recommendable customer service! She provided me with a solid mock-tail suggestion and even went over the menu in detail. She suggested we order to small  bites and 2 large bites and share everything.

We ended up ordering the okra from the small bites and the oxtails and branzino. The okra came out first. Let me tell you, the flavor of this okra is the best I have ever had. There is indeed a secret mix of seasonings that are working!! LOVED this dish at first bite! I I don't eat red meat, but  when the oxtails came out they smelled and looked amazing that I had to take a bite!-- the flavor was out of this world!! Everything was cooked to perfection. The last dish was the branzino. It had an interesting flavor and  being serviced with the rice was  an interesting combo, but it worked. When I tell you we left nothing on our plates! This food was so good! My only regret is that I did not leave room for dessert.

I would describe the ambiance as modern and sexy! They had low lighting and a beautiful cloud light feature at the center of the restaurant they also have patio seating for when the weather is nice! 

This restaurant exceeded my expectations. Please note this was not an inexpensive meal.  For the okra, oxtails, branzino and 1 mock-tail the total was $154 prior to the tip.  However, I would say it was worth every penny!  I would return to this restaurant on my next trip to NYC! Hopefully next time I can  secure a reservation in advance!

This place was expensive and I expected more from the reviews and hype around the restaurant. We have a reservation on a Friday night and sat within 5 minutes of checking in. I was expecting a fine dining experience but the hostess and waiting staff had different uniforms on and dirty sneakers on. That didn't bother me too much as that's more an aesthetics thing.

The waitress advised us that this is "family style" but I would disagree with that 100%. The portions were small which is the complete opposite of family style. We ordered the dumplings and goat empanada/patty. There were 3 of each which is hard to share as a party of 2. They were good but 3 dumplings was $21. 

We then ordered the crab curry and oxtail. The crab curry was good but only gave a single piece of roti/bread to eat the curry. There were a few pieces of crab on top that was pre cracked. The oxtail was delicious and fall off the bone. By far the best dish of the night. It took about 45 minutes for the appetizers to come out. 

I ordered the maple bacon old fashion. It was very Smokey and didn't get any taste of bacon. 

The service was a disappointment. The staff would come around and start clearing plates without asking if you were done. At one point a staff member came to remove a plate and reached over and his arm nearly hit me and my fork which had food on it. It was unpleasant and made us feel rushed. 

Overall the food tasted good but overpriced and the service was disappointing. I don't think I would return here.

Tatiana is a beautiful restaurant located right in Lincoln Center. The reservations are hard to come by unless you are a pro at using Resy, typically the only openings that can be found no matter how quick you are, are around 5 PM or 9 PM.
I was lucky to snag a reservation on my mom's birthday. When we let the server know that it was her birthday, he very graciously brought us two glasses of champagne. He was very nice and knowledgeable, every employee who we encountered there was great. 

I'm no stranger to overpriced Manhattan food, but Tatiana takes this to a new level. The crab dumplings were alright, nothing to rave about, and definitely not worth $7 a piece - $21 for 3 dumplings is insane, but that is the theme of my experience at Tatiana.
The jerk cod was a teeny tiny portion and was underseasoned. It came with a couple little squares of cornbread, which were very good. I don't see this item on the menu anymore so it must not have gotten good feedback.
The large cast-iron pot holding our oxtail came out and I was excited about the large portion awaiting us inside of that pot, but it held three sizable pieces of oxtail and a couple bits of carrot. I wish they'd present it in a smaller pot so that we didn't get our hopes up. The oxtail were cooked perfectly and were delicious, though a tad on the sweeter side.
For dessert, we got the bodega special, which was a brownie and ice cream shaped like a powdered doughnut. This was the most underwhelming part of our meal.
We each ordered a drink, can't remember the names, but we were both happy with them.

Aside from the vibe and the service, the highlight was the homemade pepper sauce, they said it was made to go with everything on the menu, and it definitely did not disappoint. If they bottled that, I'd buy it!
I hear great things about the goat patties, I can only picture myself going back to Tatiana to grab a seat at the bar and give those a try.

*** food is 4/5 stars. Initial front house service was basically 2 stars - TLDR: poor table management, overbooked, had a 9:30 res but got seated at 10:10 even though we arrived on time*** 

BUT the food is fantastic however and would love to go back with a larger group to try more of the menu! 

Ambiance+Service: so we had a 9:30 reservation, we got there at 9:30, but weren't seated until 10:10 since they told us they overbooked. That is INSANE because I would never normally wait 30min+ if I didn't have a res - and now I'm waiting 40+ even though i expected to be seated around 9:30? I also expected a refreshment or something complimentary after 20min or so to "acknowledge and apologize" for the longer than necessary wait butttt nope we just kept waiting. Service while we were seated was fantastic however, great server and super friendly. Love the blue/purpleish modern deco - it does feel kind of clubby. 

Food: 
Snow crab [5/5]: fantasticcc - the curry was so creamy and has quite a kick to it (kind of reminds me of butter chicken but elevated). Roti was flakey and buttery.

Egusi dumplings [4/5]: came out piping hot so be careful :p - the red stew was very good kind of smokey, tomatoey, goodness. 

Wagyu pastrami [5/5]: fatty and tender as it should be! The dinner rolls were super soft, fluffy, and butter I honestly wish they gave more bread to cover all the meat. The cabbage added needed acidity to cut through all of the fat and the sauce was to die for. The powdered chili on the side realllly tasted like shin ramen (that's a compliment LOL) and was super additive

Bodega brownie [4/5]: texture and taste of the doughnut was super unexpected - tasted like apple cider with a hint of oatmilk. Thought it paired nicely with the warm brownie. I'm not a huge chocolate fan so I thought the brownie was a bit heavy - but for all chocolate lovers - it is super decadent and os basically an artisanal cosmic brownie

I had the most Amazing Experience at Tatiana!! I watched the Today Show in July, and Kwame Onwuachi was on the show. I knew I had to try Tatiana after watching his segment.
I tried getting Reservations, but that proved to be a challenge, so I decided I would wait in line on a Thursday, Aug 31, to be exact. I got in line around 4:00/4:15 pm. There were about 20 people ahead of me, but luckily I was able to secure a seat at the bar.
I felt so lucky! From the Front of House Staff to the Bartender, wow what a Transformational Service experience.
My Drink was Amazing and the Food was Even better. I ordered the Curried Goat Patties as my appetizer (Wow, the flavors and the crispiness) and the Brown Stew Branzino (So good). I was so stuffed I couldn't even order dessert. The dessert choices sounded really good. I can't wait to come back and bring family/friends with me on this once-in-a-lifetime culinary journey, that is Tatiana!

Overall rating: 4.49-4.8 (I'm very torn)

Oh, Tatiana, Tatiana, Tatiana. I will try my hardest to keep this succinct because I have a lot of emotion writing this review. 

After what felt like months and months, weeks and weeks & setting MANY timers to get a reservation - it never worked out. I was ready to call it a day until my friend said they were okay with just trying to walk-in when it opened. 

I want to say while I had absolutely amazing food, I don't recommend trying to walk-in if you have night plans. This is an all-night occasion. For a 5pm opening, I arrived around 4:35. I know you see that video, there were already 11ish people in front of me. Fortunately, around 4:45/4:50 a hostess comes out to negotiate. Not really, but that's what it feels like. 

Well let me tell you. The first 3 people, got the last minute canceled tables. The next 5 or so, got the bar. Yes, the bar is small. There is outdoor seating but they recently stopped serving food because the kitchen couldn't keep up. Eye. Roll. Ok. 

Then this wonderful host gets to me and I put my name down on the waitlist. They quote me at around 2ish hours which in hindsight is like 7:30 so that was fine. She gets my number down and that's it. 

I end up waiting for my friend who is on their way and we're just going to go chill at another bar while we wait. But this is important because I saw a few people come after me & those that arrived around 5 - they weren't letting anyone in for the night. The waitlist was closed! 

While I was waiting- I got very anxious because while they took my number, they didn't actually text you to confirm (until you're closer towards the reservation). So 2 hours later and a few martinis at PJ Clark's we decided to do a walk by just to also confirm they have my number correct..

She recognized my face and confirmed she has my number. She couldn't give me a specific ETA but she roughly estimated 30 min to an hour. Fine. We end up going to their outdoor bar which was nice. I think she said there were 3ish people in front of us, I don't remember. 

30 minutes passes by (ps we have now been waiting 2.5 since I arrived) & we're basically drunk and just want someone to be honest with us. Are we staying? Are we going? I go back a second time & bless her heart, she's so nice to me and is quoting 15 or so with 1 table in front of us. Another 20 minutes goes by and we get the text. Woooo! What does that read, another 30 minutes  but at least we have a text!! 

Soon after maybe another 15 or so, we get the text that's it's ready. So what have we learned in this very long form description:
- If you are attempting a walk-in, arrive 45min to an hour before. 
- do not freak out that you didn't get a text after you gave your number. You will get a text. 
- when you check-in, ask their name & try to figure out how many people are in front of you. 

We got seated around 8:45ish which makes this a 4-hour wait.  who have I become?! 

I'm going to tell you right now, my lack of 1-star is not because of this tag game of waiting. No, our waiter was not good. He was good, he wasn't fine-dining, waiting 4 hours good. 

He was terrible at recommending food. And between my friend & I, we split two appetizers, one entree but ordered a second entree. Why? We didn't know that we ordered too much food. We didn't even touch the second entree & I feel like that's something your waiter gives the heads up on. On top of that, the food came out so sporadic. We got 1 appetizer, then an entree, then I had to remind the waiter of our other appetizer for it to then come, then minutes pass and we had to remind him a second time of our second entree. Although we really didn't need it and I shouldn't have said anything. 

Did we close down the place, yes we did. Will I come back here again given my experience? If I know someone with an AmEx card who can easily get a reservation- yes, yes I will. The food was delicious. Absolutely. And a Nigerian restaurant in Lincoln Center is an accomplishment & exciting time to be apart of.  If you have the time, do it.
Absolutely delicious! Literally 10s across the board. My favorite was the crab legs. That sauce could be a soup!

Love the atmosphere and the music selection. It was very easy to get a table despite it being very last minute. The place felt very trendy and the service was unmatched, deserving of all the praise. Our server made us feel very special and the food was great. Love the curry goat patties (and that mango chutney) and the curried snow crab was genuinely out of this world. The Pina Pina Pina was our favorite drink and the white chocolate cheesecake is worth the try.

So let's get right into why I can't come back here, nor would I ask anyone else to come here. 

Service- honestly this is the reason. Only one server made this a very bad experience. The remainder of the individuals were awesome. But our main server literally intentionally ignored me throughout our meal. I was here with two colleagues and they actually noticed it first. I didn't even think it could be a thing because I didn't do anything that would warrant her completely ignoring me. I thought I was very nice to her, but maybe I reminded her of someone after a while because her attitude was just sooo poor to me. She literally avoided looking in my direction when asking questions to a small table of 3, making her issue very noticeable. 

Generally I'm a happy person so someone else's issues wouldn't bother me, but my colleagues noticed and that was embarrassing.  And it got to a point it made them uncomfortable.  Embarrassing a customer for no reason is unacceptable. 

Next, the Food- excellent dishes and creative. I am very familiar with west African food and the chef has put a great spin on foods I grew up eating. We had the dumplings, hummus, Patties and fried okra. Ox tail, fried branzino and chicken shawarma. All amazing, except for the brownie with donut ice cream- don't get this - it was a bitter sweet dark chocolate cake like thing with ice cream hard as a rock shaped like a donut. Aside from this everything was yummy. This amazing menu is one of the reasons I am so sad I can't come back here. 

Drinks- I can't remember exact names (tonic and birthday drinks), but very good as well. 

Ambiance- lovely.

The service and staff are absolutely amazing. They are so friendly and professional and made it a great experience. The restaurant has great music, whoever made that playlist shoutouts to you. The oxtail wasn't anything special to me, probably wouldn't order it again. But the star of the show was the curry goat patties! Them things need to be sold out of a food truck or something. The egosi dumplings were also amazing. I definitely left full and satisfied. They were out of the oxtail Rangoon which was sad.

Finally went to Tatiana after trying to get a reservation for months online. We went 30 mins before they open so we get one of their coveted walk in tables. We sat outside while we waited for our table. The service and the staff were great. Ok, the food. We were 4 and shared a lot of the items on the menu. While the food was definitely good (although oily and heavy), it did not wow me as I expected it would from the reviews and the press. They get 5 stars for marketing/branding and I really believe the strategy of scarcity is deliberate to hype up the restaurant and the chef. Overall I didn't think it was worth all the effort in trying to get in. Do yourself a favor and explore Queens for new and adventurous flavors, you'll save time and money

What a vibe! I came here with no resy back in May, after a buzz had already started but before The World's 50 Best feature. I snagged a seat at the coveted limited bar and had a fabulous meal and time with fellow diners.

Food was very tasty and creative. Vibe and playlist were super cool. Chef was there that night and added to the fun. Also my bill was super reasonable given the quality and sizes of the servings.

Can't wait to be back when I visit NY again.

I've been told it's difficult to get a reservation here but I was luckily able to get a Wednesday night reservation the day before. The staff were really friendly and super helpful when it came to selecting drinks and food. 

The food was absolutely delicious. The sauces that came with the goat patties elevated them. The oxtail was so tender and scrumptious and the curried snow crab was so fulfilling. Some of the best food I've had in New York! The price is high (party of 3 and spent about $100 each including drinks and tip). Is it worth it? I don't really know but I don't regret it. It was a nice little treat! 

I would definitely recommend it for a nicer dinner with friends or on a date. The vibes are elevated casual and the music is good. If you're thinking about trying this place, do it. You won't regret it.

5th time - still some of the best food in New York; and, even better...the service is also at a 5 star level!  The team is crushing it and their GM is really elevating the team and service.  

Top notch - worth a special trip to the city!
OMG - if you can get a reservation make sure you go!!! Probably the best restaurant in nyc right now. The food is incredible, creative and mesmerizing.

As soon as I heard "elevated Afro-Caribbean", I believe I rolled my eyes and walked away from whoever was speaking. Up to this point, the world of fine dining has either ignored African cuisines or whitewashed them--and I wanted no part in that.

But one recent night, I found myself here for dinner thanks to reservations I didn't make. So I figured I'd make the best of the whitewashing and just be happy I got into one of the hottest spots in town. 

I didn't need to try that hard. The Curried Goat Patties were crisp and decadent, while the Black Bean Hummus was bursting with berbere goodness. I didn't care for the too-sweet Braised Oxtails, but the Curried Snow Crab was great for my pescatarian heart. Even the mocktails delivered, though the Pineapple Daiquiri was much, much better than the Passionfruit Orange Guava.

Bottom line: I don't like paying $50-85 for entrees I grew up eating at 1/10th that price. But I do like that the amazing spices, flavors and textures of these cuisines have managed to carry through in an upscale Lincoln Center restaurant--something I've not seen successfully done in most upscale "ethnic" restaurants. I still wouldn't pay that much again, but on pure cooking principle, it's nice to know that a change of price, clientele and scenery doesn't have to compromise taste.

Chef Kwame and his menu gives a unique look into black food and black culture. If you like bougie with a touch of blackness, this is the place you should go. Service was amazing but getting a table was definitely difficult. Ambience is A+.

I really don't want to do this but I just want it to be known that for establishments like this in the mid-high range (it's mid-range to me but I know everyone may not agree), the service starts before you even arrive. If I can't reach your team by phone or email and you're charging $50 for chicken, it's really going to bother me to no end. I called Monday at 5:19 PM to inquire if garden seating was walk-up. The phone rang and then I was transferred to what sounded like a mobile device where the automated message said "This mailbox is full... goodbye". I'm like okay girl. Let me try another extension. Where I waited on hold for 10 minutes listening to music before I hung up and emailed them. It's now Wednesday. I have yet to receive a response even though I went yesterday (Tuesday) and I no longer need this information.

I got there around 4:35 PM because I wasn't sure if the lines were still bussin like back in the Spring. I walked around back to see where I needed to stand and saw they were having a meeting. Came to the front and asked a couple standing around if they were in line for Tatiana's and they said yes, the employees would come around to get us at 4:55 PM. Cool.

At 5:05 PM someone started cleaning the windows and dragging out the sign. At 5:10 PM they opened the door and asked who had resys. They took those people out of the line and came back for the walk-ins a couple of minutes later. We got to the front and I mentioned we were walk-ins for garden seating hoping they wouldn't tell us we needed a resy for that but they said it was a 10-minute wait which was odd seeing as we were second in line. We went next door to wait. 

We were seated after our wait and I ordered a strawberry daiquiri which was on the stronger side (we like that) but still delicious sans my strawberry garnish. I eat my garnishes. From flowers to dehydrated fruit, I do not care lol. It was a minute grievance so life moved on but the rags they use to wash the tables smell like mop water so that's all I could smell for the first hour. A little bleach for some razzle dazzle should fix that. The Pog Nutcracker was fire. I was trying to put my finger on the familiar note and realized it was passion fruit. We decided on egusi dumplings and curry goat patties. The curry goat patties were very delicious and flaky, especially with that green aioli. I didn't like the mango chutney but I knew that before I tried it lol. The egusi dumplings I wasn't a fan of. The texture wasn't my favorite either. It was steamed and then pan-fried on one side. I did not taste any crab. Moving on to the roasted chicken shawarma and brown stew branzino. I loved the brown stew branzino. There was some sweetness to it and the fish had a great crunch with flaky meat. It was cooked perfectly. The rice and peas were fluffy and heavy on the coconut milk. I like! However, I did not like the chicken shawarma. It was heavy on the cumin. Even the rice was heavy on cumin. That dish leaned more towards Indian spices than anything and I was very confused but it wasn't my dish and the person who ordered it loved it. The large dishes are portioned perfectly. It was a nice size and I was surprised especially since the dishes looked smaller online. The servers were attentive and cordial so we did enjoy the service when we arrived and the music was amazing because not me throwing up the West Coast sign to Tupac (kidding but I love Tupac). There wasn't any music for the first hour when we came in. The bathroom was disgusting when I went. The person before me mentioned how gross the bathroom was and when I walked in the floor was sopping wet with urine and toilet paper strewn all over the place. The bathroom was decorated nicely overall but someone should be checking on the bathrooms consistently. Would I go again? Sure, but not on my dime. Please make sure the experience you're giving from top to bottom matches the price point, abeg.

Food tastes amazing, and I love the service of this restaurant. The servers were all very friendly and attentive. This is the first time I've tried cuisine like it, and I was blown away.

I was also blown away by the price, however, because as good as the food was, the price point is just way too high. It might be due to the location as well, but unfortunately I can't justify going back unless it's with a group of friends who have been wanting to try it, but haven't got a chance to yet.

I'm a Nigerian-American person who grew up in a Caribbean neighborhood, so l was fully prepared for this to be an amazing night of food. The food was prepared well, and the main entree portions were a good size. However, there wasn't enough authentic flavor for me. The egusi dumplings could have been egusi soup dumplings to make them more authentic. There was barely any egusi flavor. The stew that accompanied them was good. The oxtail Rangoon was very good. The entree oxtail were very large pieces of meat, but the gravy was too sweet & I'm sure it upset my stomach. The rice & beans were very good with just enough coconut milk taste. The shrimp were huge! Definitely get the shrimp. Food came out relatively quickly.

The music is very loud but fun. You'll enjoy it if you're a hip hop fan. As other reviews mentioned, they would benefit from cleaning the bathrooms more often. Our server was very nice & the staff appeared to get along. 

I would come back if someone got me a reservation but i wouldn't wait to walk-in or stand and eat.

The curry goat patties were the best thing on the menu for us. The oxtail was strangely sweet, not what we were used to as Jamaican diners. I didn't try the branzino myself but my friends liked it. The chicken shawarma was a disappointment, dry and bland. The drinks were so-so. After waiting a long time to get a reservation, we certainly expected more! The service was phenomenal and our waitress went above and beyond for the birthday girl!

My girlfriend was lucky enough to get a reservation for Tatiana on a Friday night at 7pm. The location isn't super well labeled and it took us asking a couple  restaurants in Lincoln center to find it. Service was terrific and everything we ordered was spectacular. For cocktails we ordered the pina pina pina, strawberry fields, and birthday daiquiri. Our favorite was the birthday daiquiri, followed by the pina, and we found the strawberry fields to just be ok. For entrees we ordered the braised oxtail and short rib pastrami suya. The oxtail came with 3 large, extremely tender pieces and a thick brown gravy that thickened over time as it cooled. The gravy was very salty, but it was so good. I scraped up every last drop into the to go box when we packed the leftovers. The pastrami was also so tender, and had an optionally nice kick when you dipped it in the cayenne powder that came on the side. The bread was soft and paired well with the pastrami. Portions for both entrees were very large and we had enough to take home for a small meal. We finished off with the bodega special (a homemade cosmic brownie with ice cream in the shape of a donut). I didn't love this - I found the ice cream to be a bit hard and also a bit too heavy on cinnamon/eggnog flavors - but my girlfriend loved it. My only complaint about the whole night was that the restaurant was super loud the entire meal between the music and diners - to the point you could barely hear the person across the table talk.

You can feel the inspiration cut through everything from decor, to music, to the stellar food and drinks, to the energy and sharpness of the wait staff. Every dish and drink ordered felt wow. Hard to stand up to the hype in NYC, but everything comes together genuinely here.
Had a 8pm rsvp but hasn't been seated for an hour? Restaurants are judged on food but also hospitality. The food is good but hospitality is probably a negative number.

Tatiana is hands down one of the best restaurants I've ever dined at. The stress of trying to secure a reservation here is well worth it, and I now see why the exclusivity exists. The ambiance here is dress causal, but the Hip-Hop and R&B music blasting leads to an upbeat vibe. 

The presentation from the table setting to the food was impeccable. They take tremendous pride in their appearance, which is refreshing to see. I also loved seeing the diversity among the patrons. The location inside Lincoln Center is a prime location for them. Our table was near the window, so it was enjoyable seeing people pass by and overlooking the water fountain and center itself. 

For drinks I had the POG Nutcracker and my girlfriend had the Birthday Daiquiri. The blending of Rum, Passionfruit, Orange, and Guava gave way to a sweet first taste with a slight kick in the end. 

The Crispy Okra was a 10/10. The sweetness and delayed kick of spice was such an experience. The cook was perfect as it had just the right amount of crunch without sacrificing the softness of okra. The Egusi Dumplings with crab and Nigerian red stew was another hit, with the spice hitting you again. 

For our entrees, the Branzino came out first. With large plates, they bring them out one at a time to enhance the experience, which was a pleasant surprise. The fish was phenomenal, as it had a nice crispness to it along with the savory stew sauce on top. Cutting it was like butter. The Short Rib Pastrami lived up to all the hype! I initially thought I was eating corned beef, as it had a very similar texture. But this was on another level. You didn't even need a knife to cut it. Our waitress recommends taking the Coco bread (buttery soft and delicious) and making a sandwich. What a meal this was. Even the cabbage was delicious. For dessert, we finished the night with the Bodega Special. The brownie was deliciously warm and soft, and the powdered donut ice cream hit all the right notes.

We saw the chef throughout the night, but it looked like he was only visiting the tables of people he knew or guests of the staff. Hopefully next time we'll be able to meet him and give him all the praise he deserves for such an authentic and beautiful dining experience.

I was in NYC for 12 hours and really wanted to try Tatiana before I left. I didn't have a reservation (big surprise) so I lined up around 4:15 on a Friday afternoon hoping to get a walk-in spot. The six bar seats in the restaurant are set aside for walk ins and as luck would have it I snagged the last one. While we waited for the restaurant to open, one of the staff came out with a beverage (passionfruit juice or something) which was thoughtful and the drink was delicious. I should have asked what it was. Everyone I interacted with from the hostess, to waiters, to bartenders, to what I'm assuming was the manager, was very welcoming. I already knew what I wanted - three of the small plates so I didn't need to fuss around with the menu. I got the curried goat patties, Egusi dumplings, and oxtail and crab rangoon. There were no misses. Everything was excellent. I also ordered a nonalcoholic drink (orange passionfruit guava) and it was good but nothing super special. The space itself is nice, dimly lit and intimate, in keeping with the hours it's open. It's pricey (my total was a little over $80) but I have zero regrets. Overall, based on my experience I would definitely recommend.

A solid spot if you enjoy the kind of ingredients they cook with. Had the okra, which was just on the verge of being too spicy, but was very savory and enjoyable, and the pastrami with bread, both of which were very good. Bodega special was also good, the ice cream actually tastes like donut, which is cool. Just a tip if you have a 5 pm reservation and want to avoid the line outside, there is another entrance through the lobby next door.

Definitely worth the hype! Omg everything was amazing! The trick is to arrive around 3:30-4 and stand in line for walk-ins at the bar. They have standing bar area (a little tight) and 6 seats at the bar. My party and I arrived at 3:45 PM on a Friday and we were the second group in line. 

We were seated immediately at the bar and were greeted by friendly bartenders and waiters. Kwame was kind as well! Service was top notch. 

We ordered cocktails (strong and not too sweet) which were very good. We ordered so many items off the menu! The okra was sweet and savory, one of my fav dishes alongside the refreshing piri piri salad. But omg that hummus is AMAZING! Sooooo flavorful! I would order the piri piri and black bean hummus 10x over! The STAR of the show was the curried goat patties though... Tens across the board. Hands down my favorite. 

For large plates, we had the braised oxtails (just ok) and the shawarma roasted chicken. That chicken was out of this world! And the lamb with rice was seasoned to perfection. I'm obsessed with Tatiana! I'll be back for dessert one of these days!

Getting a reservation is like waiting to see a solar eclipse. Somehow my coworker was able to secure this reservation for me. Thank you!

This place was more than just hype. There was even a celebrity sighting and I totally fangirled after seeing the Queen!

Loved the curried goat patty's were delicious with a serving of 3. The hamachi escovitch was such a tiny portion! It was an appetizer to be fair. It was very tasty with a carrot sauce?

Oxtail and crab Rangoon was good 

Entrees: if you are West Indian like myself, you have to realize you will not get traditional West Indian flavors. I leans more towards Nigerian flavors
Ordered the braised oxtail served with rice and peas   The oxtail were massive! We were served 4 large oxtail pieces in a Dutch pot. Loved this presentation. Very tender and fell off the bone. I had to remind myself these were not Jamaican seasoned oxtail. Overall, they were good. Just different. 

The short rib pastrami suya was a very large portion and delicious. It was served with a coco bread. This is a must order! 

Curried snow crab was ok. Something was missing from the curry bits a coconut curry. But needed something. 

Staff is top notch. Our server was well versed in the menu. It almost seemed rehearsed. Probably was. But I appreciated it. He was so sweet we and helpful. 
Then ended our night with these very pretty jello shots. The flavors were out of this world! 

Takeout isn't necessarily offered here btw.

Probably a 2.5-star experience.  A restaurant charging ~$190/person (that price includes drinks, tip, tax, etc.) has to meet certain standards for technique, service, and atmosphere.  The flavors were good--sometimes very good--but often unbalanced toward sweetness (the okra and the oxtails might as well have been desserts).  Technique was simple--a crispy, fried patty; a dumpling with crispy skin; a nicely cooked prawn (but not the most tender I've ever had); a nice, fudgey brownie--everything done well, but definitely  not exceeding expectations in terms of fine dining technique.  Service was cordial but overall lacking--water glasses left unfilled for long periods, wine glasses running empty.  The bathroom has a soap dispenser that spits soap at you at high velocity, and the toilet seat reminds one of a midtown office...just not a very nice experience for a "fine dining" place.  Finally, I like a lively atmosphere (I'm still in my early 30s, for the avoidance of doubt!), but the music is *ridiculously*, scream-at-the-person-sitting-across-from-you-just-to-be-heard loud.  I felt like I was dining at a nightclub, and think that the restaurant could still curate a lively, fun atmosphere without deafening music.  I won't be back, and while I appreciate what the restaurant stands for, I think that this is one we New Yorkers can leave for the tourists.  Better to spend our dining bucks at neighborhood restaurants that aren't trying to capitalize so much on hype.

street parking and garage parking nearby. beautiful fountain out front. beautiful ambiance.  The minute you walk into the restaurant, there is such a noveau vibe about it. 
Service was courteous and friendly. Our waitress suggested drinks and food upon request. She was attentive and super nice.
Food ... yummy! We had (collectively) patties with mango chutney, braised oxtail, curried snow crab and the cornbread and cod. One thing to NOTE:  these plates are not sharable sizes. You can share the appetizers but the 'large share' plates are sufficient enough for one person. All the food we had was delicious and flavored. Mango chutney was so good. Cornbread was the best part of the cornbread and cod dish. Portion size on this dish definitely could not be shared. 
Cocktails- LC negroni, dusse colada was very good. Strong enough and very tasty
The place is absolutely beautiful. Reservations are very hard to come by, great experience.

One of the hottest restaurants currently serving Afro Caribbean food in the heart of Lincoln Center. We made a reservation for a party of six on a Friday at around 5:30pm. It's otherwise impossible to get reservations for later times. 

We split several apps and entrees. The fried okra was the winning app! It maintained crisp without any sogginess at all. The goat empanadas were tastier than expected as I'm usually not a fan of goat meat. It didn't taste at all gamy. The rangoons were good too.

I thought all the entrees were so flavorful and hearty. Our top two were the pastrami and branzino. The cod came close too! We also appreciated the oxtail and the pork.

I can see this place being a great option to try once and come again a few more times for celebrations. I can admit that it is more on the expensive side but one must pay rent to be in Lincoln center I suppose.

Had an incredible meal at here last night. Each dish was beautiful, unique, and packed with flavor. The highlights include: the mango salad, the braised oxtail, and the white chocolate cheesecake (video), but honestly every single dish was tasty.

Thank you to our server @theguavastory on Instagram (who is also a chef!) for such great service. And I can't forget to mention how great the music was all night long.

Definitely pricey but great for a special occasion. Make sure to get a reservation unless you want to wait in line! There was a waiting list all evening.

So Amazing, start to Finish, decor, location, service and of course the Food,,,,,, don't Skip this NYC hot spot 
I would eat the "mushrooms take out " every night if I could 
Go Go Go!!!!!
Lovely atmosphere and amazing dishes will definitely go back prices a little high for small dishes but it was pretty good

Cool place. Worth it if you can snag a reservation. Better w a party of 4 vs party of 2 so that you can try more things. Goat patties were great w the mango chutney and the very very intense hot sauce. Dumplings I could have done without. They were fine, but I easily would choose $3 for 6 dumplings in chinatown vs $21 for 3 dumplings here. Short rib pastrami was very good when you put everything on the plate together for a bite. Really liked the bodega special dessert. Basically we got the greatest hits, and they delivered for the most part. Odd location for this restaurant literally inside Lincoln Center. 

One big negative was that our server was pretty un attentive. We had a 30 minute wait between small plates and pastrami and you could tell something was going wrong in the kitchen. Table next to us and behind us also had insanely long waits.....never a word from our server. Tell us something vs just keeping us waiting forever.

This place definitely deserves the hype as the New York Times #1 restaurant. 

Heads up - reservations are extremely hard to get. My group and I managed to get a last-minute reservation at 8:45PM on a Monday, and it was so worth it. 

APPETIZERS:
We started off with the crispy okra, truffle, chopped cheese, oxtail crab Rangoon, egusi dumplings, curried goat patties. 

The crispy okra was a good combination of sweet, sour, and also had some spice to it. I didn't have many vegetables in my meal, but this was definitely my favorite. 

The truffle chopped cheese is Tatiana's take on your local New York City deli's chopped cheese. I like how they took a staples sandwich and turned it into fine dining - the truffle was a nice addition.

The oxtail crab Rangoon really highlights how much thought Kwame Onwachi put into his dishes. I thought it was really clever how the oxtail mimicked the texture of crab in the crab Rangoon. 

Curried goat patties were my favorite appetizer by far. I'm not the biggest fan of goat as I feel like it's usually gamy, but these did not have that taste at all and the sauces that you eat with the patties made the dish for me.

Egusi Dumplings we're juicy on the inside and crispy on the outside. my friend is Nigerian and said that this was his favorite dish on the menu. The sauce that the dumpling sit on top of paired well with the flavors. 

ENTREES:
For entrées, we got the cod and cornbread, braised oxtail, pork belly pernil, and short rib pastrami Suya. 

The cod and cornbread were delicious as both were very moist and not dry at all. The cornbread was sweet and getting that perfect bite of cod, cornbread and tartar sauce was delicious. 

The braised oxtail came right off the bone and was marinated well. Solid choice. 

Pork belly pernil was very juicy, though there were a lot of charred bits that I wish were just a bit less burnt. 

Short rib pastrami Suya is a must get. Suya is spiced to perfection and when you pair it with the slaw, bread and sauce - you get a sandwich you will never forget. 

The dessert was pretty good, but I was so full I couldn't enjoy it to its maximum potential lol. For drinks I got a Tatiana Tonic which was solid. 

Overall, a quality fine dining experience - I would come back!

This restaurant truly is an ode to New York in every sense. The food is carefully thought out and crafted with unique and purposeful flavors that really make you excited to be eating at Tatiana. Yes, I know it's a hyped restaurant, but it deserves every bit of the hype. The okra is just so good - like the best okra I've very potentially ever had. The Goat curry patties could be lunch every day for me - I would really really like that. The dumplings tasty and really flavorful. Each dish feels like a bit of new york, but my favorite dish was the chicken. It brough the white sauce and hot sauce of new york food carts to the table in a way that was really fun and tasty. The chicken was sooo moist and perfectly seasoned, and the sauces were exactly what we wanted. 

Cocktails are good and the ambiance is fun, though maybe not what you would expect for a fancy restaurant. Though honestly with a group this is a great deal. The service is kind and definitely informed. I look forward to going again, and I actually have a reservation to do so - sorta crazy when this is one of the hardest reservations to get!

So obviously this place has a lot of hype, and my main question walking into this was, would it live up to the hype? From the second we walked in, to the service to the music, food and drinks everything surpassed my expectations. Our server Mikayla was absolutely amazing and super friendly. The drinks were great. The ambience was incredible. We got the, curried goat patties, hamachi escovitch, truffle chopped cheese, braised oxtail and of course the pastrami. We also got the bodega special dessert. Everything was outstanding here. The food was absolutely delicious. My favorite thing may have been the truffle chopped cheese it was incredible and super flavorful combined with their hot sauce. This is definitely a must visit. As hard as it as for most to get a reservation, I suggest you try your hardest for it.

I've been pretty hyped up to finally score a reservation at Tatiana. Long review short: the food and drinks, the service, and the vibe lived up to the hype. Can't wait for the chance to take friends here!
I have no words. The food was great, since I got to meet Kwame and invited me to his kitchen. The service is extremely nice and the food options are amazing.
Amazing. Everything from the service to each dish. Highly recommend the cod and the curried goat patties.

I was extremely happy to finally get reservations to one of the #1 restaurants in NYC, it was perfect as it was also my anniversary so the reservation was perfect timing . The ambiance was very nice, after scanning the room I could tell why this is a hot spot and why reservations are limited and hard to get. Inside had a good vibe with the music and beautiful people. The hostess was super friendly and I was about 30 minutes early for my reservations and they were able to seat us right away which I thought was super nice. Our waitress came over and greeted us and also shared suggestions from the menu. We started off with drinks and appetizers. The drinks were definitely on point and I will say probably the highlight for the night. For our small plates we ordered the crispy okra and dumplings. For Dinner we ordered the Branzino and rice and peas and the oxtail and rice and peas. Unfortunately, the food was not what I expected as for the taste and that is the overall push to give this restaurant only 3 stars. If I could rate each area I would say ambiance 5 stars, drinks 5 stars, appetizers/small plates 2 stars and entrees/large share 2 stars. 

Overall, it was great to dine at one of the number 1 NYC restaurants and I will check this one off of my restaurants to visit list.
This place was so good and deserves a Michelin star. The service is amazing and so is the food. Drinks are also very strong!

Visited Tatiana for the first time October 2023. Lincoln Center at night is pretty visually stunning, so yes I was in a good mood. The ambiance is pretty sexy, dimly lit with calm hip-hop and r&b music playing. My server was above average, she was on her job. I wasn't overly impressed with the food, and I definitely don't feel the taste of the food is reflective of the price point. Then again it is Lincoln Center, so I can only imagine. I had the oxtail entree. The texture was fall off the bone but I couldn't get passed the actual taste. Maybe I am used to traditional West Indian prepared oxtails, but I didn't finish my meal. Oxtail and Crab Rangoon was ok. I want to add, I was shocked that the restroom wasn't clean. It wasn't gross but far from clean.

Went back here and sat at a table instead of the standing only section, and I'd say I enjoyed the experience far more! The first time I was there, I had the Egusi dumplings, and I was not too fond of them. The flavor is just too rich, and I just didn't taste any crab at all in the dumplings. However, this time around, the food that we got was all on point. The piri piri salad was so refreshing and crisp and a nice  starter if you plan on having very rich, heavy food. The goat dumplings were perfectly fried and had amazing flavor, not too rich or spicy or heavy, and had just the right amount of stuffing to leave room for more food! The oxtails were the star of the show. So tender and glazed with a delicious sauce, I just wish maybe there were a little more veggies that came with the dish. But the rice was so good too. The new dish on the menu, the seafood boil, had two ginormous prawns, scallops, fish, razor clams and potatoes. It was a huge dish, and we got a lot of food so there was no way to finish it all, but if I were starving and didn't have all those apps, I would've ate all of it to myself, it was that good. All the seafood was perfect! The server we had was friendly and accommodating, the ambiance is loud and lively, maybe not the best place to bond with your mother in law hahaha, but she enjoyed it, so it wasn't a problem! If you can snag a resy, go and try a bunch of dishes and share! It'll be worth the hassle of trying to get in there!

This was below average experience for me, food was too spicy, service was lacking even at the bar, this place lacked the African experience/ element I was looking forward to. $80 for Suya? Please don't piss me off.  

The menu was also very limited. 

As an African living in diaspora, I expected better, something more traditional especially with the menu, service and ambience. Will I give it another try? Couldn't be too sure. 

I had my expectations set too high based on the hype on Socials, and my date and I left quite disappointed, maybe I came on a wrong night?

Unique 
Excellent service
Very reasonably priced & good cocktails 
Challenged kitchen 
Flavorful sauces 
Limited menu
Great ambience and location 
But overall, unremarkable

The food is absolutely delicious! But the portions are very small. 4 of us ordered 8 dishes and 3 desserts and my husband left hungry. The atmosphere is great. I loved that 90% of the diners were black. The service was fine. Why two stars? The front desk was rude, dismissive, and unprofessional. We had a 9:30 reservation, weren't seated until 10:15. Gentle enquiries were met with shrugs. Not a single host acknowledged us as the 4 of us stood in the uncomfortable foyer for 45 minutes. I am a huge fan of Kwame. I've met him. He is wonderful. But I'll never go back and I can't recommend it to anyone.
Fantastic experience from start to finish! We loved the ambiance and the pastrami was spectacular.

This is really a 4.5 Stars vs a full 5 Star, simply due to lack of reservation availability, which isn't their fault for being SO HOT!!! 
First, the Service is top notch, from the Hosts with an inviting, upbeat and congenial attitude to the same exhibited in each Wait Staff, especially ours, Mikayla P!!! Superb, efficient and had great suggestions. The atmosphere is earmarked with tasteful classic and contemporary Hip Hop, which is only appropriate given Chef Kwame's origin, their birthplace, BX! Also, Afro & World Beats graced the speakers and kept the vibe LITTY!
It was SO FIYAH, we bought birthday drinks and Appetizers for both parties, on each side, who were celebrating. One was a couple, the other was a sister dining solo. We ALL enjoyed eachother's company and food!
The food is a Vibe alone! 
We started with Appetizers:
The Curried Goat Patties, Egusi Dumplings,Black Bean Hummus (topped w a rich Lamb Ragu) and Peri Peri Salad are all a MUST! Everything's rich and unctuous, while the flavor-bomb Mango Squash Peri Peri Salad provided tropical relief. It cleansed the palate as we awaited our entrees. 
Be advised, the Peppa Sauce is NOT for the faint-of-heart! 
Our Entrees:
The Oxtail were savory and braised properly, creating a nice gravy to sop. 
Hands-down our table's FAVORITE was the Short Rib Pastrami Suya! Naija is definitely in this dish!  
Drinks were flowing, balanced well: Nutcracker,  Brut Champagne, Spicy Margaritas, M'semen and Negronis.
Overall, IF a reservation or walk-in can be had, GET HERE *Oleta Adam's vocals*

Loved this, everything about this restaurant was outstanding. Great food, service was top notch, vibes were immaculate, music was on point. Brought my mom, who is notoriously hard to please, and she loved it.

I had an absolutely incredible experience. I felt extremely fortunate as I managed to secure a reservation for my birthday. The hostess was exceptional in her knowledge of the menu and was very friendly. The food at this place is outstanding and delightful.
