Among my favorites were the oxtails, branzino, stewed chicken, and goat patties. I am definitely planning to revisit and I am eagerly looking forward to it. Special thanks to Kwame for the amazing culinary experience.

As they say, getting a reservation here is like winning the lottery! Dinner at Tatiana was worth the wait. The ambiance and decor is wonderful, the soulful music definitely set the tone and the service was great. Definitely note that the menu only has small shares and large share plates, so there are no individual entrees. For two people, we had 1 cocktail each, 3 small shares and 1 large share and we were certainly full. The standout dishes for me were curried goat patties and the oxtails which were super tender. Both cocktails, Birthday Daiquiri and Pina Pina Pina were fantastic! I definitely recommend checking out this restaurant for a special occasion or night on the town!

Come ready to eat when you finally snag a reservation at Tatiana because they will FEED you. I read an article about Tatiana now having the best pastrami in New York, and I must say, I agree. The Short Rib Pastrami Suya was perfectly cooked and so tender; paired with the pickled cabbage and the coco bread makes it such a satisfying combination. The curried goat patties are definitely the star of the small share options closely followed by the black bean hummus. Everything we tried was plentiful and also good flavor wise. Don't come here expecting a full burst of Caribbean flavors as they are balanced out with African spices. I think out of all the dishes we tried, the curried goat held the most flavor overall. The drinks are also not to be skimped on and definitely contribute to the vibe the nutcracker and daiquiri both have amazing balances of flavors while still being alcohol forward. I can't wait to return and try more of some of their rotating dishes as I was a little disappointed the truffle chopped cheese wasn't on the menu when I went. I would also recommend getting a seat in the main dining room area. We were seated off to the side in a somewhat dark corridor which was away from the action and felt even darker than normal. Lastly, the music is a true vibe and the service is also top tier. I can't remember our waiter's name but he definitely walked us through the menu and even held us down with a comp beverage when our food was taking a bit longer than usual. Tatiana, you are quality, and Chef Kwame is clearly setting a much needed standard here in NYC.

Stellar service should be called out. Our sever was bubbly, well informed and down to Earth. A well crafted menu reflective of the food of the diasporas. Started with the oxtail crab rangoon and fried okra which were just enough to get your appetite wet. Sipped on a wonderful McBride sisters Rose and then had the most amazing stew chicken- with the perfect browning- perfection.
Then we had the seafood boil- those scallops and shrimp- everything.
What a divine culinary experience!

Getting into this restaurant was definitely worth the wait. We got a 930pm reservation on a Tuesday night.

Once we arrived, we were greeted by a hostess who led us to our table. The  Afrobeat, hip-hop music drew us in to the vibe. 

I was a little underwhelmed by the aesthetic of the dining room area. It also built up my anticipation of what the food would be like despite the interior design elements of the restaurant. 

Once we were seated, I looked around the restaurant, and I loved that I saw people from all backgrounds represented. The menu was great, and it was nice to see how variety of African dishes from different countries were listed on the menu. 

We ordered the okra and oxtail wontons for appetizers and the Bronzino and Wagyu Pastrami for starters. For dessert we had the birthday cake donut.

I loved the Bronzino (perfectly seasoned with a spicy sauce on top) that I paired with jollof rice. The okra was my next favorite, which started off sweet and then turned a little spicy. The oxtail wontons were not memorable to me, and the pastrami sandwich seemed a little confusing to be on the menu but it was fun to eat. The bun it came with was delicious. I loved the doughnut ice cream which tasted exactly like doughnuts

We were lucky to get a reservation.  I had the best fried branzino.  My appetizer was a crab/oxtail rangoon.  It was delicious.  My date's dinner was very bland.  He ordered the stewed chicken.  The sauce was amazing, but the chicken had no taste.  We also enjoyed delicious mocktails.

Heard this was the number 1 restaurant in NYC. A 5:30 reservation, and they were kind enough to let us start later and end at 9p as our party was late due to a 1 Train issue. Located as a part of David Geffen Hall, you could easily pass it and not realize it was a restaurant inside. The sign is foil on glass and hard to see. The seating inside is busy, filled with pre-show, or post-show diners depending on the hour, and there's a small space that converts 4 tables into a single larger table or isolated room (the doorway doesn't fully close) for semi-private dining, in which we had 14. Music was very loud, and at one point we had them turn our area's music off to watch a presentation. At the tail end of dinner, a very sweet aroma was pumped in from the upper vents, it was too perfume-like sweet for me, gave me a bit of a headache.

Menu was preset for us, and some pre-ordered cocktails. Interestingly enough, no iced tea. First for a restaurant of this caliber... so I had an elderflower orange guava juice to start - nicely pleasant, not too sweet, but a lot of ice. Three deep sips and I was done... hm. Also nice to meet Craig, the GM. All courses shared on the table.

First course: 
- Honeynut Piri Piri Salad which I thought was one of the best dishes of the night. The persian cucumbers had been marinated in vinegar, sugar, and a little pepper, making it just like the Chinese pickled cucumbers that I love to make at home, and the little grapes were a nice balance. For 4 people to share, though, very tiny size. This easily could have been 3-4x bigger and been a better appetizer.
- Black bean hummus had a little berbere spiced lamb, sweet pickled sultana, m'semen flatbread (which reminded me of Chinese flatbread we make to go with black bean sauce pork). Was ok, but I wasn't blown away like some of my fellow diners 
- Hamachi Escovitch - 3 plates out, each with 4 pieces of hamachi. We were 14 diners. Someone should've told the kitchen and plated the extra two pieces with a sharp eye. Instead, left with two without. The hamachi was cold and firm, the flat plate and spread out carrot nage which was a nice citric sweet was hard to spread on the hamachi which would made it better (and the spoon didn't really pick up enough to roll the hamachi into the sauce). Poor plating here in my opinion - pretty but not for truly taking the food.
- Curried Goat patties were like little empanadas - the green aioli & mango chutney were good, but not enough to really slather on properly which would have made it much more enjoyable if you could cover the patties with more.
- Egusi dumplings with peekytoe crab, red Nigerian stew, and pickled pearl onions were an interesting take - the sauce similar to a tomato ragu, and more pearl onions would have made it more balanced. Rich and interesting fried dumplings.

Second courses:
- The short rib pastrami suya, with boneless wagyu short rib, caraway coco bread (like a harder, drier version of a dinner roll) and melted red cabbage - pass. It was far too salty and peppery for my enjoyment, even with the bread to try to balance. 
- Brown stew branzino was on the menu, but instead they had giant prawns, which were cooked ok, but my issue with giant prawns generally is that the flavor doesn't really make its way into the meat, and the outside is cooked tougher than the inside - pass, again.
- Take-out mushrooms - w scallion pancakes, plum sauce and pickled ginger - this was a dish that reminded me much of someone who liked these mushrooms and slathers a much of hoisin sauce on to cook, then you add some plum sauce and ginger. It was salty and sweet and savory, with some texture from a mushroom we often cut into much smaller pieces to make it easier to eat. Scallion pancakes were too thick, and super salty. While this dish I might get again to see if it was just prepared too salty and saucy this time, it didn't impress like some of the appetizers.
- sides were supposed to be rice & peas (didn't see any on my side of the table?) and crispy okra was just old okra that had been sliced in half and fried up ; good for fiber, but not really enjoyable to eat.

Desserts:
- Bodega special included a cosmic brownie (fantastic, dark, thick, rich and heavy - beautifully done), and powered donut ice cream (so-so, not a lot of flavor after the other desserts), and a "strawberry" sorbet that was orange and tasted a lot like orange-mango.
- Harlem chocolate factory white chocolate cheesecake with the vanilla mouse, chocolate ganache covering it and brown butter graham crumble - people liked this, though I'm not a cheesecake fan, but still reasonably enjoyable for the ganache.

Service - they were pretty good service, if anything very frequent on checking with drink status and water refills.

Overall, reminded me of my college roommate's Jamaican cooking which was better, so while some good dishes, it's not a favorite in my book, yet.

The menu selection was great. However, the food was not what I was expecting. I'm part Caribbean and was really looking forward to tasting a variety of the menu items . The services was great and the ambience was beautiful.
Fabulous. Just impossible to connect with anyone there. Reservations never exist. I've only been by walk in.

What a delight! Ambience is perfect for a date night, service was top notch and every dish was delicious 

My only thing is that the portion is on the smaller side but definitely worth coming

The food overall was pretty good, but I will say it's tough to get more than one large item when most of the tables are for two people. You really can only try one or at most two if you don't get any small plates. 

The pastrami suya was tasty, but felt like it was too much meat between two people and it needed some acid or some other side to make it feel less monotonous.

Service was good, though we marked that we were celebrating a birthday and that wasn't even acknowledged (which is fine, but I feel like usually at nicer restaurants they'll at least say happy birthday)

The cheesecake was the real standout, 10/10. Not that cold, delicious caramel sauce, not too sweet!

We had originally wanted the bodega special for dessert, but they were already out by 8pm. This turned out to be great for us because we loved the cheesecake

My friends and I were lucky enough to snag a prime reservation here for dinner. We were seated as soon as our entire party arrived. We did a round of drinks first. I went with a seasonal cocktail (i unfortunately forgot the name, but it was a honey/ginger drink with bourbon), which was very good. We were a group of 5, so our waitress recommended 5 from each section. While it seems like a lot, we did eat 95% of the items so it ended up being a great suggestion. We went with Egusi Dumplings, Curried Goat Patties, Hamachi Escovitch, Honeynut Piri Piri Salad, Black Bean Hummus, Fried Branzino, Braised Oxtails, Short Rib Pastrami, and Brown Stew Chicken. For dessert we ordered the Bodega Special and Cheesecake. Overall the food was very good. We had some definitely standouts (Goat Patties, Hummus, Oxtails), with some we would've passed on (Piri Piri Salad, Chicken). One additionally comment is that there aren't many options for non-meat eaters in the large plate section. They were out of the mushroom dish, so our pescatarian friend could only eat the Branzino. 

Ambiance is very fun. I loved the decor inside and the lively/upbeat vibes. Though it's bustling, we didn't feel it was too loud or difficult to hold a conversation. Our server was great as well. She made us some recommendations and checked-in on us throughout. We had great pacing and never felt rushed out. 

Overall, I definitely recommend coming in to TATIANA if you can get a reservation. My friends and I enjoyed our experience!

This restaurant is so hard to review. I'm really at a 3.5 here but I just don't have it in me to round up to 4, so 3 stars on Yelp it is. My friend and I did a walk-in on a warm Friday night in December. Got there at 4:45, waited in line, line moved relatively fast and by 5:15, had our name on the list and the hostess told us that we would be seated around 8/8:30. This was totally fine with us, and we killed some time walking around and grabbing drinks nearby.

We did indeed get seated at the bar at 8:30. Service at the bar was totally fine, nothing special but not terrible.  Now onto the food, which is full of extreme highs and lows and the result of my 3-star review:

1. Oxtail and Crab Rangoon: I am not a big crab Rangoon fan generally, but these were exceptionally good and one of the stars of the night. The sauce was delicious and the bites were cooked perfectly. Could taste the balance between the oxtail and crab. Great app.

2. Egusi Dumplings: literally hated these. They were bad. My friend and I couldn't even finish eating them because we just did not even want to consume them. The tomato sauce tasted like a can of stewed tomatoes. They are supposedly filled with crab but couldn't taste even a damn hint of it. Overall really horrible and I'm honestly offended these things are on the menu.

3. Oxtail Main: meat is cooked perfectly but no flavor. Not much more to say but just imagine a fall off the bone, perfectly cooked meat that needs salt and pepper at a minimum.

4. Branzino: this was delicious. Crispy and savory, and our favorite dish of the night.

5. Truffle Chopped Cheese: an off menu item. Really delicious chopped cheese with the perfect balance of truffle (I'm not a huge truffle fan, but they got it right). Overall very tasty but it would be extremely hard to mess up a cheesesteak truffle sandwich, so I'm not gonna give them a ton of credit here.  This kind of item is a lob.

6. Spicy margs. Excellent! That's all I have to say.

As a final note, the food comes out very haphazardly. One minute we only had the Rangoons and then sat for 15 minutes without anything. Next thing you know, we have the oxtails, branzino and the dumplings all crowded on top of each other. I know that the kitchen sends out plates as they're ready, but this seems like an excuse to avoid any kind of timing or planning for the patron's dining experience. If you're the best restaurant in NYC, gotta do better.

Was lucky to get a reservation here for an early evening weekday dinner!

My party was seated immediately, and the server recommended ordering 3 small plates and 1 large or 2 small plates and 2 large depending on which larges you order. My party (of 2) opted for 3 small plates and a large. The large (braised oxtails) was not too large, so my party could have easily gotten another large or at least another small. 

They also brought out some hot chili sauce that was VERY spicy. Only a very small amount is necessary per bite. 

Here is the ranking of the dishes I ordered:

1. Curried Goat Patties - only slightly goaty! These held up very well (no one likes an empanada that falls apart from being soggy), and the sauces were a great addition. 

2. Egusi Dumplings - had a very warm flavor, probably from all the delicious oil at the bottom. My only wish is that each dumpling had an equal amount of crispy to them from being pan fried (the top dumpling has a large crispy portion, the one at the bottom had significantly less). 

3. Crispy Okra - subtle hint of spicy, but otherwise really solid crispy vegetable with seasoning. Nothing fancy here. 

4. Bodega Special - this is the dessert I ordered because of the presentation. The cosmic brownie was a blast from the past! I was pleasantly surprised that the ice cream was formed into three small donuts (different from the presentation I've seen in pictures). Nothing special flavor wise but hit the sweet craving. 

5. Braised Oxtail - exactly what I would expect for oxtail, nothing special. Meat came off the bone pretty easily. 

Overall, a solid meal but nothing that would make me crave it again and again (especially with how hard it is to get a reservation).

Just an absolute pleasure from start to finish. Ambience is fun, our server was extremely friendly and helpful in navigating the menu, in house sommelier helped pair each dish and each plate/drink was top notch. The "adult Jell-O shots" are fun and flavorful, the dumplings were perfectly crispy on the outside with great flavor, the curried goat patties are phenomenal, the short rib pastrami suya is such a delicious/fun dish, and the fried branzino is an absolute masterpiece. No clue how it can be deboned so well, fried to perfection and still maintain so much flavor and meatiness. A shocking star is their house made habenero sauce. Oh my god the chef needs to bottle and sell that asap. Completely worth the hype,

I have admired Chef Kwame's culinary genius since his top chef days! This place was worth the wait ( I didn't have a reservation) and it's convenient that there's a bar right outside and stores nearby. Going shopping helped pass the time. The goat empanadas were  beautiful ambience, nicely curated playlist, and great service. I can't wait to go back!

Not for us. Snooty and silly. 

Emperor's new clothes.

But i guess the location is convenient.

Amazing amazing amazing. Okay I went here all the way back in July and am just catching up with yelp reviews. But I can't wait to go back. Food, service all great and the atmosphere was fun too. Definitely a good spot for a birthday dinner or a group, or a super fun date. 

So hard to get a reservation. We didn't have one. Not sure if this is still the case now, but I recommend showing up at 4.30pm and waiting in line as they have some tables and seats at the bar available. About 6 people, including the two of us, got seated at 5pm, and then after that it was a 45 minute wait. 

This place is on a lot of best restaurants lists and it's well deserved. Exactly what you want dining out to be- good food, good atmosphere, relaxing and non pretentious. Good times.

I'm grateful to live to see a black owned restaurant in the heart of #LincolnCenter.  The hiphop music playing, the decor, the vibe and of course the food all tell the story of Chef Kwame's life in New York City. 

This place is so hard to get a reservation to, it took weeks! But we finally got one (via Resy) and I'm happy to have experienced dinner here. 

I will say I wish the oxtail portion was bigger especially if it's a shareable dish and I was totally expecting jollof on the menu but we had was perfectly delicious. The sauce on the oxtail was a tiny bit sweet but because I was so full I took mine home and reheated it, it wasn't as sweet and I can honestly say I'd eat more right now if I had it. 

Finding the location is a bit tricky once you get to Lincoln Center, there's 2 entrances outside and inside of the center but it's really not far for the subway (parking is brutal in this area so your best bet is to take public transportation). 

Price wise, a meal for 2 people incl cocktails could run you a pretty penny so this is a place to splurge. 

The wait staff was a blast, our waitress was super helpful with suggestions and seemed so happy to work there. 

I tried several of the cocktails and the nutcracker was my favorite. 

I'll definitely be back when I am able to snag another reservation. 

Full list of what we ate: 

CORNBREAD & COD
Smoked Jerk Cod, Buttermilk Soubise, Fennel

BRAISED OXTAILS
Rice & Peas, Thumbelina Carrot, Chayote Squash

EGUSI DUMPLINGS
Jonah Crab, Nigerian Red Stew, Pickled Pearl Onion

CURRIED GOAT PATTIES
Green Seasoning Aioli, Mango Chutney

After much waiting to get a reservation, my Partner and I were thrilled to experience Tatiana. We mainly enjoyed the appetizers (Black Bean Hummus and Crab Rangoon). However, to our surprise, when we asked for extra Pita bread, we were charged $12 extra on a $18 dish. I don't mind paying for great food, but the lack of price transparency was a major red flag. We also had the Pastrami, which was extremely salty. The tables were close together and wobbled and the vibe was chill, but Tatiana was neither the luxurious experience we waited for and certainly was overpriced.

Finally made to this restaurant..... as a walk-in! Showed up at 4:30pm with only 6 people in front of the line. We were checked in around 5:15 with an additional 20 mins wait to be seated. They have a bar next door where you can order a drink and take it with you once your table (bar seat) is ready. This is what I ordered:

Apps/entree: Try the hot sauce! 

1. Egusi Dumplings- delicious but I would skip it 
2. Curried Goat Patties - very very good! 
3. Oxtail & Crab Rangoon - a must! 
4. Seafood Boil for two - to die for! Very big dish. 3 people can eat from it. The shrimp were gigantic and delicious as well as the scallops. As for the sauce, if I can use it as a face mask, I would do a mask 10x a day and lick it off my face! Lol. 

Drinks: all solid and beautifully made 
Espresso Coquito - OMG ..... can this be my morning drink? 
Nutcracker 
Honeymoon 

Good luck getting a reservation (pretty much impossible) but have hope..... go early and do the line!!! It's worth it!

Food 10/10 Service 10/10 Vibes 10/10 Cocktails 10/10- not one complaint! Perfect from start to finish! Kelly, Monica, KWAME   !!! 10/10!!! Highly recommend, pricey but the portions and quality call for the $$$$!

The food is decent but the service is really really really bad. The hostess wouldn't seat me without my friend, which happens, but also doesn't allow you to wait at the bar. She later came by to say that I could order a drink ($30) and wait in the hallway. They don't change out your cutlery between $40+ entrees. They don't take your coats. The bus boy started folding napkins at the empty table next to us and someone else was publically stuffing menus on our way out the door. The "specials" she listed were printed on the menu, which surprised her, and me since they're pictured in the NYT. The ambiance is fine. It's very purple with 2018 light fixtures and not the kind of place I imagine Tchaikovsky playing directly above. I wanted to like this but I'll stick to the Lincoln.  This was essentially fancy bodega food with service worse than a bodega.

Is this place inventive? Yes. Is it a one-of-a-kind restaurant? Yes. Is the food any good? ...meh. I feel like this place tries hard to be contemporary and unique that it forgot somewhere in the process that the food had to taste good as well. I consider myself an adventurous eater, but artistic qualities of a dish should be the sidekick, not the main character. 

We started out with the crispy okra, crab dumplings, and the goat patties. The crispy okra was so sweet, it was a borderline dessert. The crab dumpling might as well have been filled with mashed potatoes, because you couldn't taste anything resembling seafood in there. The goat patty was the best of the three small plates we had, but it was marginally better than a street empanada, and four times the price. 

Now to the "star" of the show, the wagyu short rib pastrami. While I give kudos to this restaurant for making something you don't typically find on a menu, this dish really missed for me. I feel like one has to try really hard to make something with the words "wagyu" and "short rib" in it taste dry, but unfortunately that's the case here. The curing the beef into pastrami was an interesting take, but not if it meant sucking out every bit of moisture from what was otherwise a juicy, succulent piece of short rib. Pairing the meat with the bread they provided just exacerbated the dryness.

I was really looking forward to this meal given all the accolades, but sadly left underwhelmed. Maybe it's my palate, but I felt like they prioritized giving us an interesting meal, but at the expense of a tasty one.

Tati Tati Tati...  
So glad I could patronize and support this BOB in Lincoln Center ! I've attended many shows since a young child in Lincoln Center, yet would not ever have thought that I'd get to eat from a Black owned business right here in the yard ! 

Let's get into the drinks- I got a LI Iced Tea. It was charged as a grey goose drink + extra. 
It was okay, def wasn't a LIT tea. 
I'd give it a 6.5/10 

I know because that's my drink!  

The food menu was a bit ehhh misleading. 
On the website it lists a "Chopped cheese" as a small plate. On the restaurant's menu, it wasn't listed at all. 
That could've been an indicator of something, yet I persisted. 

I love to review based on at least an appetizer and an entree so I proceeded to get the chopped cheese along with my meal. 
When I got the bill, the chopped cheese was almost $50. Quality item and amazingly delicious! 
However, I don't believe that it's a small plate. It's more of an entree.
Perhaps that's why it wasn't on the "in restaurant menu," 
I don't know. Either way based on the website, vs reality, the portion was a bit deceiving. 
9/10 
(only looses 1 point bc it's not an appetizer as projected on the menu)

Let's get into the pastrami.... LORD HAVE MERCY that pastrami was EVERYTHING and more ! It was tender and tasty! A completely delicious mouthful   
9/10 

The decor was dimly lit and seating at the bar is for about 6 people so don't get too excited about being seated there. It could take HOURS! 

Overall, I will return and look forward to trying even more dishes! 
May this establishment stand ! 
Hoping nothing but the best for them!!! 

Overall I'd give them a 9/10 for their amazing food!

I really really wanted to love my experience here given the hype and it was overall good but not amazing. The ambience and environment are fairly average, it felt like I was in a hotel restaurant and surrounded by a ton of people. The wait staff was subpar and didn't seem interested in anything to do with us (except for the guy filling our water, shout out to him). We got the goat pastries which were amazing as everyone says. The rest of the meal was good, enjoyed our choices. The pastrami was a must (best pastrami I've ever had) and the oxtails were great. The dishware, which usually doesn't bother me, was confusing. The oxtails were served in something straight off the stove. For the price point, worth a try but not worth a repeat.

My sister said, "at least the music was good and the bathrooms were clean". 
I would not tell someone not to eat here, and would probably return with a friend if they so desired, but other than that I'm good on my one time, and am grateful for the experience.
It was just iight and appreciate what the brother is trying to do, but I guess when you're familiar with the cuisine it left desiring more. 
Yes, fine dining is an holistic experience and large portions are not to be expected but the food looked lonely on the plates. Literally three oxtails...  Goat meat patties were good but salty inconsistent chunks of salt. We had a few other things, but nothing that left me going dang I need more of this.
Service was alright. Waiter was patient. 
Reservation process whack.
Also a Caribbean Africa spot and no fried plantain aka dodo?!

What can you expect from a restaurant everyone is talking about? It will either live up to its reputation or it is totally hyped up. Well we wanted to find out for ourselves and the verdict is in... IT IS AMAZING! No joke. Honestly. If you are able to get a reservation or can endure long line of walk-ins outside the building, I encourage you to do so. From the moment you walk in you are greeted by smiling faces. The ambiance was a perfect blend of warmth and sophistication. They definitely know how to make you feel special. We were there celebrating our 20th wedding anniversary with 2 other couples. As soon as we mentioned that, we were offered glass of delicious champagne on the house. We have decided to taste every single appetizer on the menu and let me tell you it was difficult to pick a clear winner. The most surprising was their black bean hummus, which we ordered 2 more off. Every bite was a symphony of flavors complementing each other. So light, refreshing and culinary delight. With that we enjoyed some of their finally crafted cocktails and wine. For our main course we chose Take out Mushrooms, Braised Oxtail, Short Rib Pastrami and Pork Belly Pernil. All these delectable array of dishes showcase the chef's skills and creativity. We ended our dinner on a sweet note with coffee, rum cake, brownie and cheesecake. We can not thank enough Craig, the restaurant's manager and our waiter Neo J who made this dining experience memorable and one that surpassed our expectations. Job well done! Can't wait to be back for more

Food was very enjoyable. Everything was full of flavor and well seasoned. The service was good but not exceptional. Ambiance was on point. Given all I would definitely return and look forward to doing so.

A friend recommended that I visit this restaurant during my work trip as there is a considerable amount of buzz around it.

I decided to walk in without a reservation and was put on the waitlist. This visit was well worth the hour-long wait. 

I was offered a seat at the lovely bar, and the waiter immediately offered me water and walked me through the interesting menu. To get a feel for the overall menu, I opted for three appetizers-- the Crispy Okra, Curried Goat Patties, and Oxtail & Crab Rangoon. All were delicious, but the Curried Goat Patties, with their well-balanced mango chutney, were my favorite. 

I ordered the Suntori Time cocktail, which was also delightful. 

This restaurant has a sophisticated vibe without seeming pretentious. It's very clear that every aspect of this restaurant was well thought. From customer service, aesthetics, and of course to food and beverage-- this experience was seamless. Definitely recommend this restaurant.

4 - Met Expectations
This place did not blow me away, but for the price the quality of the food and service was what I expected. One very cool thing they did was hand out cups of tea to the people waiting in the walk-in line. The curry patties were fine for the small share, would try something different next time. The braised oxtail and rice were good. The bodega dessert was very cool and unique! Would recommend that. I encourage you to read the back-story about this place so that you can appreciate the thought behind the decor, music, and of course the dishes.

My date and I made it our mission to secure a reservation at Tatiana by Kwame Onwuachi. It was challenging for us, but well worth it. Plus, it was a great team building exercise. 

Tip #1: reservations open each day at noon, with only a 28 day window. This is a great option if you have patience. 
Tip #2: booking is through Resy, which is owned by American Express. While the tables are not held specifically for AE clients, concierge can place you on a priority waiting list. 
Tip #3: the entrance is quite discreet. Ask one of the guards to point you in the right direction. 

The venue is dark, yet vibrant. The music creates a relaxed atmosphere. My date and I were seated promptly for our reservation. 

We started with the oxtails. For our entrees, we shared the chicken and oxtails. Our cocktails were expertly created. I ended with the Harlem Chocolate Factory White Chocolate Cheesecake. 

Now. I was admittedly nervous about my dining experience as someone with a severe allergy to onion. Afro-Carribean cuisine typically incorporates onions. I preemptively took medicine to coat my stomach and was just fine. The food was absolutely delicious. The phrase "falling off the bone" applies to every entree we tried. My date and I were drizzling the stew over the rice which was a delectable combination. I had difficulty sharing the cheesecake! It was divine. 

Overall, we immensely enjoyed our dining experience and would love to return!

Food 4/5 | Service 5/5 Ambiance 5/5

I loved every minute at Tatiana. We were able to score reservations for 5:30pm and it was generally packed for dinner time. Despite that, our waitress was so attentive and sweet. We were seated right away and the waitress brought us a free glass of champagne for our anniversary. That gesture alone was so a sweet surprise! I couldn't believe they did that! The food was amazing! Didn't even get a picture of the goat patties but those were so delicious and rich and they go so well with the small hot sauce they served you for the dishes. And Wow it's super spicy! You need only a bit of it as it has Scotch bonnets  
The hamachi was a refreshing and cut the richness of the other foods like the Egusi dumplings which were very good but I could've went without ordering. The chopped cheese was perfect and the buns were soft and pillowy and had perfect amount of truffle. My favorite dish and crowd favorite was the pastrami suya. There was sooo much meat and the bread paired with it was so buttery and perfect! I would so go back to Tatiana but I would recommend for an anniversary or birthday

let's start with the 7:30pm reservation - didn't get seated till 8:15pm - no problem
waiter was great 
Curried goat patties are trash - golden Crust makes a better goat patty -seriously it's bland not even worth the $8 per
 the sample rice they offer with the large share oxtail is laughable 
Only thing i enjoyed was the OXTAIL & CRAB RANGOON
the restaurant is more worried about getting ppl in and out the seat under a hr they wouldn't  even allow Togo orders from The small share ( appetizers ) you can't even wait by the bar for it - once you order don't even think about ordering again - I honestly don't see my self going back - actually had to take my date to another place being that we were still hungry 

Place looks good great area

We got the fried okra and the pastrami. The okra I thought was just ok--it came with a sauce that I thought over powered the vegetable. The sauce was good, don't get me wrong, just thought the sauce was the star and not the okra. The sauce was also RIGHT on the cusp of being to salty. NOW...let's talk about this pastrami....10/10. It was perfectly salty; the cabbage was slightly sweet and tangy; and the rolls were soft and buttery. I loved it so much. Drinks, service, and ambiance were also good. The music was a vibe, but also not too loud. I would definitely return!

Curried goat patties: A+
Egusi dumplings: A-
Hamachi escovitch: A
Oxtail & crab rangoon: A
Braised oxtails: B
Short rib pastrami: A+
Jello shots: B+
Bodega special (cosmic brownie & powdered sugar donut ice cream): A
Rum cake: A

Shoutout to that crazy cold snap that hit NYC a couple weeks ago and made someone cancel their res last minute! Without it, I would still be on Resy every day trying to crack the code on getting in. 

The empanada-esque goat patties and short rib pastrami were PHENOMENAL. Once you have them, it's clear why Tatiana topped the NYT's restaurant list. 

I really enjoyed the hamachi -- it was really fresh and the sauce it came with was nice, I would order it again but my tablemates weren't as wild about it (namely, it felt like a dish we could get anywhere). The oxtail & crab rangoon was also great -- generously filled, flavorful, and not too salty (which happens too often with oxtail imo).  I can't remember specifics with the egusi dumplings but recall liking it. The braised oxtails were okay -- yes they were fairly tender but we were underwhelmed. Although this is one of their most popular and highly recommended dishes, it was the lowlight of the meal. 

The bodega special and rum cake were fantastic. The powdered sugar donut ice cream actually looks like little donuts which is a fun little touch! The rich chocolate brownie mixed with the ice cream was lovely. The rum cake was moist and the sweet cream added the perfect amount of sweet to it.

Their cocktails are really good, and STRONG! The pog nutcracker was the table favorite, and I even liked their negroni even though I am not a negroni person. The jello shots are so cool and pretty and tasty but expensiveee and will be a one time thing.

The vibes/decor are trendy, and even with the low sorta moody lighting the place feels upbeat. The service was also top notch! 

As much as I loved it (I'm still salivating over those goat patties and the short rib pastrami), it will be awhile before I can afford to go back. The bill for the three of us came out to over $500.

Incredible experience. Believe all of the hype!! Located in Lincoln Center, Tatiana has something for everyone, with incredibly unique and delicious dishes. The stand out for me was the short rib large plate, and the hamachi appetizer. The inside has a cool and fun vibe, and our waitress was extremely knowledgeable. If you can get a reservation, run don't walk to Tatiana!

The food honestly was excellent, everything we ordered was 10/10. The only thing that ruined our experience was the wait time and not realizing who our actual server was until over an hour into our dinner. It took us over an hour to get 1 drink and 1 appetizer. The whole meal ( 1 drink each, 2 apps, 2 entrées, 1 dessert)  took over 2.5 hours from start to finish. They also served me my entree before my partners and i ended up having to wait about 6-7 minutes until their dish came out so the food was not hot when i finally got to try it.

The food was delicious and came quickly. (For fine dining, I don't believe the food should come so quickly, but the taste didn't suffer.)

The service was very good. The waitress was attentive and had good recommendations.

I'm giving this place 4 stars because the ambiance is lacking. I think the owner sacrificed a lot of the restaurant's personality by being in Lincoln Center. (The main seating area is in a medium sized room that kind of resembles a restaurant in a museum.) I think he would do well to leave Lincoln Center for a larger space that could show more of his personality (where he could create a VIBE). I think ambiance is so important when a restaurant comes with this hype and price tag, and it was a bit underwhelming.
Food was amazing. Servers were consistently present & knowledgeable of the menu. The vibe was classy, sexy, & warm.

Absolutely amazing Caribbean food with great service. Manhattan lacks Caribbean spots, but this place is exceptional with its fish, oxtail, and other meat options. The cocktails were also great. The trick to getting a seat is to arrive early if you haven't made a reservation.

My tastebuds were on another level during this dinner. I was surprised how each dish was executed so well. From the texture to the flavors, I still think about this dinner. I don't think I've ever had okra done better. The startes were so delicious and the hot sauce, I wish was on my kitchen counter. The desert took me to a very special childhood moment on steroids. The decor is stunning, with beautiful gold chains that reflect the perfect hue. Chef Kwame was in the kitchen, to our surprise, he stopped by and spoke with us for a hot minute. The fact he took that small time out of his evening to talk with us made this dinner that much more special. What a Chef.

The food is TOP TIER! Service was undeniably great. The server was very attentive to all of our needs and the ambiance of the restaurant was very welcoming. 100/10! A must try. I cannot wait to be back.

I set up a notification in resy but woke up this morning only to have to pay $$$ to cancel a reservation I never made
Very upset 
Be very careful when setting up notifications with this establishment you might end up with a 5:30 reservation that you have to pay $50 to cancel

Be warned

It was every thing they said it would be. The staff is more than attentive. I burned my toughest k. The goat Patties i just could stop my self. But please do not sleep on the peri peri salad the flavors are phenomenal. I dined solo so i went with the pork and how they get that thing so crispy is beyond me. But dam it's good. And I'm still dreaming about dessert.

This restaurants deserves all the love it's been getting! Me and my family had one of the best meals/experiences we ever had in New York. The customer services, vibe, & food were all outstanding. We ordered almost the whole menu and they did not disappoint on anything we ordered. The only  bad thing I can say is the short rib was very small for $85 but it tasted amazing. The Ox Tails were amazing they were different from any others I've tasted. The flavors were immaculate sweet & savory with a sticky texture my favorite dish for sure. Wash all it down with one of their cocktails from the bar and you are ready to go. That being said I know this place is very hard to get into but you have to find away to book.

That curry goat patties were to die for. And I don't say that lightly. Everything was good but that stood, jumped and flipped out. I was also a fan of the egusi dumplings. You walk in and the light is just low enough to be sexy yet still be able to see. I liked the ambiance of the place, our server was super knowledgeable about the menu and says the owner lets them try it first to be able to speak on what to recommend which I love and think is so smart. The short rib was excellent, no notes with the bun. The okra was good I'm not used to okra not in a stew or slimy which I like so this was an experience. What is underrated imo is the mushroom entree. That was a journey and I loved the scallion pancake it came with. That paired better with the short rib than the brioche bun imo. Dessert was great, we got the golden rum cake  but I'm not a sweet focused person. Worth the hype off the aforementioned dishes.

After several failed attempts at securing a reservation, I was forced to use a third-party service to pay for a reservation. Occasion: birthday. 

Food: The waitress gave my partner and I a complimentary glass of white wine to start our meal. After that, we were given the menu. I ordered the short rib pastrami suya, and my partner ordered the fried branzino. We were told that the dishes would come out individually so we had the fish first. 
Portions are intended to be shared. As a non-fish eater, I can say this was probably the best fish meal I've ever had, and the rice was an excellent pairing.

Tatiana's is apparently hailed for their short rib pastrami, but I felt the entire meal was a tad underwhelming. It was essentially a sandwich you had to create, and the flavors didn't come all the way through the way.

Ambiance: I expected the ambience was favorable, with popular hip-hop music as the backdrop to the evening. 

Pricing: This is definitely not a cheap date so definitely bring your wallet. We opted to not have dessert. 

Other notes: I'll say the bathroom was incredibly dark, and I almost thought the lights were out but I did capture a great selfie in there, so I guess it worked out fine.

Overall, this is a high end take on African and Caribbean taste, which is something you rarely see executed on this level, and for that, I have to tip my hat. Being someone of Caribbean descent, it felt great to see the praise Tatiana's has received globally.

My experience was positive, but after waiting several weeks to try to secure a free reservation, and ultimately having to pay for one, I can't say in good faith that I would be making a return trip anytime soon (if I was even able to get through to making the reservation for free this time around).

In my opinion the restaurant is severely overrated. Nothing to talk about . The chicken was OK , but the side dish for chicken terrible , tasteless and super spicy . All four our  appetisers were below mediocre level . Mango sherbet was tasty, but well  overpriced for the size of portion. Service was OK , at least attentive. Sorry !

Worth the hype, worth the price and worth the wait!!!!

The food was amazing, so few fine dining spots in NYC serve food outside of the normal French, American + Japanese bubble. Not to mention the fact that every single dish was a fusion of cultures, and so well thought out. 

The oxtail, the empanadas, the pork belly, and short rib were all delicious. The Jell-O shots were so fun, never seen that before. The coquito was also delicious. 

Music had me dancing in my chair all night. And the service!!! Super attentive all night, from the minute we walked in to the second we left. 10/10 experience.

Tatiana is celebrity chef Kwame Onwuachi's ode to his Afro-Caribbean roots given the fine dining treatment, which is the first I've experienced with this cuisine. Hopefully this changes over time and there's a range of experiences one can have eating this food. Tucked into the palatial Lincoln Center, the beautiful space had a city vibrancy to it-- a hip hop and r&b playlist, mood lighting, an excited crowd. 

Checking out the menu, Kwame loops in tastes from his upbringing, from African (the crispy okra and egusi dumplings for example), to Caribbean (like with the goat curry empanadas and braised oxtail), to NYC by way of his famous chopped cheese small plate and a dessert called the "bodega special" consisting of a powdered donut and cosmic brownie. Nostalgic for those of us who grew up going to bodegas. 

The popular "takeout mushrooms" that many effusive reviewers convinced me to order as well as the chicken were not my favorite and the small plates were in tiny portions (though the egusi dumplings were very tasty), but the entrees are larger. 

Near our table Chef himself was there, flirtatiously engaged in conversation with a couple of ladies for what seemed like the entire duration of my meal. Overall the menu is not so vegetarian friendly FYI, and it's definitely a splurge night out. But the global mash up of flavors and fun ambience as well as their delicious cocktails make it worth a visit.

What else can I say that hasn't already been said about the culinary triumph that is Tatiana? As many reviewers mentioned, getting in line by 4:15 before the restaurant opens is the easiest way to get a table. I came here on a Wednesday and there were already a few people ahead of me at that time. At 5 pm sharp, the doors opened. Once the 5 pm reservations were seated, the hostess began to take the few parties in front of me. After a short wait at check in, I was seated at a table by 5:30. 

Walking into Tatiana, you just feel it's going to be a good time. The décor is hip and trendy, the music is fun and upbeat without being too distracting. Our server was an absolute gem. She went over the menu with us, pointed out some of her favorites and recommended dishes be shared family style. Upon reviewing the menu I was disappointed to see some of the standout dishes were no longer available, specifically the short rib pastrami suya, which was very much the reason I was there. We started with the hamachi, curried goat patties and crispy okra. The hamachi was fresh and soft, paired with a vibrant green sauce. The curried goat patties were perfectly crisp, and the curried goat was some of the best I've had in my life. The crispy okra was impeccably seasoned and seared. For mains, we ordered braised oxtails and mom dukes shrimp. The oxtails were incredible and the mom dukes shrimp were enormous, paired perfectly with dense buttery Texas toast. My only regret is not having enough room for dessert. I will be back!

I was worried I'd feel the restaurant was overhyped but I was not disappointed. I loved the food (though I do wish the portions were better because 3 oxtails?!). I loved the music, the staff, and the fact that the drinks actually had liquor in them! Our server, Monique, was so sweet! Restaurant servers often appear overwhelmed and rush you through your dinning experience but she had a calming presence and was warm and welcoming - indeed making us feel "at home."  Wish it was easier to get reservations so that we could return more often but glad we had a great experience.

Delicious meal filled with unique riffs on delicious flavors. The patties and the pastrami are MUSTS as well as the cosmic brownie - the donut icecream was so cool! 
Very cool space and atmosphere. Service was okay, would have expected better for the cost/vibe - I think we just got unlucky with our server as the waitress serving the table next to us seemed to be phenomenal. 
Excited to see what Kwame does next!

The food here is absolutely delicious. The customer service is perfect , and the setting is just right . I definitely would recommend going if you're lucky enough to get reservations . I will most definitely be going back when i get that chance . I had curry goat empanadas, crab/oxtail Rangoon , braised oxtail , fried Branzino , and the donut ice cream with cosmos brownies for dessert . Lemon drops for drinks . Check out my tik tok ( jeriicarenee9 ) and my reel on ig Jeriicarenee .

I was very excited to try out this restaurant. I love the concept, Afro Caribbean by way of NYC. However I was a little disappointed in the food. The food did not come out hot at all. The pastrami, the dish I was looking forward to the most, came out barely warm and dry. I am very familiar with suya and the suya powder seemed diluted. We didn't even finish it. My favorite dish was the egusi dumplings. I also liked the rangoons. The atmosphere is nice and the service wasn't that bad. I was surprised how good the drinks were. I got the Negroni and the nutcracker which was recommended.  I am hoping they  make some changes and perhaps I may go back. But overall overpriced for an average meal.

I got so lucky on a Monday that I was on my phone and Resy notification popped up that a table opened up at 5pm, and I quickly snagged it!
When I got there, there was already a line of around 20 people waiting at 5pm, so just know that if you are planning to try walk in. 
Anyway, I'm so happy that a restaurant like this exists in New York. It's so refreshing, chic and very unique. 
Service is great and the ambiance is a vibe. You may end up seeing a celebrity! I saw Jerry Seinfeld sitting two tables away from me. 
Now the food, we tried the goat patties, lamb hummus, dumplings, jumbo shrimp and my partner tried the oxtail stew. Got the cheesecake for dessert. Everything was delicious, but what stood out to me the most were the goat patties and the shrimp. These two were bursting with flavor and they were just amazing. 
I would definitely come back here, if I can get a reservation! Lol

Incredible restaurant that lives up to the hype, considering how hard it is to get a reservation at this place. Ambiance and vibe of the place is amazing, upscale venue but they're playing upbeat music the entire team. Service was superior. 

Food was incredible. For two people, we did two apps and two mains. The goat patties to start is a staple. For mains, highly recommend the braised oxtail. We also did the Harlem chocolate factory white chocolate cheesecake for dessert, which was unreal.

I cannot say enough about this exceptional restaurant. I have been following the chef for some time and finally was able to get a reservation for my anniversary. The location is in the middle of Lincoln Center and was beyond gorgeous to compliment this equally elegant restaurant. From the moment I entered, I was greeted by friendly staff who were immediately attentive and responsive and didn't feel pretentious or stuffy. I started at the bar and enjoyed two cocktails while I waited for my plus 1. The drinks were fantastic. By the way, I am a mixologist who travels to exceptional cocktail bars. This place had drinks that stood out. They were refreshing, while spirited and tasty. The nut cracker was not too boozy, but a delightful game changer like I have never had before (I usually hate this drink made by other establishments). Then, once we were seated, we ordered a medley of dishes from the Hamachi Eschovitch, to the Oxtail and Crab Rangoon and the Egusi Dumplings to start. Everything we ordered was eclectic, unique and truly melted in your mouth. Some items had a bit of a kick, but nothing overwhelming (except for the side sauce provided - beware). Then, for dinner, we enjoyed the Sofrito Roasted Chicken which was perfectly cooked, juicy and had an assortment of flavors and reminders of my childhood (just like grandma made). We also ordered Mom's Shrimp Dish which was another award winning dish. For dessert, we ended the meal with the rum cake. Spectacular! I highly recommend this phenomenal restaurant for a unique and exceptional culinary experience. Kudos to Kwame and wishing you much success.

Excellent and special place. Sleek vibe with a great playlist (a little loud for those that mind - not me!). Within Lincoln Square - can be a bit tricky to locate.

All of the food was incredible. Do not sleep on the crispy okra. I could have eaten another two orders - the perfect amount of spice to make them truly addictive. 

Also, you cannot miss the Short Rib Pastrami. The presentation is beautiful and the taste is even better. Additionally, you can get creative as you eat with the bread to make sandwiches, cabbage, spice rub, and sauce. 

Highly recommend reading a bit on Kwame Onwuachi - great story.

The hype is real. Great flavors, innovative combinations and just damn tasty! We tried some of the more popular dishes and they all were great. 

The best dishes were the curried goat patties (tons of flavor) and the Short rib pastrami suya which was tender and delicious. It was paired with a melted red cabbage which we couldn't get enough of.

The take-out mushrooms were really good but the star of that dish was the scallion pancake which was one of the best I've ever had. I'm still amazed that it held its heat the entire meal.

We also had the egusi dumplings which were very good but completely overshadowed by the other dishes. Still good but felt bland compared to the goat patties.

The recommended was 2 small and 2 main dishes but that seemed a bit too much, especially since many of our dishes had a lot of carbs. 3 small and 1 main is probably more appropriate. 

Overall a great visit and we'll be back.

The staff was amazing.  Kudos to whoever is in charge of the playlist.  The food was good, but I believe it is overhyped.  No real bar due to bar seating used for reservations.  If there is a random opening I would go back but would jump through hoops to obtain a reservation.

New York is a tough town, where being everything you should be can still bury you beneath a 100-story gleaming glass tower of expectations. Every dish and drink we had at Tatiana was rich, complex and exactly what I wanted. But none of it measured up to the difficulty of getting a reservation here (or, quite frankly, the absurd $85 price of the short ribs). 

Come to Tatiana without the pretense that the food media has bestowed on it, and you'll leave full, warm and content.

Had an extra night on a work trip and am trying to visit James Beard nominees when I have time and am in the mood to splurge.  Tatiana did not disappoint.  I sat by myself at the bar (was seated right away walking in on a Friday night at 8:30).  Had the spicy marg, fried okra, and the dumplings.  Everything was outstanding.  The fried okra is one of the best things I've ever eaten!  The ambience is great too - right at Lincoln Center, overlooking the plaza.

Had a reservation for a Monday evening at 9pm for 3 people. Music was good, just the right volume and vibe. The place was packed. Server was welcoming and provided suggestions. We ordered cocktails first and those took very long to come out and so we skipped on any additional rounds. We ordered 3 small plates: curry goat patties, the oxtail crab ragoon and the honeynut piri piri salad. We ordered 3 large plates, the braised oxtail, the branzino, and the brown stew chicken.  The food came out very quickly, each plate coming out just after the other. First the small plates then the large plates, with little time between. It all felt a bit rushed with no time to digest but it was also on the later side so wondered if that played into it. We were already on to our first large plate before the cocktails made it to the table. The honeynut salad was by far the favorite at the table! Every ingredient was fresh, crisp and refreshing and it was unique. I would get this again but not share! Everything else was good, but I wasn't blown away. I think my local uptown caribean spot does better patties. That said, I'm glad to have tried the restaurant and the reviews are amazing but I didn't quite understand the hype. Its possible I let the hype build up for the food create for high expectations. I don't think I would go back with a group or make a reservation, but if I could grab a walk in bar seat for a quick cocktail and that salad, I would!! Huh

Where do I start? This restaurant is a whole vibe. Spectacular service with such an attentive and friendly staff. I didn't think I had one person taking care of us, it was an entire team working together. 
The food was out of this world good. Best Afro-Carribean food I've had. Everything we ordered was so tasty and mouth watering delicious. Everything is meant to be shared and could easily be shared with 4. Small entrees are not so small and large are large. Chef Kwame Special spicey sauce was definitely firey and had a kick to it. Careful if you can't handle spice. Oxtail & Crab Rangoon, short ribs, and fried branzino are a must. Short ribs were filled with flavor and soft and flakey. Piri piri salad was also good but there were other options I would go for over this.  There were multiple oxtail dishes and we just couldn't decide. Went with the small plate because we had to get ribs. 
Ok for dessert the brownie cake with donut icecream was a good pick! We were so stuffed but still finished the dessert.
Chef Kwame was hanging around the entrance and was very friendly, taking pics and chatting with everyone. 
I can see this place getting Michelin very soon.

Returned to Tatiana to try some new items. We went on a Friday and waited about 20 mins. Not bad at all. I ordered the holy grail, curry goat patties. Love that crust; has just the right pinch of salt. We also ordered the egusi dumplings, the black bean hummus with Berbere Spiced lamb and the seafood boil. 

I've had the egusi dumplings before and thought they were just ok. Same goes for this visit. The hummus was cool but I wish the lamb flavor stood out. The flatbread pieces that came with the hummus was flimsy so it made it hard to pick up the hummus.  Now, for the showstopper, that seafood boil. I had grilled shrimp, andouille sausage, scallops, salted cod, mojo razor clams, spiced butter and sourdough. Do yourself a favor and order that. Loved the flavor and the portion. At the time of our visit, it was the most expensive item on the menu and it is worth it. We had enough for leftover. Cocktail wise, try the Birthday Daiquiri. For additional, visit @iFancyNY on instagram.

Definitely worth the hype. Everything was fantastic. Large sharing menu: the oxtails were the star! Pastrami was good, but not on the level of the oxtails. On the small sharing menu: dumplings and goat patties- both good. Definitely get the brownie. Outstanding.

Arrived 1 min after we passed our 15 min grace period and was told our table was gone, because the previous maitre'd screwed up the reservation. Told us our table had a 6:30 reso? How could that be when we're allowed to dine for 2 hours. 

Honestly, if this was the type of restaurant I thought it was, they wouldn't have given us grief. Eventually, the manager came by and sat us right away. Already left a sour taste in our mouths. Not Michelin worthy at all - not that they care. Okay, enough bitching. 

But, the food was very good and if you forget what I said above, this would have been an easy 5 stars.

Goat patties are a must. 
Tuna was good - spicy 
Egusi dumplings were eh 
Branzino was cooked well but I didn't love the sauce
Oxtail is what you'd expect. Sweet, salty and gelatinous 
Bodega brownie was good. Donut ice creams were creative but missed on flavors
Rum cake was bomb

The food is incredible. It is a great blending of flavors from so many different places. The okra appetizer was amazing. The cocktails are well crafted. It is a great meal.  The server was knowledgeable. The service was good but it took a long time to get our meal. We sat down at 5:15, and the main meal was not served until 6:45. We had finished the appetizers by 6:15. The ambiance is casual. The place was packed and the music is slightly loud, though you can hear. Overall, a fabulous meal.

This is a hard table to get for a reason: It is ABSOLUTELY worth ALL of the accolades. 

Was fortunate to be invited to a Guinness event here, and while most of the menu was specially curated with dishes infused with the beer, there were items like the Honeynut Piri Piri salad that were from the main menu and showed the full breadth of a dining experience at Tatiana. 

And in case being surrounded by the greatest talents in music, dance, and acting in the Lincoln Center and Juilliard vicinity didn't already excite your senses, being served exquisite Afro-Caribbean dishes in a stunning space by a top-tier staff that takes every detail to heart should. Chef Kwame has created a place that feels and tastes like the kind of home where the people are as spicy as the food...and I LOVE it.

Came for the famous ribs, fell in love with the chicken. Tuna and hamachi (appetizers) were decent but not as special as oxtail & crab rangoon. Excellent service. Very cool venue. Loved the cocktails.

I really wanted this restaurant to live up to the hype - and it mostly did. The only drawback was the small space-  between the loud music and conversations it was very hard to hear. Everything tasted great and was well seasoned - but I wouldn't say there was anything I was dying to have again. The two most interesting dishes were the boozy jelly squares and the bodega special dessert- would highly recommend both! The goat patties and the egusi dumplings were great appetizers and the oxtails and pastrami were solid dishes.

Tatiana was rated best restaurant in NYC for a reason and my review reflects that! 

Decor/Ambiance- The restaurant was beautiful on the inside with a modern feel with 90's & early 00's R&B playing through the speakers. The definition of a vibe. 

Reservations- We did a Walk In as an actual reservation is near impossible to get. We arrived at 4:15 on a Thursday and waited 45 minutes until it opened at 5pm. There were 9 people in front of us so we felt confident they could accommodate us. (And we were right, we even got a table!) 

DINNER- PHEW! We started with the Curried Goat Patties (9/10) and they came with mango chutney and another garlic-base sauce that was amazing. Next we got the Black Bean Hummus with Lamb (9/10) which was also our waiter's favorite. AMAZING. Next up Oxtail & Crab Rangoon 8/10. Now onto the main courses. We got the Braised Oxtail (9/10) and the Short Rib Pastrami Suya (7/10). Everything is so well-plated and elegant and the Suya really steals the show in that regard. HOWEVER, flavor wise the Oxtail outshines the Suya and I would recommend that over the Suya but they are both worth trying. 

DESSERT- We started with the Bodega Brownie Special (7/10) which was good but to me it was just an expensive fudge brownie ...it was good but how good can a fudge brownie really be. Lastly, we ended with the Golden Rum Cake (10/10). I only gave out 1 10 in this review because everything was amazing but this cake was definitely deserving....OMG! It's a must when you go.

I'm still shocked that my party of 4 was able to experience this on my recent trip to NYC. Plan was to line up as walk in at 4:15.. we didnt get in line until 4:50 and there was a pretty decent queue. After seeing ppl walk away and hearing a quote of next table at 9pm, we were prepared to get turned away but they said 'if you can be finished by 7pm we can seat you now' (it was 5pm) - heck yes! (So note that ur chances largely depend on your party size- parties of two had it the worst)

Sooo worth the anticipation. We ordered starters of Egusi dumplings (8/10- good but the most mediocre dish of the meal), lamb-topped black hummus which was 10/10, including the Msemen bread that cane with it. Tasted like a croissant, they need to sell that by the bag/loaf lol. Our mains were the short rib pastrami suya and the oxtails. No complaints on either, both a good 9/10 and would get them again. Super flavorful, meats tender and well seasoned. Cocktails were well-made, my spicy margarita was Spicy!! Dessert of cosmic brownie and rum cake were fantastic. 

Restaurant was gorgeous and service was an A+.. even as it approached 7pm and we double checked with the waiter if we were ok to order dessert. He didnt hesitate to ring it up and told us not to rush. Really appreciated that as i know similar hot-spots can be strict. Will definitely return because i need to try that king crab curry and goat patties!

Had a very pleasant evening. Fine dining vibes with hip hop/r&b. All the staff were so nice and professional.  The food tasted very "top chef".

What we ate:

EGUSI DUMPLINGS - how does someone make something so good. This was my favorite dish. 5/5.

OXTAIL & CRAB RANGOON - I worked at 3 Chinese restaurants as a kid. This is the best crab rangoon I've had. 5/5. 

BRAISED OXTAILS - so good. We didn't leave a single piece of meat on the bone. 5/5

SOFRITO ROASTED CHICKEN - very surprised about the generous portion. I wish I could make chicken like this. Almost licked the plate clean. 5/5.

* Chefs kiss *
I must say it is not easy getting a reservation but if you do manage to snag one, definitely go!

Tatiana is one of the most sort out restaurants to get a reservation at and it did not disappoint. My oneeeee takeaway was that although I had a 9:30p reservation, my party and I was not get seated until minutes to 10.

Now! Let's get to the food! We ordered 3 appetizers and two mains and they were all delicious. (I'm terrible at describing real flavor so I won't go there) but, each serving was packed with flavor, the right amount of spice and surprisingly filling despite the portions being on the smaller side.

For starters we had the:
- Egusi Dumplings
- Oxtail & Crab Rangoon
- Curried goat patties 

Mains:
- Braised oxtail 
- Fried Branzino
Both came with a side of rice and peas

Our choice of drink was the Pog nutcracker and it was the best upscale rendition of a NY nutcracker I have ever tasted.  (very well made cocktail)
and for dessert of course we closed out with the bodega special !

Would I go back again absolutely, am I in a rush to play hunger games again for a reservation no.  But it's definitely an experience and if you can make your way there I do recommend you do so!

I'll start off by saying-- I do believe the hype is real and I really enjoyed my experience here. Was definitely worth the price and the wait, and I would recommend to others. That being said, I'm happy just having experienced it once and probably wouldn't go through the effort of getting in again haha. 

To start off with, in order to have a chance of getting a walk in seat (I gave up on Resy), you need to be there at least half an hour before opening. The line starts outside-- don't make the same mistake I did and wait in the wrong place lol. My favorite dish of the night was probably the curry goat puffs. The flavor of the curry with the sweetness of the chutney, the green sauce, and a hint of their house-made hot sauce? Perfection. Absolute must-order. The fried okra I enjoyed but could probably skip.

Entrees were bigger than I expected; the pastrami and oxtail were both delicious. Of course I also had to get the bodega special for dessert. Ice cream donuts had the exact flavor of powdered donuts and idk how they did it, but the texture almost mimicked the texture of donuts as well. Brownie was warm and yummy. For service, our waitress was really sweet and the overall vibes were just very cool. Drinks were decent (nothing particularly noteworthy; got the nutcracker which basically tasted like elevated apple juice lol). Don't overlook the Jell-O shots (weren't on the regular menu for some reason, had to ask for them), which were absolutely gorgeous.

This is not the #1 restaurant in NYC, not by a long shot. I thought the appetizers were good, not spectacular. For entrees we ordered the mushrooms with scallion pancakes for ~$56, and the wagyu short rib pastrami for ~$86, and after a few bites I decided I would never return here. I wanted to like this place a lot and was warned not to feed into the hype. I'll happily pay $300+ for a date night but this just wasn't worth it. 

I should've listened to my friend Leo.

I came in wanting to love it. But honestly the food just want anything special for the price. Unfortunately the marketing and hype just don't add up here. There are far too many options in NYC for this to be anywhere within the realm of worthwhile.

Food was very good overall. Not sure if would rush back due the the prices. But its definitely a good idea for a fun date night or special occasion. We did have a delay with one of our entrees but we were comped an appetizer for the wait. Very good experience

When looking for a top tier restaurant where the personalized staff service is outstanding, the cuisine is filled with food selections cooked in succulent spices and aromatics that awaken your pallet which can be paired with an amazing cocktail selection. The ambiance makes you feel comfy and elegant all at the same time. The location is fabulous as you are right in the middle of NYC at the Lincoln center plaza with views of creative sculptures 
TATIANA is definitely where you want to be.
Interesting concepts throughout the restaurant menu and space. Great services throughout the meal.

4.5 stars rounded up to 5. The only half star off is because I thought that dessert was not that great here.

This was seriously one of the best meals I've had in NYC. Vegetarians and vegans beware, this is not the restaurant for you as the meat is the star of the show here. Getting a reservation here is difficult but not impossible. They also take walk-ins, so even if you don't have a reservation, you could just go wait outside the restaurant before they open to ensure that you get to eat here. My friend and I had a reservation but also the first couple in the walk-in line literally got sat at a table right behind us like basically at the same time. 

The decorations give it a cool swanky vibe, service was stellar and the silverware and tableware definitely made you feel like you were eating at a fancy restaurant, which it is! I ended up paying $150 for my portion to eat here, but it was worth it. If I were to go again, I would for sure get the curried goat patties, honeynut piri piri salad, and braised oxtails. Everything else that I tried here was just okay (egusi dumplings, oxtail and crab rangoon, and short rib pastrami suya, cheesecake). Though, I did really enjoy the bread that came with the short rib pastrami lol. Really, the ultimate star of the show was the braised oxtail! Such rich meat that melts in your mouth. One bite of this and I was like this sole dish is the reason why I cannot be a vegetarian. Dessert was a bit of a letdown here though; the cheesecake was very pretty but didn't blow my mind.

I highly recommend you dine here at least once, you can't go wrong with the braised oxtails!!! It's a bit of a pricey meal but it's worth it for a once in a while splurge!!!

I loved the food! The chef is amazing. They check off most of the boxes like food, ambiance location except I don't understand how you can hire such untrained staff. This is my 2nd time here and although my sever today was better than the first time we went, I felt like I came to a diner. That's how their service is. First time was a disaster the server was worse than soho house. And today this guy gave us the wrong menu and acted like we weren't making any sense and not even a sorry gave you the wrong menu..instead acted like I should be glad he gave me one correct menu. Just makes no sense. Plz train ur staff if you wanna have an upscale restaurant to ensure the service is atleast above average otherwise your prices and scarcity make no sense! Giving 3.5 stars for service.

If you are fortunate enough to get a reservation know you're in for the best food you've ever ordered. The food is indescribable. Every single option is better than the last. The flavors are perfection. From the second you enter be ready for an exceptional food experience.

Who got in as a walk in? This girl! 
Besides the luck with a bucket of heavenly blessing it took to get in, I had a great time interacting with some of the kindest staff in the business and meeting new folks at the restaurant. My favorite dish was the mushrooms and scallion pancakes. BOMB! The goat and oxtails were fabulous as well. Fried branzino surprised me... I enjoyed it and I don't think I've ever had branzino fried, nor would that be the first way I would choose to have it prepped. It's geared for sharing so go with someone you actually like that can eat all the foods so you can just enjoy. Cocktails were solid. We skipped dessert because we were so full from the food. And we enjoyed the spring patio space. Super cute. Also, their playlist has all the vibes. Would I return? Certainly! Would I wait in line for hours... No. But I live in Brooklyn so take that with a grain of salt I guess lol.

Second time coming here and it was amazing as expected. First of all, the host Caitlyn - exceptional. Came with a friend to try our luck before the opera and they capped the line just as we were next. We pushed our luck, and by the grace of God (and Caitlyn we got in lol) everything from the service, to the food, to the atmosphere was 10/10. Tried the curry goat "patties", okra, and rangoons to start and split an oxtail as a main. Cosmic brownie as the dessert. Damn, it was good. All of it. Didn't buy drinks, but they looked tasty as well. Check out the food pics attached and try to grab a Resy, or try your luck like we did. I suggest getting there by 4pm to have a chance at the first come first serve seating. They open at 5pm. You won't regret the wait ;)

After two years of trying I finally got reservations to Tatiana.  Was it worth the wait?  No.  It is creative Caribbean food.  I would give it a B.  The mushrooms large plate was tasty.  The goat patties were average.  The fish was fair.  Service was good.  The room is noisy, but comfortable.

The food was served fresh and hot out of the kitchen. Service was very Attentive  and Professional. The atmosphere was relaxed with a classy vibe. I would highly recommend going here if given the opportunity.
Fresh with a generous portion (enough for me and my granddaughter) the chocolate cake is addicting

I think the food is average tasting , small portions and very pricey but the drinks were delicious! 
The service was excellent and the ambience was inviting.

Was Tatiana an incredible meal? Absolutely. Is it the #1 restaurant in New York? I don't think so. 

A 4.5 is closer to my true rating here.

I stopped in on a Tuesday off of a lucky 5:45 PM reservation. We were greeted and brought two complimentary glasses of wine for a special occasion (definitely a plus here).

We ordered the Egusi Dumplings, Goat Patties, Braised Oxtail and bodega special.


Egusi Dumplings: 5/5, though felt a bit light on the filling
Goat Patties: 5/5, best dish we had. Mango chutney was great.
Braised Oxtail: 3/5. Honestly pretty disappointed with this one. The oxtail wasn't particularly tender and the sauce quickly congealed into a sticky mess.
Bodega Special: 4/5. Nothing crazy - just a brownie and some ice cream. Did enjoy it though.

It was a tad off putting how loud the interior of the restaurant was, but no major complaints.

I don't think Tatiana is worth fighting for a super hard reservation or waiting in line for hours for, but if you get lucky it's definitely worth going.

Loved Tatiana! My favorites were the goat patties and the dumplings. The meat inside the patties were so tender and went so well with the mango chutney. The oxtail main dish did not stand out to me as I had hoped, but was still great and a pleasure to eat! The Bodega Special was also a nice treat. 

Overall, I would love to come back to try the other appetizers or the Short Rib. Service was great too, they served us free glasses of champagne for our anniversary. The only complaint would be that the music was a tiny bit too loud :(

Would love to come back if I can get another reservation!

Tatiana 2023 New York's Most Hyped Restaurant Super Favorite
Tatiana by Kwame Onwuachi
10 Lincoln Center Plaza, New York, NY 10023
 100+ per person
Tatiana, one of the hardest restaurants to book in New York, walkin with difficulty, hit the spot! Located inside Lincoln Center, the decor is super beautiful!
The food is North African/Caribbean flavors and each dish is special and delicious :
CRISPY OKRA fried okra, honey and mustard seasoning is delicious and not too greasy!
 CURRIED GOAT PATTIES Lamb stuffed dumplings with green/mango/chili sauce (quite spicy).
 BLACK BEAN HUMMUS with a perfect shortbread, hummus topped with lamb mince, savory and fragrant!
 SHORT RIB PASTRAMI SUYA (cover photo) a must!!! Wagyu Short Rib (bacon version) with buns and purple cabbage, the waiter said we were actually allowed to assemble this set by ourselves, and it was really good!!!! The bacon was not salty at all, it was soft and flavorful, and the cabbage was sweet and sour and refreshing!!!!
 Dessert Cosmic Brownie + Powdered Donut Ice Cream This dessert was also amazing! The ice cream was in the shape of a donut and also flavored with donut, and then the brownie was a copy of the cosmic brownie that Americans used to eat when they were kids, so full of creativity!

The menu is very short, I guess it's a random point not to step on mine kind of, is I will come back to two brush three brush restaurant, really like it!

Let me preface this review by saying I debated for a while how many stars to give this restaurant and I think 3 is the right amount. 

The star deduction is driven by a few factors. First, there was a LONGGGG wait between our small plates and our large plates. It completely disrupted the flow of dinner, and I got bored sitting at the table for that long. Second, the music is entirely too loud. I'm in my 20s and love a nice vibe and music. But after screaming across the table for 30 ish min, my throat started to hurt. My husband and I probably said what to each other more than 50 times.  There's a difference between music creating a nice ambiance and music destroying any possibility for conversation. Third, some of the dishes weren't good. The okra small plate was nearly inedible. How can you mess up okra? For dessert, we got the bodega special which is their take on a cosmic brownie with ice cream that is shaped like powered donuts. It was just ok. Nothing to write home about. 

With that said, our server was very nice. And we loved the oxtail/crab Rangoon small plate and the branzino large plate. My husband liked the oxtail large plate, but I wasn't a fan.

All in all, I won't be back, and I don't quite understand why it's rated #1 on the New York Times list

Have been struggling to get a reservation but dying to visit. So we arrived on a weekday right at 5 pm to stand in line and get a table as a walk in. Service was great.
