Menu doesn't have a lot of options but more than enough and the flavors vary drastically. We tried 2 appetizers, 3 entrees and 1 dessert plus we all tried different specialty cocktails. Everything was great. Favorite items were the curried goat patties and the short rib pastrami suya. Understand why people love this spot so much. The menu is very unique.

The food is amazing from start to finish! We walked in as a table for 2 on a random Friday night around 8:30pm and was seated 10 minutes later! Was prepared for a much longer wait so that was a pleasant surprise since it's mission impossible to get a reservation. Highlights for me include the short rib suya that is flavored to the gods and was melt in your mouth and the goat curry patties with their perfect crust. The prices are a little outrageous for the amount of food you get, for instance I thought they were really cheap with the amount of meat included in said patties but the food is so good I'll let it slide lol. Cocktails were also a vibe; I'm really enjoyed the Pog nutcracker which tasted like a tropical fruit dream. Overall a great experience and definitely worth the hype.

Tatiana is an absolute gem of a dining experience. The decor is tasteful and sophisticated with a modern blend of music. The service was amazing and each dish was better than expected. A fabulous dining experience. I def plan on coming back!

I can't give this place enough stars! The food was amazing. My favorites were the okra and oxtails.

The drinks weren't good. It was a shame that great food wasn't paired with great drinks. 

I'll try to return here on every NYC visit.

The venue is nice. Inside is a modern flare look. The staff here are true professionals (front and rear of the restaurant). The food is seasoned just right! The bar tender was putting his foot in those libations! More please! The only issue for me was the curried king crab dish. I was given only one roti to sop up all that magnificent curry sauce. I asked for one more roti to finish the job. Please remember this. The larger dishes are meant to be shared. One roti is not enough. Also, there should be a little more crab legs. I was charged $10 for one roti. I believe that two roti (minimum) should accompany the curried king crab dish. I will return to try out other dishes. If you're in the area. GET SOME!!!!

Fabulous delicious and creative food 
The service is wonderful and warm. Christian was amazing!!! Great recommendations, funny and a pleasure. 
My only minor comment is that the music was a bit loud.

I went to Tatiana a few weeks ago with a friend. I was excited to try the restaurant, as it has been lauded by critics. We walked in and were put on the waitlist. The wait wasn't that long, but the hosts forgot about us on the waitlist and skipped over us for 1-2 parties, which was a little annoying.

The restaurant is beautifully decorated, with a nice and open layout. The service was good.

I tried the following dishes:

Egusi Dumplings (Jonah Crab, Nigerian Red Stew, Pickled Pearl Onion) (2.5/5): I did not love these. The mix of flavors wasn't my favorite, and the crab was a little dry. I definitely would not order this again.

Honeynut Piri Piri Salad (Persian Cucumber, Seasonal Grapes, Crispy Quinoa) (4/5): Probably the best thing I tried. The produce was really fresh, and it all went nicely with the piri piri sauce.

Fried Branzino (Rice and Peas, Cilantro, Onion) (4/5) A nice dish. The branzino was tasty, and it went nicely with the accompanying rice, which was good on its own.

Sofrito Roasted Chicken (Sazon Tomato Stew, Gordal and Castelvetrano Olives, Tarragon) (3.5/5): The chicken was decent. Cooked nicely, not dry, but honestly not the most memorable.

Bodega Special (Cosmic Brownie, Powdered Sugar Donut Ice Cream, Sorrel) (4/5): A good brownie and good ice cream.

Icee Cart (Mango Sorbet, Cherry Granita, Vanilla Curd) (2.5/5): I wanted to like this because I love icees, but it was just okay. The presentation was poor, and it wasn't memorable.

Overall, I had just an okay experience at Tatiana. I was hoping for a lot more given all of the hype, but I was left wanting. I don't see myself returning anytime soon.

I dined solo at Tatiana and had a wonderful experience. Although the restaurant opens at 5:00 PM, I arrived at 3:30 PM because I work across the street from Lincoln Center and didn't want to take any chances. I was the first in line, but it started to grow around 4:15 PM, likely slower because it was a Wednesday.

The decor is lovely, and I was seated at the bar, which was a bit tight but not uncomfortable. I started with the crispy okra, which was heavenly--perfectly seasoned and not spicy at all. For my main course, I had the braised oxtail, which was also heavenly and very filling. Dessert was a delicious white chocolate cheesecake (pictured below).

Overall, it was a great experience, enhanced by singing along to Mary J. Blige's music playing in the background. Tatiana is on the expensive side, so I recommend going for a special occasion or if you really want to treat yourself.

Brunch ain't it. I came here for the mothers day brunch hoping it'd be just as good as the dinner reviews were. A couple of mistakes were made. 
1. The prefix menu was not given ahead of time nor was there a a second option for those with allergic to shrimp (my mom loves grits but it had shrimp imbedded in it)
2. It was more Black Southern Food which I love, but where was the ackee/saltfish (Carribbean) and bread/porrodge (Afro). The menu option felt rushed.
3. The food preparation was not consistent, my puffs were overfried but the table across had light brown fluffy ones *side eye*

I gave this restaurant a five cause I went to the dinner for my bday and it was AMAZING. I sat outside since I was a walk-in. Waited 2hr!! But it was worth it. Also free dessert for your bday this place gets an A+++. The servers were amazingly sweet too. Dem Oxtails....no words you must try on on your own. Lastly the fried okra was an unexpected star, the perfect snack if packaging.

Also appetizers need to come out hot like the entrees. Warm those plates.

Aimed to obtain a reservation and to no avail.
First time we went and joined the line for bar seating; we just missed the first seating cutoff.
We arrived earlier another day (4:15 PM) and we made the first bar seating. The lighting was superb; music called for a dance floor to work off all you will consume.
Seated at the bar (met a couple from Toronto while on line); we shared reviews.The cuisine from the presentation to the popping flavors was delightful. Go, order and savor the flavors. Next time, the oxtail  is on my mind.Two small plates to wet our plates of rangoons and empanadas. We shared the branzino. I primarily consumed the okra. I even offered some to a single diner just next to us; due to the quantity provided.
Excellent service and the food!! Chefs kiss. Visiting came with friends definitely will return!

Waiting in line in the sun for over an hour to get in was a bit much.  Sitting facing the glass window was not ideal but the rest was everything.  The okra and branzino were incredible as was the rum cake.  The rice that came with the branzino was divine.  The lady next to me had the empanadas and let me try which was equally good.  I also enjoyed the rum cake.  What made the evening extra special was the privilege of having Christian as my server.  He  made it that much more special.  I unknowingly also got to meet Chef Kwame.  What a nice soul!

Was super excited to get a reservation for Tatiana but I do think the hype may have set too high of a bar. It was good and I think it's a fun place for a date/special occasion -- but I don't think you need to rush here/wait hours/buy a reservation. 

Tatiana has a fun vibe which definitely got us excited for the meal. The service wasn't the best though. Our waitress was a little rude to us (got sassy when i asked about their non-alcoholic drinks) and wasn't at attentive as she was to the table next to us. She wiped down their table, changed their plates/silverware and told them the specials -- but didn't do that for us.

Food-wise: There were some hits and some that were disappointing. We loved the oxtail and the cheesecake dessert. Definitely our favorites of the night. My husband and I were split on the curried goat patties and the dumplings -- I thought the patties were great but you have to get everything in one bite. The dumplings were just ok to me. 

The biggest disappointment was the pastrami suya. Katz's pastrami is wayyy better and jucier . The meat here was dry. The bread was nice and fluffy but I wish there were more of it (definitely not enough to make sandwiches with all the meat.)

Overall, would give Tatiana a smidge under 4 stars. Would recommend trying once but no need to hurry back or kill yourself trying to get a resy.

Tatiana was first brought to my attention by one of my friends - she had heard great things about it and really wanted to check it out. Trying new restaurants is kind of our thing, so when she suggested we go together it look little convincing to get me on board. This proved easier said than done, however, as Tatiana has been ranked first in NYT's list of best resaurants in NYC two years in a row. As such, there is much hype surrounding this restaurant and it's difficult to secure a reservation. After multiple attempts, my friend snagged a 5:15pm table on a Monday - and since there's never not a good night to go out to eat, we headed over after work. 

Tatiana is chef Kwame Onwuachi's "love letter to New York City", and as such incorporates elements of the cuisine he grew up on in the Bronx: Afro-Caribbean at its core with some city-specific flair (see: dessert). As if I wasn't excited already to dine here, him being from the Bronx only made my anticipation grow. Anyway, the restaurant is located in the heart of Lincoln Center - no really, it's located in David Geffen Hall; kinda hard to spot as the exterior blends into its surroundings, but not invisible. When we arrived we were greeted by a line of people waiting to get in, however these were walk-ins so we walked right in and were led to our table. I really liked the decor - there's a good amount of seating in relation to the size of the dining room, large windows to let light in, and subtle earth tones with accents throughout the space that really added to the aesthetics. 

Before anything, we started with drinks. We had two rounds - I started with the Pog Nutcracker and then had the Suntory Time. Both were delicious - super smooth with great flavor. As far as food, they don't have a large menu - there's only two sections and everything is meant to be shared (hence the section names "Small Shares" and "Large Shares"). In line with what was described, the menu consists of mostly Afro-Caribbean fare that has been modernized/elevated. Our server suggested that we order two to three Small Shares and two Large Shares - so that's what we did. For smalls we got the curried goat patties, oxtail and crab rangoon, and honeynut piri piri salad. For larges, we got the shawarma roasted chicken and the short rib pastrami suya. 

So in general, all of the food was delicious. Before any of the food came, our server placed a sauce on the table and recommend we put it on everything. - I did dab it on a few things but was very sparse as it was quite spicy (it was good nonetheless). For our smalls, my favorite was by far were the curried goat patties; they had an interesting flavor and came with a really tasty sauce - I didn't expect to like them so much. The rangoon were the weakest IMO, and the salad was light with a refreshing flavor. 

Both of the mains we got were excellent; the chicken was liberally seasoned, had great flavor, and was paired with a generous helping of white and hot sauces. The dish also came with a side of turmeric lamb rice which was delicious. I'm still thinking about how juicy and well-seasoned that chicken was - mmmm yes. The short rib pastrami was awesome, one of the best dishes I've had in a long time. The meat was super super tender - like pull away with a fork tender, the red cabbage and sauce it was paired with were the perfect complements, and the caraway coco bread it came with was super soft. I'm going to be thinking about this dish for a long time - truly great stuff. 

Dessert is really where I saw more of the NYC vibes kick in - we decided to get two: the Bodega Special and the Icee Cart. The former is what I've seen splashed all over social media: his take on a cosmic brownie and powdered doughnuts. The brownie was rich (but not overly rich), but the real star were the doughnuts - which was in fact powdered doughnut-flavored ice cream. I was floored by this - I couldn't believe how close the flavor of the ice cream was to actual powdered doughnuts. Credit to Kwame and team for achieving this. The Icee Cart was a refreshing finish - mango sorbet, cherry granita, and vanilla curd. They were bold flavors that worked well together and contrasted the relative richness of the Bodega. Both desserts were super creative. 

Service was excellent; we were taken care of by Mio (not sure how to spell his name), who guided us through the menu and made sure we were taken care of. You would expect a restaurant of this caliber to be stuffy, but everyone was super chill and friendly. Overall, Tatiana was an excellent experience and worth the hype. Food, service, and atmosphere were all slammin' - the work to get a table here is definitely worth it.

This was an excellent dining experience. From the moment we walked in until we walked out I had a great time.  We had a reservation for 5pm on Friday. We did not have to be seated. They do have you wait if your entire party has not arrived. 

We ordered the Oxtail and Crab Rangoon, the Curried Goat Empanadas and  Egusi Dumplings for appetizers. 
The Oxtail and Crab Rangoon were amazing. They had hints of the crab and oxtail. They were crispy with a creamy burst of filling. It was small 10/10. 
The Curried Goat Empanadas were delicious. Flaky crusts, gave way to tender curry goat filling. They were served with a mango chutney and green sauce.  Eaten either way 10/10. The Egusi Dumplings were ok, I mostly tasted the spice. 7/10. 
We ordered the Braised Oxtail, Short Rib Pastrami Suya and Shawarma Roasted Chicken. 
The Braised Oxtails are the star. They were succulent, tender, with a slightly sweet sauce served with glorious rice and peas. 10/10
The Short Rib Pastrami Suya comes with sliced pastrami, red cabbage and coco bread to cut into little sliders with a peanut sauce. It was also tender and packed many flavors that worked well together. 9/10
The Shawarma Roasted Chicken was roasted just right. It was juicy and seasoned well. 8/10

For dessert we ordered the Harlem Chocolate Factory Cheesecake. It was very good, but not special. Tasted like regular cheesecake with a chocolate coating and caramel sauce. 6/10. 

The servers were attentive. Water glasses were always full and all requests were honored quickly. 

The ambiance was amazing. It is a beautiful open space layout. The music was great and loud, however, my table could hear each other when speaking.

It is a place to see and been seen, the evening we went we saw a famous comedian and an iconic basketball player's wife.

The food here was very good; the mushroom entree and all the breads were delicious. 

But at a price point this high -- and it is extremely expensive-- the service should be impeccable. Instead it was inept, clueless and unhelpful from start to finish. One example: our server had no idea what was in the hummus, nor did he seem to understand our questions about how to make it vegetarian. (It was resolved but not after having an unfriendly, painful five minute conversation.) It's a small menu and there's no excuse to not know it from back to front, and if there are questions or concerns, you should approach those with an enthusiastic effort to help and a clear answer once you find out. The folks who brought the food could not be understood, both because of the noise level and their soft voices. None of them smiled once. 

For as much as we paid, the service should have been professional, friendly and beyond accommodating. It was none of that. I get better service at my local diner. Not going back.
Loved the okra, the music was fantastic, service was excellent. Highly recommend to anyone in the area.

We came on a Saturday night at 5 (with reservations). Note: there is a separate line for diners who have reservations. The hostess was extremely friendly. Our waitress was Beatrice who was very patient and provided helpful recommendations. The food.... was subpar. Lacking in flavor in ways I cannot explain. I wish I had a better experience but unfortunately I cannot subscribe to the hype. As mentioned in other posts, the price point is not justified.

It was my wife birthday & we had an elegant time .The restaurant decor was amazing , the atmosphere was priceless , music  was definitely on point . As for the food it was amazing , nice texture , delicious spices and me and my wife will definitely visit this  establishment again . My wife love the drinks which was hitting and I must say the kitchen smell was off the radar

If you love spice & spicy food, this place is for you. The amount of flavor in each dish is amazing. Make sure to ask for their house sauce if you LOVE hot sauce. The desserts here are to die for - tbh I'm not a big dessert person but the desserts here changed my mind. 

Great food, great service, great ambiance

My son who lives in NY was able to get us a 5:15 PM reservation on a Friday. The ambiance had a nice cool vibe. The service was great in all aspects. we had no issues and everyone from our server to the managers was friendly and helpful. I saw reviews that said the music was too loud but I guess they addressed that by the time we went. 

The food was very good. we had the curry goat patties, the oxtail and crab rangoon, short rib pastrami, braised oxtails and fried branzino. The curry goat patties were perfectly flavored. There's 3 to an order. the rangoon was good but it's a pretty small bite. we all had one each. the short rib pastrami and fried branzino were amazing. the pastrami was so tender and melts in your moth. some of the best beef I've ever had. The branzino was delicious. perfectly cooked. there is a sauce on it I would opt to get on the side next time. I wasn't a huge fan of the oxtails. everybody else at the table liked them.

All in all Tatiana lived up to the hype.

spontaneously got a reservation for 4 on a friday which was very clutch - thanks tatiana team and resy for making it happen! after hearing so many good things we needed to try

came at 5:30pm on a saturday and it was decently crowded. the music was a little too loud where it was hard to hear your own voice unfortunately. 

food wise - everything was so delicious and amazing. we got a ton of stuff to share: the egusi dumplings, curry puff with goat, pastrami, and cosmic brownie. our waitress did a poor job of explaining the portions - so we were a group of 4 but all small plates came with three items. even the waitress said she recommends to share but like - with small portions? didnt like that

otherwise the food was SOO good omg. the flavors were there and the quality was stunning. i loved everything - the dumplings were saucy, the curry puffs were savory and juicy with the meat, and the pastrami was also juicy. the chef came out to explain to us how to eat the pastrami and whats recommended and the actual flavors the food is made of. so good and so cool!! 

the cosmic brownie was a fun icing on the cake. it was a friends bday and i was shocked they disnt comp the dessert since a restaurant like this has nothing to lose but it is what it is

would totally recommend and come back

Great location, interior vibe and ambiance is classy and immaculate. I walked in without a reservation and was able to get seated about 1.5hrs later which is no surprise for a place like this where reservations are highly recommended. I got the curried goat patties which were cooked to perfection. Meat was full of flavor and the mango chutney was to die for. I also got the non alcoholic beverage with orange, passion, and guava which paired perfectly with all the dishes. To finish of the night, i got the bodega desert which consisted of a house made cosmic brownie and ice cream donuts. Presentation was great but the taste of the brownie was a little over cooked. Service was great as waiters would check on you in a timely manner. Overall this place cost a about a $100. I would come back here again if celebrating something but its not my top choice.

Is this place worth the hype, Yes. I'll be honest, getting a reservation was not easy and it's not cheap either. But I very much enjoyed my meal and the ambience. Ordered the crispy okra and the curried goat patties. My first impression was how flavorful the spices were in both these dishes.  For entrees we shared the infamous short rib pastrami suya, it was the best pastrami sandwich ever. Then the Braised oxtail which was even better, this was my favorite dish of the night. The sticky sauce and the tender meat was out of this world delicious!!! Finished off with the Instagram worthy "Bodega Special" The faux doughnut, actually made out of ice cream and the decedent brownie were both very delicious. Lastly we tried all 3 Jello shots. I don't really love the texture of Jello but decided to try them anyways. The texture I still didn't love, but the sophisticated flavors with herbs and fruit made it worth while.
Overall great meal, I can't wait to try this place again, if we can get another reservations, hahahaha!

Pretty unique restaurant with flavors I am personally unfamiliar with. If you are interested in trying new flavor palettes or if you're familiar with Afro-Caribbean dishes, this place is the way to go!

We got the curried goat patties to start and the patties were STUFFED. The patty itself was super crispy and flaky, and the goat filling was so juicy and tender. This does have a hint of game if you are not a fan, but worth getting.

The egusi dumplings were good but quite pricey for the portion. We got three dumplings for around $20.

We then got the braised oxtail (my favorite dish) and it came with a side of rice. The sauce was HEAVEN and the meat fell off the bone. We mixed it with the rice and it was so good.

We got the pastrami suya which actually was my least favorite because 1. super pricey and 2. kinda dry even with the sauce that came with it. I would skip this dish.

We then got cosmic brownies and it paired well with the doughnut ice cream. The ice cream tasted exactly like the powdered doughnuts and is reminiscent of my childhood.

Definitely unique flavors and I would go back

Phenomenal!!!!! I see why it's the best restaurant in NYC AND why people stand in line for it. My friend snagged a reservation, so I had to go.

For the appetizers, we had the egusi dumplings, curried goat patties, oxtail and crab Rangoon, tuna kifto, and piri piri salad.

The salad was cool but it was more of a concept of a salad. But the oxtail and crab Rangoon almost made me cry with how good it was. Same with the curried goat patties and egusi dumplings. He's done a really great job at fusing cultures.

The short rib suya?!?!? I closed my eyes. It melts in your mouth. 12/10. We also had the bodega special, and it's so cool how he makes the ice cream into donuts. My favorite was the cheesecake.

I can't wait to go back!

For NYT's #1 spot in NYC - this place fell SHORT. Or NYT is going to crap; both are probably true

Was lucky to only have waited an hour for a walk-in, but would not re-visit even if a reservation fell into my lap. Didn't find anything to be upset about with the food, but also was not really impressed with any dish. Felt that the flavors were largely muted and the restaurant was afraid to make any bold statements on anything. Prices are typical of fine dining, but imo there are lots of other fine dining places to either 1) come out feeling more full; 2) feel like the chef taught you something new regarding flavor profiles, cuisines, etc; 3) any of the above. Alternatively - go to any one of the hundreds of non-fine dining restaurants and actually have a better time. 

Candidly, my experience was also colored by really rude service. Completely deadpan attitude; didn't write down our orders and ended up having to come back twice to clarify; noticeable change in behavior and attitude if we didn't order enough food, drinks, or refused dessert ($20 for a Little Debbie's brownie - was I being pranked?). Came around when we had 2 bites left in the short rib dish to ask 'why we weren't using the bread and making a sandwich out of the meat as the chef intended'...probably because no one actually bothered to tell us that.

Ignoring that, this would still only be a 7.5/10, 8 on a generous day. Don't waste your time or money if you care about either. If you don't, keep refreshing those Resy's just to tell everyone that you've been to the top restaurant in NYC.

Three of us tried to get a reservation as soon as they opened to no avail.  So it being a Saturday, we decided to get there 2 hours prior to opening., we were first in line and knew that they will not seat parties greater than 2 at the bar.  That said, when the walk in line was finally allowed in, we were made to wait an additional 10 minutes while parties behind us in line were allowed in.  When we finally were seated on the patio, I failed to understand why we were made to wait that additional time when we obviously were going to be seated out there from the beginning.  And, having waited the two hours with an immobilizer boot on, it would have been nice to be seated in a timely manner. The service was excellent and the food and drinks great but be prepared for  entrees with hefty prices with small portion size not warranting them.  One experience is enough

The food is absolutely amazing. You can't go wrong with anything that you choose. The service was excellent. The vibe is very cool with music playing overhead. I HIGHLY recommend and it will exceed your expectations.

Food and service were pretty good overall. I definitely prefer the appetizers more than the entrees. I love the music they were playing - good 90s and early 2000s throwbacks. I would go again to try the other dish. 

Appetizer/Small Plates Ordered: 
- Crispy Okra 
- Egusi Dumplings
- Curry Lamb Patties

Large/entrees 
- Braised oxtails - giant oxtails; super tender 
- Short Rib Pastrami Suya- good but nothing special. I wouldn't get it again (imo slightly overpriced) 

Dessert
- Bodega Special - great way to end the meal

You know how airport food has a big disconnect with the prices they charge and the food's quality? That's Tatiana, except Tatiana takes the cake.  

Make no mistake though, the food is indeed good. But at $50+ on average for a main and $20+ for an appetizer, I expected better and thought I would learn something new. Furthermore, service was shockingly bad and inconsistent. We had some wait staff that were cordial, but our primary waitress gave us an attitude straight from the start. 

I would happily pay up if the food was really out of this world, but at the current quality of food and service Tatiana does not deserve its price point and the hype. I probably would only go back if I were starving or forced to - just like with airport vendors.

Had the pleasure of dining at Tatiana's a few days ago for my husband's birthday! He was looking forward to trying one of their signature dishes- the infamous oxtails! This restaurant didn't disappoint! There were so many delicious items on the menu that making choices was difficult! The oxtail patties are a must as well as the pastrami- so many dishes to try and enjoy, and the cocktails didn't disappoint! The restaurant has a lot of energy and the buzz was positive. Special thank you to the manager Jake Myers whose professionalism made the evening that more special! Tatiana is a must if you are seeking a Caribean/African experience in New York City!!

First time at this highly hyped hot new-ish restaurant. Short version - definitely worth the visit.
Long version: Is it, in fact, the best restaurant in NYC?  I mean that's a really tough judgment to make - there are so many really fabulous spots. This is up there among the top tier though for sure. Our server was super nice, friendly, eager to offer  advice. Service was a little on the slower side though. We probably would have ordered a couple more drinks if we were checked on a little more - by the time we were checked on, it was a little too late in the meal for us to embark on another round. Our second app took a long long time to come out - long enough that we started to so wonder if there was a mix up.  But those were small things - and the main reason we were there (the food) was overall exceptional. We got the goat patties and the rangoon, both which were unbelievably delicious (close your eyes and savor kind of delicious.) Well balanced flavors, tender filling in the patties which were literally melt in your mouth. Oxtails for dinner equally a must order, fall off the bone tender and seasoned impeccably. The cheesecake for dessert was a great finish. Shrimp was a bit of a miss unfortunately, slightly overcooked so not as succulent as I had hoped. The sauce though was excellent. For two people, they advise 2 apps, and 2 mains, but I think with a heavier main like the oxtails, one main , 2 apps, 1 dessert is perfect. Now to the really important info: Because I did an extensive Google search with really confusing and contradictory info, on how to actually get to eat here given how difficult it is to get a res, I'm sharing my hard researched info to hopefully help others to get to experience this fabulous meal.
Sent hubs to stand in line for a Friday res. He got there around 4:15 pm, there were about 30 people in front of him. At 5 pm, someone from the restaurant took the first 10 or so people in for immediate seating. There was about a 20 minute pause where nothing happened (presumably because they were getting everyone settled and their actual reservations seated. Then someone came out again and started handing out time slots to come back for either bar or outdoor seating (you don't get to choose, it's whatever is open.) With the 30 people in front of him (less parties since he said he was the only person who came alone for the line (sorry!!!) he was given a time at 5:45 of 7-7:45 to come back. So any time during that slot. We came back at 7:30 and were seated within 5-10 minutes at the bar (the people in front of him got the patio - so just chance where you end up.)  So yes, super hard to get a reservation, but definitely doable to come and eat here if you want to. 
Overall a great place, will be a place we return even with the extra effort required.

This restaurant was phenomenal . The service was impeccable, the vibes were chill and the food was out of this world. Everything was made to perfection. The curry goat patties the oxtail and crab appetizers oh so good. The braised oxtail was delightful, the curry crab was delish and the pastrami was butter soft. The bodega brownie and rum cake delish. Ate too much. Definitely have to go running tomorrow. A 5 star review from me and my fam today.

Very underwhelming food for a place that is named the "best restaurant in NYC". I waited ~40 minutes in line prior to opening, and we got seated in the first round (but still around 5:20pm, as they stagger seatings). A little bit before opening, a server comes out to offer POG juice to all those waiting in line, which was much appreciated in the humid NYC summer heat.

We ordered the egusi dumpling, curried goat patties, braised oxtails, and short rib pastrami suya to share for the two of us. Honestly the concept of all these dishes is inventive and unique, but they all just seemed to miss. 

1. The egusi dumpling tasted somewhat raw. 
2. The curried goat patties were good but nothing special. 
3. The braised oxtails were probably out favorite dish but the presentation of this caught us off guard - why would you serve this in a huge crockpot and only fill half of the pot with oxtails and five pieces of vegetables? And the sauce was overly sticky which created a slightly burnt taste on the oxtails. 
4. Short rib pastrami suya was our least favorite. Everything about this dish was too salty, and the bread was weirdly sweet and not soft. 

We had originally wanted to order their dessert, but we were too full, and also too disappointed to want to try. 

Obviously this is NYC's top restaurant so I would still recommend giving it a shot, but we were pretty underwhelmed.

*Experience: We were able to get last minute reservations for a party of 5 and was seated immediately upon arrival. The ambiance of the restaurant was relaxing and the music selection was great! Servers were attentive and friendly. 

*Food: We ordered - 
- Rainbow jelly shots - very pretty with gold dust and fun. But not a "to-die for" item. 

Small shares 
- egusi dumplings
- crispy okra  
- black bean hummus 
- curry goat patties: these were basically empanadas 

Large shares 
- take-out mushrooms - my vegetarian friend loved this. Good variety of mushroom selection. 
- short rib pastrami suya: definitely the highlight of the meal where everything just melts in your mouth! 
- brown stew chicken; very juicy chicken that we basically packed to go. My friend reheated it the next day and the quality was still there! 

Dessert: 
- Bodega Special 
- black coffee: really good quality brewed coffee!

I thought the food was overall good, but not great.

I was surprised to hear this restaurant is called the best in NYC. I thought all the food was good, but I didn't love anything. We waited in line for the bar/outdoor patio seating so I'll start with our experience doing that.

We got in line at 4:30 p.m. on a Tuesday. There were about 15 people in line in front of us. Luckily we heard the outdoor patio was open, because that gives many more walk up spots. We should have been a party of three or four (we were a party of 2), because they kept asking for parties of 3-4. After every single party of 3-4 in the line was seated they opened up some of those bigger tables to a party of 2 (like us). We got really lucky we were one of the last couple of tables seated before they started taking names and telling people to come back at 6:45 p.m. I had just waited in line for Torissi and they text you when your spot is almost ready. Not here, they just tell you to come back.

We were seated at 5:30 p.m. and were super lucky to get an indoor table (that seated 4). They said we would need to be done by 8 p.m. I laughed and made a comment about how we would definitely be done by then. I was wrong, we left at 8 p.m. The service ended up being very slow and weirdly paced, but I'll get to that later.

This is what we got:

Egusi Dumpling - I thought it was good, but not great.
Curried Goat Patties - this was one of my favorite small plates. It was bursting with flavor, the crust was flakey and the goat was tender.
Oxtail Rangoon - I thought it was good, but again wasn't wowed. There were four to a plate and I ate one and gave the other three to my sister.

After this we waited for about half an hour before we got our large dish, the Braised Oxtails. I watched another table finish their large dish before ours came. It was bizarre since we put in the entire order at once. 

Braised Oxtails - absolutely delicious. The meat was fall off the bone. This was my favorite dish of the night. However, I get oxtail at a Jamaican restaurant near me for about 1/4 of the price so it's hard to say that this dish is worth the $58. However, I have noticed that everything is more expensive in NYC.

Then for dessert we got the Cosmic Brownie. The actual brownie was just ok, but the powdered sugar donut ice cream is amazing. It's more of a mind blowing trick than anything. It tastes exactly like a sugar donut. 

My sister got three drinks so our total came out to $278 with tax and tip. It was good, but I don't think it's the number 1 restaurant in NYC. I wouldn't stop someone from trying it out though for themselves. 

The decor is beautiful. I like the purple lights and the gold chains that are hanging. Also the people working the hostess stand are extremely friendly, so A+ for first impressions.

My rating for Tatiana's is really based on context- the hype, the reservations being taken by bots and not being able to get one (not sure why the restaurant isn't doing anything about this) and also the fact they wont put you on a list and text if a table is open, you just have to come back. l had really high expectations and although some of the food truly was unique, the end result left me wanting more and feeling a bit disappointed. The ambiance is really cute, the service is very nice, and the goat patties and oxtail were truly good, but other than that the food was just okay. The crispy okra was way too salty and I had a lot of hope for the Debbie brownie since I grew up with it but I felt let down in the taste of that as well. id recommend if you want to really try something new and unique, but otherwise i would not go again

Tatiana has been on my list of places to go for a while and it was amazing. It was definitely different walking through Lincoln Center but the ambiance was fantastic as my group was seated in a little alcove room. We ordered mostly what was recommended and nothing felt disappointing. Even some of the apps were things I'd want to eat every day. It's on the pricier end but definitely go for the experience.

Also a shoutout to the great service and for the team texting me that a reservation opened up!

I can't even begin to describe this dining experience! Honestly, it was the ULTIMATE DINING EXPERIENCE! As you can see by the pictures that we tried almost half the menu, if not more! Each dish had its own vibe. The menu felt like home cooked meals if that makes sense. Our server was TOP NOTCH! He was engaging and beyond kind. He made sure we had everything we wanted and needed. If you're able to secure a reservation at this venue (which takes a bit of work but worth it!), make sure you come ready to be blown away. 10/10 recommend

This place was amazing, the food was incredible, so much flavor, the vibe was immaculate, although hard to get a reservation and the people and workers were super nice and attentive. I felt like i couldn't complain about a single thing, it was that good. Must stop while in NY

Finally snagged a resy after months of failed attempts. I'd give this place 3.5 stars. The food was good, but tbh a bit overpriced and I'm not fond of items ordered coming out as they are ready, instead of the same time. Glad I was able to dine, but I probably won't be back.

I can see why this reservation is so incredibly difficult to get.  The ambiance is very hip but still elegant-not stuffy at all.  The service is superbly attentive/friendly and even goes out of their way to accommodate any time constraints you may have later in the evening.  The star--of course--is the food itself.  For small plates, the Egusi dumplings were an incredible first bite to start the night off with, I strongly recommend this option although you really can't go wrong with anything on the menu.  However; believe me (and everyone else in the reviews), you simply must try the short rib pastrami suya.  It is their poster card dish for a reason and arguably one of the best bites NYC has to offer!

Great contemporary Nigerian food. Was not easy to get a res when we went but got the details on TikTok. Dope crowd and vibe. The actual place looks like an airport lounge but once the lights dim, the vibe is better. The goat patties were sooo good. Super inventive menu. But very expensive.

Tatiana by Kwame Onwuachi was fire hit after fire hit. The ambiance was really nice, even when you take yourself on a solo date. The restroom was pretty bumpin' with the music blasting in there. Service was on point. Kiyah hooked me up with a bar seat. Definitely knew how to seat well to ensure that everyone on the walk in line would be able to snag a table and not wait too long. Christian was a fabulous bartender, came in with solid drinks and solid food recs. He's right, don't sleep on the rum cake.
I had the crab and oxtail rangoons. Great filling and crispy. For my large plate, I did the short rib pastrami. SO.FREAKING.GOOD. very tender and flavorful. And the caraway coco bread..mmHmm.
Definitely would go back again.

The experience here is nothing short of exceptional. We started with the crispy okra, curried goat patties, and black bean hummus. Each dish was a delightful fusion of flavors. For the mains, we indulged in the braised oxtails, short rib pastrami suya, and mom dukes shrimp. The braised oxtails were incredibly tender and flavorful. The short rib pastrami suya, was a melt-in-your-mouth experience.

Tatiana's menu is eclectic, innovative, and packed with bold, tasty flavors. Chef Kwame's creative flair shines through in every dish, making this spot an absolute must-visit. The food here is all the raves, and rightly so--it's a delicious journey that you'll want to take again and again!

Had the pleasure of dining at this wonderful restaurant on our vacation with my cousin.  It was a Tuesday night but inside it felt like a Saturday evening.  The food, staff and ambiance were amazing!  The host greeted us upon arrival and thanked us when we left.  The GM was simply the best.  The execution of the food was spot on.  My only regret we didn't have room for dessert.

The food at Tatiana did not disappoint. And I'm pleased/relieved, considering how hyped -- overhyped -- this place is. We had the pastrami dish, which was incredible -- an homage to the pastrami sandwich. The meat itself was so tender. But I really loved the cabbage, and perhaps "best red cabbage I've ever eaten" doesn't sound like much, but it's true (and I have eaten a lot of cabbage). My other favorite was the curried goat patties -- beautiful pastry here, and delicious filing. I also loved the chutney that accompanied it. Husband loved the crab Rangoon. He's a huge fan of the "traditional" (cough) version, and I wasn't sure what he'd think of the changes to the dish -- the oxtail, the heat. He wasn't sure after eating one, but after the second one, he was duly impressed. We also had the dumplings, as well as the okra -- both dishes were good and surprising in their own way, but not earth-shattering as the other dishes. Unfortunately, after the first couple of small dishes, it took forever for the rest of the food to come out, which really threw off the rhythm of the meal. But service was otherwise solid. 

And dessert. Wow. We went with the bodega brownie and the powdered sugar donut ice cream, the latter was pretty Proustian as it absolutely conjured tons of memories of being a little girl eating those (terrible! Delicious!) little hostess donuts.

For what it's worth, I'd struggled to get a reservation for this place but happened to check around 3pm on Resy and a spot was available. I didn't get a notice (even though I'd asked to be notified of openings), so don't give up refreshing the page, I guess. In the end, it's worth it.

I've been trying to get reservations for Tatiana's for a few months now and found myself researching how I could get to experience the food. My friend and I decided to take our chances and walk-in. We arrived at 4:45 (restaurant opens at 5) and approx. 20 ppl were ahead of us. We got lucky and were seated in the dining area instead of outdoors on the patio by 545. The ambiance is very nice and the customer service was on point. We had no complaints about any of the food options we chose. The food was delicious and I'd definitely visit again.

I've been here twice now and each time has been fantastic! The food is still fabulous, it doesn't take too long to get in. We sat outside this time and was on a Tuesday. Love the garden, felt like you weren't in NYC.

What amazed us by our experience, was apart from how flavorful the food was, the friendliness and professionalism of the staff. From hostess Darnelle who effortlessly accommodated our large group of 6 gregarious adults and one happy baby. Waiter Neo was amazing! He was flawlessly professional! At one point I asked him if he was an actor he was so good! We shared all our dishes (sorry for the lack of pictures): we had the CURRIED GOAT PATTIES, BLACK BEAN HUMMUS, SHORT RIB PASTRAMI SUYA, FRIED BRANZINO, SHAWARMA ROASTED CHICKEN AND THE BRAISED OXTAILS!!!! The portions were all plentiful for us all to try and we were stuffed at the end! We tried the cheesecake which was a bit too decadent and rich for us and the brownie which was delicious. The presentation of the dishes fed our eyes before our stomachs and I loved how Neo perfectly pronounced the African ingredients. Neo was a rockstar. We sat outside on the patio and were immersed in the opera music from the Lincoln center which led to the magical ambiance of the evening. We are new parents who don't get out much so this was a pure treat for us.  All in all, a joyous and memorable experience.

Tatiana has a Michelin star for a reason. I can confidently say that this was one of the best meals I've ever had in my entire life. 

I still think about the okra on a weekly basis. This is a must have must try 11/10. 

Everything was curated with so much thought and culinary expertise. I would eat everything on the menu if I could. If you can snag a reservation, this is the restaurant to go to. The dessert is insane. How does ice cream taste exactly like powdered donuts? A once in a lifetime experience. The restaurant itself is a little difficult to find since it's inside the Lincoln Center itself but it's a quaint space.
Went during the week without a reservation and was able to be seated within 30 minutes. Ambiance was great, food was solid.

Wow. Just wow. From the cocktails to the food. Service is spot on, and shout out to the hostess that worked Friday night 9/6/24 you are really really good at your job and I hope your boss sees this and gives you a raise. Great music played all evening and not overly loud.  My wife and I split the follow - Curry Goat Patties A++, Cod and Cornbread A++++ and Braised Oxtails A+++. No wonders it's impossible to get into this place!

Always an amazing time!! I celebrated my birthday here with some friends visiting from Atlanta and we were all throughly impressed. Neo assisted us with our meal, and drink selections and he was spot on with every recommendation. Tatiana's is one of my favorite restaurants in the world and after this visit my friends understood why.

i'm thinking that the only way to get the best of the situation is to go to the restaurant and find out for yourself that the food is great and the people are happy to help you and the ambiance is there is romantic and i love it so much

One of my girlfriends and I got together to get food and drinks. When we arrived we parked on the street nearby. We walked into a busy restaurant. It was kind of small but nice. We sat at the bar, and Christian was our server/bartender, and he was nice. I ordered the vodka martini, and it was good! My friend ordered Dusse Colada, and she enjoyed it. For food, she ordered the Fried Okra, Oxtail & Crab Rangoon, Curried King crab, and fried Branzino. I tasted it all, and I really enjoyed the Rangoon and and king crab. The branzino was ok, I didn't like the sauce too much. The place is pricey but all in all it was a good experience!

Tatiana truly isn't in need of any good reviews. I love this restaurant so much. I wish it was located in DC.  Everything on the menu is exceptional. Ambiance 10/10 and the music sets the tone.

Best items on the menu:
-Curried goat patties 
-Short rib pastrami 
-Braised Oxtail 
-Pri Pri salad 
-Mom Duke Shrimp

Of course Tatiana was amazing . We walked in on a Saturday afternoon. We waited for like 30mins and got seated at the bar . The goat patties and Bronzino were amazing . The wait staff was great and the drinks were hitting . I had two pina coladas and I'm still thinking about them . As a Caribbean person this food felt like home .Can't wait to go back !

A phenomenal restaurant. I don't think they have a bad thing on the menu. And I love that everything's sounds phenomenal. I was just happy to get a reservation, which is probably the biggest issue with this restaurant. It is still such a restaurant that it is very difficult to get a reservation.

4.5 stars for Tatiana. 

Tatiana lived up to the hype--it was excellent! We rarely venture to this area for dinner, so it was fun to get a change of scenery. We had a 7:30pm reservation, arrived on time, and waited about 15-20 minutes to be seated. The place was packed and full of energy. Total cost was around $350 including 20% tip.

Food - 4.5 stars.
The food was excellent, offering an imaginative and fun blend of flavors.  
- Starter 1: Egusi Dumplings (4 stars) - Fantastic flavor, but not overly creative.  
- Starter 2: Curried Goat Patties (5 stars) - Amazing balance of flavors with chutney and white sauce, not too goat-y.  
- Main 1: Short Rib Pastrami Suya (5 stars) - Fun dish, big portion! Best enjoyed by combining the short rib, slaw, and roll, especially with the hot sauce.
- Main 2: Braised Oxtails (4 stars) - Delicious but the sauce was a bit too sweet and thick for my taste.  
- Drinks: Cocktails (3.5 stars) - The Old Fashioned was mediocre, but the spicy margaritas were good, with a nice balance of sweet, salty, and a little kick.  
- Dessert: Jello Shots (4 stars) - Fun and visually appealing, though not much flavor.

Service - 4.0 stars.
The staff was professional if a bit cold. Our waiter was knowledgeable about the menu and struck a good balance between being attentive and letting us enjoy our meal. Overall, the service was solid.

Ambiance - 5.0 stars.
The interior was stunning with an upscale club-like vibe. We were seated near the perimeter, separated from the Lincoln Center crowd by ceiling-height chain curtains. The cool blue chandelier artwork added to the atmosphere, and the place was buzzing.

Ambiance is great , with hip hop and upbeat tunes playing in a fun atmosphere. Food is different and great with African and Creole influences. The  short rib pastrami was fantastic as was the crab dumplings.Bodega doughnuts were also delicious!

I was fascinated by all the buzz around Tatiana and was lucky enough to get a reservation for my birthday week. It did not disappoint. I looooooove food and sampling different flavor profiles and this place was so hip and fun and the perfect place to do this. The cocktails were very good. I had the spicy margarita and the nutcracker really loved the margarita. The service was great, people circling to keep water cups filled. Shae, our waitress was really great too, easy to find and readily available even though she looked like she had a lot of tables to look after. The atmosphere was clubby with loud music. 

The menu is small plates as apps and the large shares for entree to share or not to share. I like the idea of shared plates so I can easily sample dishes from my dinner companions, so that was really fun. The curry goat patties are to die for!!! Make sure to put the sauce and compote on it to get the full experience. The cod and corn cake was really good too. The dumpling were ok, would try something else if I get another chance to dine here. 

For large shares we had braised oxtail, crab with scallion pancake, short rib pastrami and the mom dukes shrimp. The highlight was the oxtail. The short rib pastrami was a little salty but combined with the pickled cabbage it was very good. The shrimp dish was heavenly and the brioche that it was served with was sooo good. 

We had to get the bodega special for dessert because everyone was commenting about it on reviews and it was such a ny-er name, it cracked us up. It was very good and fun. Very whimsical, elevated warm brownie with donut shaped ice cream. Eating both together in one bite was key for us. Unforgettable dinner!

Gotta start with , Reservations are strongly recommended.

Chef Kwame Onwuachi draws on his West African roots and the flavors of his childhood in the Bronx and elsewhere on this menu with signature dishes like egusi dumplings, filled with crab and sea bass in a brick red sauce. The centerpiece--oxtail--arrives in a large pot with two glistening pieces resting in a thick sauce. Marinated for more than a day, and served with Thumbelina carrots and chayote squash along with rice and peas.

Beautiful interior that truly belongs at one on my favorite landmarks in NYC, Lincoln Center. 

Pro tip: Don't sleep on the short rib pastrami suya, oxtail,and curry goat patties.

Lucked out with a same-day reservation at an actually reasonable time (7:15 PM). While the pacing of our meal was weird, the food was amazing and I'd say it mostly lives up to the hype. Also, prepare to drop $$$.

I tried:
+ Dussé Colada cocktail - perfect 
+ Karaoke honeymoon - solid 
+ Egusi dumplings - great 
+ curried goat patties - so good, and the chutney is amazing 
+ Short rib pastrami suya - absolute best thing, must-order 
+ Braised oxtails - good but don't need again 
+ Bodega special - great the doughnut ice cream was uncanny. Tasted exactly like Donettes 

Re: weird pacing - our first appetizer (the parties) came within seconds of ordering, then it was over a half hour wait for the second app (dumplings). First entree came 10 mins later so suddenly we were rushing to eat everything. 

Otherwise no notes!

A girlfriend and I snagged a 7:45 reservation last Wednesday night and I could not have been more excited. We had a little bit of difficulty finding the entrance to the restaurant but once inside it was smooth sailing. The main dining room has an almost clubby vibe to it that we really enjoyed. Our waiter for the evening was great but he did forget about my Mango allergy a couple of times and brought a mango jello shot at the end of dinner. Luckily I asked what the flavors were before popping one in my mouth! We made friends with the girls at the table next to us and ended up sharing a few dishes so we were able to try the following: 

Curried Goat Patties - Absolutely delicious, one of our favorite things
Crispy Okra - Good but not a must order
Hamachi Escovitch - This was a miss for us. The fish was sliced too thick and it was missing spice. 
Take Out Mushrooms - This was another miss for us and we both thought that the mushrooms were too sweet. 
Braised Oxtails - served as a stew. Very comforting and good.
Short Rib Pastrami - exactly as good as everyone says that it is. If you are from Texas, it is basically BBQ brisket. Very rich, very indulgent.

Overall we had a really fun time and enjoyed our meal, but there were two entire dishes that we disliked enough that we only took one bite so I can't give it that 5th star.

Tatiana was worth the wait for resy's. The ambiance and service were effortlessly elegant and down to the last detail perfect. Having said that, nothing was better than the food. My top recommendations are the crab and oxtail rangoons, and the tuna for starters. I had the chicken shwarma as my entree - the best chicken over rice I have ever had!

What a culinary gem! The flavors are simply amazing, showcasing vibrant dishes that tantalize the palate. Our servers Cristiano & Monica were welcoming and attentive to detail. We also had Amy advise us on a splendid delicious wine that paired with every single bite. The ambience was very fun and dim. Perfect for a date night. Loved the music as well. A delightful dining experience that leaves you craving more! Will definitely come back.

Trying to get a reservation here is a mess...I'm sorry but I just have to start off by mentioning that. I stopped by after work on a Wednesday evening around 5:30 without a reservation and asked for a seat at the bar. It was JUMPING at that time to my surprise..like wow. I was put on the waiting list and was told it could be up to a 2hr wait..but I knew what I was getting myself into so that was fine. I left and returned about a hour and a half later and was seated at the bar. I started off with their margarita and it was strong.. which we love. Next were the goat meat patties..10/10.. especially with the scotch bonnet pepper they have. I next got the ox tail.. the pieces were huge but that was just an 8/10 for me. Finally for dessert.. the powdered donuts and cosmic brownie shouldn't be skipped 10/10. One particular bartender was super kind, attentive and made the experience great. The music and overall vibe of the restaurant was solid. My suggestion when coming here is come during the week when it first opens. Good luck

Making reservations was absolutely absurd to say the least!! We tried to make it online but it seemed impossible (it opens on a certain date and time...). We went in-person and the wait was 1.5-2hrs and it was when the restaurant opened up. Seating was so challenging we ended sitting at the bar. 

The food was tasty but I was expecting more for the hype. Not a lot of choices on the menu. Drink: pog nutcracker was amazing! The desserts were super small and not worth the cost. Service was nice. The atmosphere was a nice vibe & modern. Finding the exact location wasn't so easy either. I would not go back here unless someone is able to actually give me a reservation time.

Ever walk into a restaurant so excited you feel like a kid on Christmas morning? That was us--two huge Top Chef fans--walking into Tatiana by Kwame Onwuachi on a cold January evening for my fiancé's birthday. As longtime admirers of Kwame's journey (he's like the culinary version of a superhero to us), the anticipation was real. And guess what? Tatiana did not disappoint.

First Impressions: Hot Tea, Warm Hearts

We showed up as walk-ins (risky, we know), but the Tatiana crew didn't flinch. Despite the freezing weather outside, they kept things cozy by bringing us steaming hot tea while we waited. Honestly, we felt like royalty--if royalty wears coats and scarves and stares lovingly at a cocktail menu.

Cocktails: A Creative and Playful Selection

Our evening kicked off with a round of cocktails that were as creative as they were delicious:

Benton's Old Fashioned - Smooth and smoky, this classic was elevated with a touch of elegance. Think bourbon at its finest.

Espresso Coquito - A creamy, caffeinated delight that tasted like dessert in a glass. If holidays had a signature cocktail, this would be it.

Karaoke Honeymoon - Playful and vibrant, this drink was a tropical getaway in a glass--bright, refreshing, and just the right amount of sweet.

POG Nutcracker - A fun twist on the NYC favorite. Fruity, boozy, and perfectly crafted, it transported us straight to summer vibes even in the dead of winter.


Each cocktail was thoughtfully presented, complete with gorgeous garnishes and crystal-clear ice that sparkled in the low light.

The Food: Comfort Meets Class

The food was a journey of bold flavors and inventive takes on familiar dishes. Here's what stood out:

Egusi Dumplings: Crispy on the outside, savory and comforting on the inside. These dumplings were pure magic--one bite was all it took to win us over.

Oxtail & Crab Rangoon: Flaky, golden perfection with a rich, savory filling that left us speechless.

Short Rib Pastrami Suya: This dish combined deep, smoky spices with soft buns, making it the ultimate comfort food.

Hamachi Escovitch: Light, fresh, and bursting with flavor. The avocado and fish paired beautifully with the tangy escovitch sauce, making this a refreshing addition to the meal.


At this point, we were fully convinced: Kwame is a genius.

Dessert: The Bodega Special - A Sweet and Nostalgic Farewell

We ended the meal with the Bodega Special, a playful tribute to New York's iconic corner store snacks. It came with powdered treats, colorful candies, and a candle that added a touch of whimsy to the celebration. It was the perfect end to a perfect evening--a sweet, lighthearted nod to nostalgia.

Ambiance: Modern, Warm, and Effortlessly Cool

Tatiana nails the balance between chic and welcoming. The modern interior feels upscale but never stuffy--it's the kind of place where you can celebrate a special occasion or just pop in for a drink after work. The thoughtful service and artistic plating made every moment feel intentional, elevating the entire experience.

Final Thoughts: A Culinary Love Letter from Kwame

Tatiana isn't just a meal--it's a story told through food, cocktails, and ambiance. From the hot tea on arrival to the inventive cocktails, flavorful dishes, and playful dessert, Tatiana by Kwame Onwuachi exceeded every expectation.

Whether you're a Top Chef fan, a foodie on the hunt for the next great meal, or someone who just wants to be spoiled for an evening, Tatiana is the spot. We're already plotting our next visit--and hoping they keep the tea on the menu permanently.

Don't do their tasting menu, or what Tatiana calls the "trust us" menu. You're basically just paying more for less food since everything has to be shared family-style. The real kicker was when we were given one cheesecake at the end of the night to share between the three of us. Do better, Tatiana. Also, they sat us down 45 minutes after our reservation, despite the fact that we pre-paid $200 per head. Walk-in customers get better treatment and a fairer value for what they pay.

Resy reservations for this place are pretty much gone in seconds, but I lucked out by snagging a cancelled reservation via Resy notifications.

I read somewhere that if Empire State of Mind were a restaurant, Tatiana would be it and I'm inclined to agree. It has a clubby atmosphere and they're bumping hip hop and R&B all night long.

What we ordered:
Curried goat patties- really excellent. Crispy crust with rich filling. Really loved the vinegary chili sauce they provide on the side.
Egusi dumplings- good, but probably the most expensive dumplings I've ever ordered.
Curried king crab- I found the curry flavor to slightly overwhelm the taste of the crab, but overall well executed. Tasty roti for dipping.
Lamb rib special- my favorite dish of the night! Tender, unctuous lamb offset brilliantly by fresh herbs. They should make this a regular menu item.
Pastrami short rib- yummy though I was pretty full by this point to fully appreciate the dish.
Bodega special- very amusing presentation with ice cream shaped like donuts. Tastes exactly how you think it'd taste, and the brownie is warm!

I've had better meals in NYC (sorry Pete Wells), but nevertheless it was a great experience I'd repeat.

An overly loud music restaurant really ruins the whole experience... As we walked it, it feels like a nightclub. It was unpleasant that we had to shout to talk for the 2 hour dinner. 

Was it worth it?
Short Rib Pastrami Suya for $86 uhm.

My favorite might be the Mom Duke's Shrimp.

Yet still traumatized by the experience.

To put it simply, this restaurant can be described as "A vibe". The location and setting is just beautiful on the inside and outside with Lincoln Center being the view from the windows. The service here is also great and our waitress was helpful and attentive but...for me it's always about the food

For what you're paying, the food is just good. Unique! but good. The short rib pastrami, fried okra appetizer, mushrooms, crab legs and piri piri salad all had great flavor and prepared well, but none of them were mind blowing and the amount of crab you get was pretty small for the price

The Cod with Cornbread and the Lamb Ribs (special of the night) were 11/10 dishes I would come back for and justified the price. The flavors were outstanding and Cod and Cornbread was a combo I didnt know I was missing out on

Overall, if you want to come for the experience and "Wow" your friends with a unique food experience, I would say go for it if you got the cash to spend, otherwise I just think this place was a bit overhyped
Go now. Egusi dumplings and Rangoon were top notch. Music was awesome. Staff was friendly.
Don't know why it's so impossible to get a reservation for this place! Just For some glorified street  food to be dolled up and served to ppl who act like this is soooooo exquisite and exclusive!

Tatiana is definitely an experience I had been waiting for. We were only able to get a table by getting there at opening and hanging around until 9pm on a weekday. Very much in demand. The menu seems to change from time to time. It's a little dark inside but definitely a nice spot to be in. The food itself was really good. The service was also great. I think it's important to understand that this place is mixing flavors from specific regions and so you might not really have the Nigerian or Jamaican flavor winning in a dish with a name from the region. That's the only reason it's not a 5 star

First, Get the short ribs...

Ok now for the review. 

As a fellow Bronx native who knows good food, Chef Kwame did an outstanding job with Tatitanas! The homage and elevation of The Bronx and NYC cuisine is mind blowing. 

We ate

Egusi Dumpling- It was delicious 8/10. I don't have anything to reference it to because I've never tasted Egusi. Would I order it again... absolutely. 

Green Caesar- light, airy and delicious 8/10

Curry Goat Patties- 9/10 light flaky crust, curry goat filling was full of flavor but not over powering. Don't forget to use the sauce and mango chutney if you want to have a flavorful party in your mouth. It makes for the perfect bite. 

Braised Oxtail- 7/10 it's really big braised oxtail in a glaze sauce with a side of rice and peas made with basmati


Short Rib Pastrami Suya 
Bodega Special 


We drank 

Pina Pina Pina 
Watermelon Margarita 
POG Nutcracker
LC Negroni
Mascato 

Everything was amazing and I can't wait to go again

Went with a party of five in October. Given their #1 NYT ranking and fancy location, I was expecting self-importance, profiteering, and  slighting of the food, but I was completely wrong. Instead, the staff was warm and gracious, expertly informed and eager to please, and the food was engagingly new while comforting and delicious. Most impressive: the management exhibited extreme self-discipline and care of its diners by leaving several tables unoccupied despite a line of waiting patrons in line. Our interpretation was that while the kitchen and serving teams perfect their skills, this new restaurant keeps the customer count down to a level where every guest receives first-class, prompt yet unhurried attention. Hurrah for Tatiana!

Beautiful place. And no exaggeration when I say the food was AMAZING. Sheesh! I happy danced all night and was grateful to Jake & staff who accommodated myself & friends for my birthday dinner. They are very hospitable and pay attention to every detail! (I'm so serious.) And did I mention the food? No notes. Wonderfully seasoned. Great presentation. Taste buds were happy! I should have also ordered some to go! Ha! And prepare yourself for the drinks because the cocktails are STRONG & yummy!

LOVED. The way to get in (after many failed Resy attempts), is to go stand in line before opening. They have 11 bar seats saved for walk-ins, and we got there at 3:45 pm on a weekday and were the second ones in line. (Granted, it was raining so that might have driven people away). I think even the person that arrived at 4:30 got in at that first seating. Otherwise, they take your number and will call you when something opens up. 

My only issue was that the portions were SO BIG (and thus, felt pricey). Like - if you're just two people, you really can only order 4 things max, and even that is too much food. We ended up boxing up some and taking it home. Why can't the shortribs be half the size so we can try more things? 

Bests:
SHORT RIB PASTRAMI SUYA (just have to do it)
CURRIED GOAT PATTIES (did not sound like something I'd like but then we both LOVED them)
FRIED BRANZINO (I was so full by the time this came out that I don't feel like I fully appreciated it, but it was yummy)
BODEGA SPECIAL

Good but wouldn't order again:
EGUSI DUMPLINGS

Those 4 things (plus the dessert) plus two mocktails came out to $300 after tax/tip.

Food, ambience and service all great. 10 - 10 - 10 across the board.  I ordered the Branzino and Oxtails, chef's kiss. I do recommend to order the large plates. The small dishes are extremely small but tasty.

How did I miss leaving a review for THE Tatiana? I've been twice  and both times were incredible.  Staff is so kind and made sure I got the outdoor seating for my access need (though the indoors and restroom are wheelchair accessible too).

Everything is phenomenal especially the short rib pastrami, oxtail, egusi dumplings, curried goat patties, and the hummus with lamb. Cocktails were on point as well.

If you can get a table, go! You won't find a better meal anywhere.

The music playlist really enhanced the ambiance. It was just such an amazing chill vibe. The service from the staff was 10/10. Every time I needed a refill it was done without asking, they folded my napkin when I left to the restroom, and every staff stopped consistently to ask how we were doing. The food was out of this world. We had the curry goat patties, oxtail ragoon and oxtail for main entree. We would definitely go back again and it is worth the hard to get reservation.

One of the hardest reservations in nyc and I was so excited to finally dine at Tatiana. I went on Thanksgiving Eve and there was already a line outside, but that was for walk-ins only. I had an early reservation at 5:15pm and was seated immediately. Chef Kwame Onwuachi even greeted us as we walked in. The ambiance is beautiful and lively, my fiancée and I were seated at the corner which was perfect. For cocktails, my fiancée ordered a sangria and I had a glass of Riesling. The food we shared were the egusi dumplings, curried goat patties, scallop guisado, short rib pastrami suya, and cosmic brownie for dessert. My personal favorites were the curried goat patties and the short rib pastrami. Everything was very good and filling. The staff was very friendly and the service was impeccable. It is definitely worth trying.

Absolutely lives up to the hype. Delicious food, harmonious cocktails, warm and enthusiastic service. Vibe and ambiance impeccable. 10/10 recommend and much gratitude to everyone from Chef Kwame to the entire staff.

There should be six stars available for some restaurants. This one definitely needs six stars. We had a required trip to NYC and scored reservations for one of the hottest restaurants in NYC and maybe all of the US.  Everything about Tatiana is exceptional. The service is incomparable. Every single person who served us was kind, attentive, and helpful.  The decor is cool and feels very chic.  It's a little dark inside, but made for a cooler atmosphere. We had a table off to the side of the main dining room, which was a bit quieter and definitely cozier.  We ate an amazing amount of food, the quality of which I have never had before. We ate almost every dish from the small plate menu; highlights were the jerk lamb ribs, the oxtail & crab rangoons, and the goat patties, but the hamachi escovitch and Egusi dumplings were also off the charts. Large plates includes braised Oxtails which are Chef Kwame's specialty, the Mediterranean chicken, and the deconstructed wagyu pastrami.  Honestly, I don't have the words for how amazing this food was.  If you get a chance to get a reservation, plan for a stellar experience.  We were also lucky enough to meet and talk to Chef Kwame for a little while. If you don't know his story, find the Netflix special about him. He was so very kind and very down to earth. We'll remember this meal for years to come.

We arrived at 4:20pm for walk in on a weeknight (when they open at 5pm), there were already about 5 people ahead of us. We heard about this place from Infatuation (#1 restaurant in New York) and since we were visiting from California we had to make it happen. It's definitely gotten busier since getting such big publicity, and we didn't even try to get a reservation since I heard that was very difficult. We were able to get a table for 4 at 5pm! It seemed that there were not a lot of groups of 4 so that was an advantage in the standby line (vs a 6:30 pm return time if we were a group of 2)
The menu rotates but some items stay the same. We LOVED everything. They recommend 8-10 items for 4 people, we split 8 items and 2 desserts and that was perfect.
The highlight? Vegetarian wise it was the "Take-Out Mushrooms" which featured amazing and plentiful Oyster Mushrooms. For meat lovers the "Braised Oxtail" was amazing, apparently the chef has been perfecting the recipe for his lifetime. The Cosmic Brownie was out of this world!!
The jerk lamb rib isn't pictured because we devoured it immediately!!
We will be back again 100/10!!

Our friend somehow managed to snag a reservation here. Overall a very pleasant experience -- a bit pricey but I enjoyed each of the dishes we got.

Cornbread - fantastic starter. 
Goat patties - solid.
Crispy okra - really easy to eat, glazed with honey and tastes like fries.

Oxtail - absolutely fall off the bone, melt in the mouth delicious. The sauce is a little heavy, but otherwise very good.

Short Rib Pastrami Suya - Holy, when this came out we realized we may have overordered. It's a huge spread of meat. I will say I wish there were just a bit more bread to counter the meat, but at the end of the meal I was STUFFED.

DESSERT! - The Bodega Special lived up to its hype. I was surprised at how much it tasted like powdered donuts. I think I'd come back to have this again.

Tried to get a reservation 31 times losing to bots each time. FINALLY got one through someone's kindness and genuinely thought this was going to be more hype than delivery, but I was so wrong. The meal was INCREDIBLE. Service was also amazing. We figured we wouldn't get to go back soon so ordered more than recommended. For apps we got the piri piri salad, goat patties, fried okra, dumplings, black bean hummus and then for mains we did the pastrami and oxtails. We also had two nonalcoholic beverages the pineapple daiquiri and the guava/passionfruit one. Everything was honestly good, but the piri piri salad, fried okra, black bean hummus and pastrami were knock outs. 

My husband said it was the best salad he ever had.
It was the best okra I will ever have. 
Highly recommend making a sandwich with the pastrami. 

A restaurant living up to the hype. Cannot wait to fight the bot takeover and get another reservation next year.

ABSOLUTELY delicious. 

My friend was hyping this place up for MONTHS before I finally got around to it, and to my delight, it did not disappoint. All the dishes I tried were good, but the oxtail is to die for.

Ambiance is great too. It's very lively, but can be a little loud, so if you are looking for something quiet, this might not be the best spot. It's also kind of hard to get a reservation, but they do take walk-ins if you get there before they open.
The reservation process is simply ridiculous.. they really need to fix it .. you wait thirty days to be told sorry " our waiting list is full for the next two months ... NOT WORTH THE WAIT !!!
So excited to finally experience (can't wait to get to DC!!!) great service, atmosphere and food that leaves you wanting more!!! Well done!!!

I've had the privilege to dine in one of the top restaurants in NYC and also one of the hardest reservations to get into more than once! 

The place is on the small side tucked in a corner. The maximum number of people allowed for this restaurant is 6 people and all have to be present in order to dine in. 

We started off with the complimentary champagne from the manager. Cocktails were amazing. The nutcracker, karaoke honeymoon and sangria were delicious. I also ordered the pineapple daiquiri mocktail. 

We ordered a bunch of small dishes to share:

Egusi Dumplings - one of their signature appetizers. It's worth trying once. It's initially Steamed then pan seared. 

Crispy Okra - amazing starter definitely worth ordering. Personally I want to replicate this recipe on a air fryer. 

Curry Goat Patties - another great dish worth ordering, wish there was more. 

Cornbread and Cod - pleasantly surprised how good this dish was by combining a cod, sauce and cornbread in one bite. 

Jerk Lamb Rib - this dish was initially part of the large share section of the menu but it was moved to the small shared portion. The dish came with bread which tasted amazing. Just enough to share with 6 people. 

Now to the large plates. 

Braised Oxtails - this dish was amazing, rich and filling. This dish was made with love. The oxtail meat fell off the bone. The combination of oxtail, sauce with the rice and peas was memorable. 

Fried Branzino - this dish was also amazing. Fish was perfectly fried. I would definitely order this again. 

Mom Duke's Shrimp - this dish was great. Personally, it was a lot of work to dissect the whole shrimp especially the head. The shrimp, butter sauce and toast was very good. I was starting to get full after consuming the toast. 

Short Rib Pastrami Suya - this dish was the highlight of the dining experience. The pastrami melted in your month. The dish was deconstructed to make a pastrami slider with the cabbage and coco bread. 

The manager gave us a piece of bread equivalent to roti to dip in the remaining oxtail sauce. This bread was amazing and it should be in their regular menu. 

We ended the night with the bodega special. The dessert shared with 6 people is just right because it would have been rich. 

Previously I dined several times and I tried the oxtail and crab rangoon (worth ordering once but personally it felt like it was a standard dish), honeynut piri piri salad (worth trying once, but dish was small with a beautiful presentation, scallop guisado (worth ordering), take out mushrooms (large portion always had leftovers), shawarma roasted chicken (chicken was tender and portion was large, ended up taking it home) and golden rum cake (great dessert doused with rum that one can get drunk on due to low tolerance). 

The staff and service were amazing. Teresa, Jake and Vesna were awesome serving and accommodating us. I'll definitely return to dine again, but reservations are hard to come by.

If you can get a reservation definitely grab it! Ambiance is great they play rap/hiphop mix. The food was excellent but definitely different types of flavors than I'm normally used to. Spicy Smokey. The branzino was my favorite but the empanadas as appetizer was also delicious!

Wow! Absolutely amazing experience. We had the Cornbread, Fried Okra, Egsusi Dumpling, Oxtail & Crab Rangoon, Braised Oxtail, Mom Duke's Shrimp, Peri Peri Salad and the Chopped Cheese. Dessert - Bodega Special. The quality and flavor of the dishes was exceptional. Our favs were the Oxtail & Crab Rangoon, Chopped Cheese, Mom Duke's Shrimp and the Peri Peri Salad. The food and sauces exploded with flavor in your mouth. The Peri Peri Salad is a must. The dessert was incredible with a warm brownie and ice cream that just paired so well together. I want to give a huge shout out to our server Beatriz. She was absolutely amazing. Super friendly and amazing service. She contributed to our amazing experience at Tatiana.
