We will definitely come back. The ambiance was great. Good music in the background that kept the vibe upbeat. All the staff were exceptional and deserve a huge thanks.

Many boyfriend and I came to Tatiana's to celebrate our anniversary and it was perfect!! The ambiance gave the place and intimate feel and the service made us feel like VIP's. The wagyu pastrami was so soft and flavorful and the empanadas were a great app to start the meal. Make sure to get the bodega special as a dessert -- best brownie and ice cream donuts ever!

Miraculously landed a day of resy for this place after many months of trying. Sometimes these hyped places disappoint but this spot totally lived up to all the deliciousness. The honeyed okra is still something I'm dreaming about. The braised ox was so dreamy and short rib pastrami so mouthwatering. Cocktails were also very well thought out as evidenced by the mixture and photos. 

Service was very attentive without being stifling. My husband who really loathes super formal settings was just so pleased to have high caliber cooking without all the fuzz. 

Ambiance was so relaxed with many happy clientele to finally be dining at this hotspot.

Another fantastic visit to Tatiana by Chef Kwame. Still one of the best dining experiences you'll find in NYC. From the music, to the decor, to the service, to the excellent food. Tatiana does not miss. Music is always a vibe and def keeps you moving on your seat. It's an eclectic mix of patrons which shows how Chef Kwame has delivered authenticity and culture to attract folks from all corners of the word and big apple.

Service is top notch, as always. A lot of rockstars on the team. Darnelle, Pierre, Monica, Kia, Miuset. Everyone made my return experience excellent and I could speak more highly of them.

Food is unmatched. Just know, when you go to Tatiana, you're going for the quality. This ain't Applebees so don't expect any happy hours or 2 or 1 specials. You pay for the top notch food which is prepared and presented as ordered/available. Meaning your items arrive in courses. Depending on hunger levels, consider 2-3 apps, and 2-3 larger dishes per couple.

Yes, Reservations are difficult but well worth it once you finally secure a seat.
The service here is amazing and all the dishes were quite flavorful and interesting. My favorites were the pastrami, goat puffs, and the shrimp.

This was definitely a hard reservation to get.

Everything on the menu was designed to be shared. I appreciated the menu since it was organized into three sections (small share, large share, and dessert), with everything ordered from smallest to biggest, which made it easier on me with fewer decisions.

I ordered the following:
- Egusi Dumplings
- Curried Goat Patties
- Hamachi Escovitch
- Oxtail & Crab Rangoon
- Braised Oxtail

I feel like the portion sizes were quite small across the board considering the price tag associated with each dish. The egusi dumplings were underwhelming, so I recommend skipping them. The curried goat patties were really good and came with two great sauces. The hamachi escovitch was phenomenal, and the oxtail & crab rangoon were crisp to perfection, albeit both dishes were very small. The only big dish I ordered was the renowned braised oxtails that came with rice. I believe that is a must-order if you ever manage to get a reservation. The meat was super soft and melted off the bone.

The staff there was super attentive and very friendly. They always refilled my water promptly (much needed, as I was trying out their hot sauce). The music was a bit loud, which made it hard to have an intimate conversation, and there was Hollister lighting.

TL;DR: perfect date night venue with flavor packed small and large shares. $100+ per person with dinner and drinks!

Managed to snag a last minute same day reservation for table for three on a Sat evening, and we were promptly seated on time. Dim lit modern decor welcomes you with floor to ceiling glass windows giving an amazing view of Lincoln Center - we got lucky with a comfy corner table too! A perfect date night venue with music and noise levels on the louder end.

We got straight to ordering which included three small plates Egusi Dumpling, Curried Goat Patties, and Crispy Okra. Okra was the winner for us which hit a perfect balance between sweet and spice and while the goat meat was very well cooked, the patties were on the greasy end. Small plates on an average were priced between $22 to $28.

Our large share included Mom Duke's Shrimp ($55) and Take-Out Mushrooms ($52) and portion sizes were large enough to share between three adults for a single plate. Our amazing server Francesca did recommend getting just one large share, but there weren't as many great options for vegetarians!

Service was amazing and food arrived within 20-25 mins of ordering and as it was prepared/ready. Definitely worth visiting once and we will visit again just to enjoy their large shares!

It lives up to the hype! What a fun experience overall. The staff were so kind and welcoming and helped accommodate our limited time. The short rib pastrami suya is the stuff dreams are made of. I'm counting down the days until I can dine here again and try more dishes!

I honestly don't get the hype. The food was mediocre at best, yet the prices are sky-high--$30 for some curry puffs, really? The best way to describe the menu is Elevated bodega bites: Deli meat couture, fried Twinkie eleganza...And no, those aren't compliments.

As I sat there, I couldn't help but wonder--who is this restaurant even for? It feels like "poor people's rich food"--taking familiar, inexpensive dishes, adding a bit of flair, and slapping on an absurd price tag.

Oh, and the noise level? Unbearable. The music was blasting so loudly that my ears were still ringing when we left. It completely ruined our experience, to the point that we struggled to enjoy The Magic Flute at the Lincoln Center afterward. 

The space is tiny, the atmosphere chaotic, and rowdiness seems encouraged. A table near us was celebrating a birthday, and the whole scene felt... well, let's just say it was a lot.

Servers seemed overwhelmed, and water cups were not filled as often as I'd like them to. Save your money. This place isn't worth the hype.

Still by far my FAVORITE restaurant! Talk about consistency! Every time I eat here, the food and drinks are as excellent as the first time I came here!

If you're an oxtail lover, you MUST get the oxtail! Every time I come, I get it and will continue to get it again and again!

Ambiance in the restaurant is excellent. Dimly lit but not too dark. Always great music playing. It's like a party at dinner. 

Service is always spot on! Food is spot on! Had the oxtail of course, curry goat pattys and the Bronzino which also is delicious. All are a must try!  

To wash it all down, you must try the Pog Nutcracker!

The atmosphere was great, the service was impeccable, the curry goat patties was great. I personally didn't like the brown stew chicken and the oxtails. I think I was expecting more Caribbean flavors but It was definitely more on the African side. If I go back, I would get more goat patties and try a different entree dish than the 2 I tried. The reviews were so great but not my favorite.

Absolutely loved the food. We had the pastrami of course, so popular, it's not pork, it's wagyu short rib. The cornbread was delicious  wish they gave more (order 2 ) lol  We ordered the fish and there were a few bones but tasted so good and fresh. Prepare for spice! The best drink I ever had called the Nutcracker! Playlist is always fire!

Food was excellent, though I would argue they were stingy with the sauces. Many dishes were a bit spicier than I expected (fine for me, not so fine for my partner who cannot handle spice) but all delicious. 

The service for me was really the atrocious part of this place, particularly considering how expensive it is. To start, not enough bathrooms, and everyone in our party of 6 waited for at least 10 minutes at some point throughout the meal. They were also out of paper towels. For a place that walks around the dining room demanding that you check your coat, not having to dry my hands on my clothes would have been a nice touch. 

We waited 30 minutes to be seated for our reservation. Party of 6, multiple rounds of drinks and we didn't skimp on our food order. At no point during the meal were we lingering by any stretch of the imagination. There was a bit of a delay at some points because one of our meals was forgotten, and we were all forced to scarf this dish while staff grabbed our plates literally from under our raised forks; and at one point a server dropped a full glass of water on the floor and soaked the table next to ours (staff was appropriately apologetic and cleaned it carefully, though no one bothered to replace the water glass until we asked). 

None of these issues would have been worth a poor review - mistakes happen, and good food compensates for most transgressions. But the real kicker was 5 minutes after receiving our coffee (which was received 10 minutes after our dessert), the maitre d' approached our table and asked us to please wrap it up as he had other reservations waiting. Note: at this point we hadn't even received the bill yet, a fact he could have easily checked with his staff prior to approaching us. When we alerted him to this fact he was apologetic, but it definitively left a sour taste in our mouths after an otherwise great meal. To seat us 30 minutes past the start of our reservation while also demanding we vacate our table 5 minutes after receiving our coffee is... definitely not a vibe I need to pay this much money to experience.

Honest review of Tatiana's: 

I finally had a chance to go to Tatiana's located at 10 Lincoln Center Plaza NYC! Reservations are very hard to get but luckily they do hold limited bar seating for people. I arrived two hours before they opened so I could secure my seat so an accordingly! Inside you are greeted by very hospitable staff where they user you to your seat. The din ing area is lively and electric so do t expect it to be a quiet space. My first dish I tried was the crispy okra and I'll tell you it was like no okra I have ever tried. It was seasoned with Honey, mustard, and pepper sauce with a slice of lemon you can squeeze. The crisp was amazing but that honey to heat ratio was unforgettably delightful. My main dish was short rib pastrami suya, boneless wagyu short rib, caraway coco bread and melted cabbage.  This was a home run for me, the short ribs were very tender with a great pastrami taste! I started making little pastrami sandwiches with the coco bread and cabbage and it reminded me of a fancy Katz deli sandwich! If I had it all to do over again I think I would have ordered the jerked lamb rib because that sounded amazing. I guess it just means multiple trips are a must. Overall this experience was exceptional and highly recommend you put this restaurant on your must list coming to NYC!

This place was such a vibe.. the owner Chef Kwame is a doll and so hospitable. I went here on last minute reservation availability and it was worth it. The ambiance is nice with some rnb and hip hop music playing in the background. Our server was Dee and she was so sweet and attentive. Now let's talk about the food.. appetizers I 10/10 recommend the curried goat patty.. the crusty was flaky and the meat was so flavorful my table ordered 3 orders of this. We also asked for the crab and oxtail Rangoon which I really enjoyed especially with the ginger soy sauce under ( it does have cilantro so if you're not a fan I wouldn't recommend).  For our large plates we tried the scallop guisado which was good especially with a side of brioche to dip in the sauce, probably not enough scallops for two people but I enjoyed it myself. The stewed chicken was A1 the sauce was delicious and the chicken was super tender falling off the bone, it came with a side of rice and peas. The other plate I tasted was the oxtail which I would absolutely recommend, it had also like a glaze on each huge piece of oxtail and no need to worry u can eat this with a fork and knife because it slides right off the bone, again served with rice and peas ( I didn't want rice but I did taste it and felt the rice was under done). The rum cake was very good and a cake with a rum syrup dessert as the name not what the traditional rum cake tastes or looks like. The cheese cake was ok reminded me of a Klondike bar. I tried the Jell-O shots and I enjoyed them especially the passion fruit flavored one but the other guest at my table disagreed. I would definitely return and would love to sit at the bar where u can see inside the kitchen. The place is a great place to celebrate a special event or date night.

Delicious but the only reason I'm giving it a 4 star is because the pastrami was $86 and felt like a good pastrami but not $86 worth. 
Everything was delicious but for the price point and the hype I can't say I was blown away. 
The only dish I would come back as a must try is the goat pattys.

You never know what to expect with these extremely hyped restaurants. My visit was a pleasant one. I didn't indulge in every dish I wanted to try because I was in a rush however my one dish delivered in spades. The secret to walk ins is to arrive early. I was told they can only sit six people at a time at the bar & there's a 2 hour limit. It's worth mentioning that the music they play is nothing short of epic for an old man like myself. I'm assuming there's daily specials considering that what I choose. Get here asap when in NYC

Valentine's Day dinner. Set menu with tons of choices.
- excellent Jell-O shots
- love the honey okra ate it all with the spiciness
- cooked oysters were excellent 
- the cornbread and caviar was dry for me but my group loved it
- lobster was solid but not very filling for two
- scallops were my favorite. the sauce was so good but wish there was rice!
- great dessert and not overly sweet ice cream

Overall, another 5/5.

First I'll preface this by saying this is the most impossible reservation to get. I waited in the cold 20 degree weather for an hour to get a bar seat, and I didn't even make the first seating. I got there at 4, and I didn't sit till 7. People at the front of the line were there at 1pm and keep in mind this was a Thursday evening, so not even the weekend. The only reason why I give it 4 stars is the wait. The food however, is impeccable. The pastrami was phenomenal, the dumplings were great but overpriced for what you got. Would come back if there's no wait but to wait again for that long, it would be difficult to justify.

If you have a shellfish allergy, DO NOT GO. While the food was alright, my options were very limited due to the restaurant frying EVERYTHING in the same fryer. I'm not sure why Okra and Curried Goat Patties are fried on the same oil as fish and shellfish, which is the most common food allergies. For being the #1 restaurant in NYC, I'd expect to have a seperate fryer for seafood/shellfish. Severe cross contamination can occur and reactions can occur to any of the diners  Be Aware. Won't be back.

Wow wow wow! This experience might just be my death row meal. I'm shooketh ! 

Must order:

Seelip pineapple mocktail (don't ask questions) 

Cornbread - light and was a corn variance of olive oil cake 10/10

Goat curry patties - these were next level rich with balanced flavors of sweet and savory and fatty with the sauce and crispy with the shell - unreal I will dream about this dish 


The oxtail was rich and melted in your mouth drenched in a glaze that had a nice spicy kick! 
Lamb - amazing sauce fall off the bone.
 
Every single piece of meat (oxtail, lamb, pastrami) was melt in your mouth cooked perfectly and seasoned perfectly. Every corn bread and milk bread was buttery and fluffy like a pillow dream at mattress firm 

The goat curry patties - shut the fck up Those were SHOW STOPPING holy sh!t. With the mango chutney I could cry  

The flavor had soo much depth and felt like a warm hug like idk how to describe it. Almost like Indian food with so much  aromatics and rich sauces I'm in heaven  

Ambiance wise - it's the perfect New York City flare to fine dining with loud blasting hip hop serving amazing food & being able to have conversations as loud as you want - I like it. Our waiter was sweet. 

That cosmic brownie and powered donut dessert - absolute show stopper ! I'd sell my first born for that recipe! 

I would give it 5 stars except we ordered the truffle chopped cheese which we were most excited about and it never came . Let's hope I can get another res here! Again!

OH EM GEE...my meal was AMAZING! Reservations were impossible (especially last minute) BUT I was able to walk in and get a seat at the bar on Wednesday night. So glad I did! Things I loved:

- everything I ordered. Literally. The crab and oxtail Rangoon, the goat beef patties and the pastrami suya...packed with sooo much flavor. Didn't disappoint. 
- the pastrami suya again. 10000/ 10. (the person next to me convinced me to get it...I then convinced the guy on the other side of me to get it) it was that good! Legit melts in your mouth. 
- the service was TOP NOTCH! from the hostesses, to the bartenders, to the managers...10/10. Even though I sat at the bar, I appreciated that the bartender came from behind the bar to take my order, explain the menu etc. nice touch.

There were so many more items on the menu that I wanted to try...which only means I'll have to come back to explore! Great experience! Great food!

I just lost my elite status after 6 years so idk about writing reviews anymore HAHA
but I had to come back to say something about this place.

I WANT to be supportive but to be honest, this place was a bit of a hit or miss with its dishes, and for the level of ambiance and price, I feel like we should not be missing.

Granted, something my friend and I were wondering was whether this place gets hyped up for Caribbean food or food that uses spices and people who aren't familiar just hype it up like "wow I've never tasted anything like this before"

But -- 
I will say, the short ribs (?) or ribs with the buns were actually insanely good -- they are right 100/10 and I would order again.
The goat curry patties? Also very good! 9/10

But the egusi dumplings were just okay 7/10 and to be honest the biggest disappointment for me was the ox tail.

Idk if it's because I'm Korean and the dumpling and the ox tail dish are things I've had before -- and I grew up eating spices -- but there was nothing shocking interesting special or anything noteworthy about this oxtail...wtf?
Maybe I'm bad for thinking this way, but I imagined that at a restaurant so hyped up and so difficult to attend that's charging way up for the food they are serving -- at least there would be creativity involved. But I didn't feel that way here.
I felt strongly with the oxtail I could easily go to another restaurant and get way more oxtail with a more complex or interesting seasoning for less money. 6.5/10 for the flavor, a holistically 5/10 given that we paid 58 dollars for a couple small pieces of something that tasted...middling
That being said - the drinks were good! Very delicious.

You know, I'd say I'd give them a detailed score of maybe 4.1 or 4.2.
It was good and actually I would 100% try the short rib buns and the goat curry patties and their cocktails. I imagine if we had ordered only those it would have been a 4.6/5 experience. But Alas we wanted to try a range of things, and I felt punished for it.
That being said -- I feel like this depends on your familiarity with spices and ethnic (?) food -- as a Korean who grew up with similar dishes, I literally took the first few bites of the oxtail and was like um, I think we have something that's the same and my mom makes this dish better...and that was the end of that dish for me. But maybe if you're someone who's culinarily limited, then you would love this because you would be shocked that people do in fact eat spices. 

But yes all jokes aside it was worth a visit, get the rib the goat curry patty, the drinks -- maybe don't get the other things we got and try something else (and report back) because I could go again but I will NOT get the oxtail.


Also one last point, this restaurant is not super fancy in terms of its food or its ambiance, and one. Thing I didn't like was -- okay cool stay true to the culture and the vibes I love it -- but why do they have to skimp so much on portion size then?? I felt like if you're gunna charge a lot for the dish -- at least overwhelm me and douse me in the culture with generous portions. I say this because one restaurant I couldn't help but think about was San Ho Won In SF -- yes not Caribbean, but a Korean restaurant that is being kinda fancy but kinda culturall "true" and yes their meals are costly too but one thing I love about them that I wish was true here -- is they just are very generous with portion sizes -- and I believe this is part of the culture? So why give us great music, great spices but suddenly when it comes to portion we acting high brow? I personally did not like that and wish that at least give us a lot of food. Then there wouldn't be so many reviews on here saying ohhh 86$ for this dish was crazy -- it's not just cuz of the dish but the portions itself were just way too small and I'm like isn't this place carribean?

Well-deserved acclaim. I never understood why ethnic foods are considered fast casual fare to Americans when they're the most labor intensive and cost much more to make considering the catalog of ingredients. Tatiana honors the Afro-Caribbean cuisine with Michaelin star ingredients, excellent execution, and warm hospitality service. We went on valentines day and were greeted with smiles coming from the host and waitress upon arrival. The ambiance was smart sexy with music just low enough to have a conversation. The menu was a little different since it was pre fixed. I really wanted to try the egusi dumplings but was persuaded not to.. instead, we got the curry chicken patties, crispy okra, and the hamachi escovitch to start. We found ourselves going back for the crispy okra over and over and over. It was so rich and crispy, but don't get me wrong all the apps were incredible. We then got the branzino and wow. Unconventional and refreshing. I'm tired of boring old bronzino with lemon, butter, and 2 grains of salt, you can find this dish 500 times over here in nyc. This had some sort of Caribbean seasoning profile. Warm, earthy, spicy, but still tasted light and delicate. Definitely not to be looked over. Then the oxtail came out.. get it. The spices tasted fresh and aromatic, the gravy was sticky, the meat was tender. The most elevated Jamaican oxtail I've ever had. I got that same high when I have Sichuan cuisine. A feeling i didn't think was reproducible. This was also the first place in years that I've had a california red wine that I liked. Finally, I am by no means a dessert girly but they were also great. The cosmic brownie was sticky and fudgy, and the golden rum cake was addictive. Overall and exceptional experience. I'd definitely be back and you should definitely give it a try.
Outstanding meal, a place I will come back to for sure.  Short rib pastrami is out of this world and a must order.  Everything was great.

Exemplary Service!  Let me begin by saying this is not a restaurant I would have chosen. It's just a tad fussy for me, but not for my daughter so off we went. I still don't know how she gets some of these hard to get reservations, but she does. The dishes were all really good , I had favorites and " fair" choices. The only dish I did not like and was really disappointed in was the crispy okra. Sad it was. Now my daughter is willing to come to the restaurant and show you how it's done in the South. I'm not talking heavy cornmeal either. Let me just say that if you nailed that okra, you would never have an empty seat. Kwame, we are big fans. I can get fried okra, my daughter lives in NYC and has to make it herself. My favorite was the oxtail wontons and oxtails and rice. I had so many dishes, I was exploding. See for yourself. I didn't label all the dishes because I frankly couldn't remember them. I am sure I would have had they been more memorable. For me anyway.,My daughter is actually going back on business next week.
Food was definitely amazing. Worth the hype. Didn't have a reservation, but put my name in and came back in an hour for a walk in.

Have been here twice and had an amazing time and left so full both times! It can be a little hard to find the restaurant as it's literally in the middle of Lincoln Center. The music is always amazing and the service is attentive. The goat patties and oxtail are my favorite dishes, and we got to try the truffle chopped cheese as a special on my most recent visit and it was also so good. The chicken and branzino are also really great dishes with great flavors. Such a great addition to the NYC restaurant scene!

What is there to say that hasn't already been said about Tatiana? The food is delicious, the vibes are just right (elegant but not stuffy) and the service manages to be both chill and efficient at the same time. Pretty much everything we ordered was phenomenal. The menu changes from time to time but based on the current rotation, I highly recommend the cornbread with curried honey butter (a week later, I still think about that butter), Egusi dumplings and braised oxtails. The theme running through the menu is humble dishes, many of which you'll see in different forms in the various ethnic neighborhoods in NYC, elevated to new (and expensive) heights. That thesis may put off some people, but I am a huge fan.

It's only March and I've already found my BEST BITE of 2025... in Tatiana. Tatiana not only wins for best bite of the year, but also wins for BEST SERVICE of the year. Everyone was superrrrr friendly and accommodating. I can definitely see why they're ranked #1 restaurant in NYC 2 years in a row!!

Tatiana has been on my to-go list for a while. But with reservations being absolutely impossible to get, I had to find a good time to try walking in. I ended up trying my luck on a Tuesday afternoon. I arrived around 4:40PM, and there were already 7 groups in front of me. I didn't end up getting seated in the first round (it's still spring so they didn't have outdoor seats yet), but I put my name down for 7:00PM and was seated around 7:05PM in a bar seat.

I had high extremely high expectations, and those expectations were actually met!
- Short Rib Pastrami Suya: 10000/10 (this is THE BEST BITE I've had so far this year. The meat is soooooo tender, the sauce is to die for, and the bread is very buttery. I'd come again and wait in line JUST to eat this.)
- Curried Goat Patties: 10/10 (lovely empanadas with extremely flavorful curried goat inside. Meat was very tender, empanadas were perfectly cooked, and the white sauce that came on the side waa great.)
- Bodega Special: 10/10 (great brownie and great donut-tasting ice cream. Can't say this is the best dessert I've ever had in my life, but it was still great.)
- POG nutcracker: 10/10 (loveedddd the cocktail! It was fruity, not too sweet, and it complemented all the dishes perfectly.)

Note though that the vibes are clubby and "young". It can get a bit loud in there, so it might not be the ideal restaurant if you want to have deeps convos.

I finally made it to Tatiana as a walk in! Myself and my SO (party of 2) arrived in a long (about 20 people in front of us) line shortly after 4:30 PM at the Lincoln Center and was able to secure a reservation at 9 PM. Crazy, I know, but we had low expectations regarding the walk in reservation system so we decided to stay in the area until it was time for our reservation. We returned around 8:30 PM and was seated at 8:46 PM. While we waited in the lobby we were offered the beverage menu and was able to place our drink orders. The hostess were very kind! I'm not sure how many of those other individuals that were standing in line at 4:30 PM actually returned to Tatiana at their given reservation time.

We were seated comfortably at the bar area and I counted at least five other people seated there as well. The bar isn't long or big, but just enough to seat about 7 people. I was definitely excited to support Chef Kwame as I've heard many wonderful things regarding Tatiana and esp from Pete Wells himself per the NYT!

While looking at the menu, the small share and large share plates looked very promising. All shares are mean't to be shared. We decided to start slow to gauge whether or not it would be worth it to indulge in more items. We started with the egusi dumplings, curried goat patties, and crispy okra for our small shares. For our large share we went with the braised oxtails. Everything was seasoned extremely well and if the menu said an item had peppa sauce then you definitely tasted the peppa sauce! Tatiana did not leave any seasonings to our imagination, which I appreciated! However, none of the dishes truly wow'ed us nor justified the pricing for us. (Ex: 3 curried goat patties were $26) I have no cons regarding the food, but our least favorite was the crispy okra. We love some heat (spice), but there were many flavors going on and some a bit more overpowering than the others. Although the food was flavorful and delicious, it was a fairly average dining experience.

Tatiana also has an extensive wine list, but only six white wines and six red wines are offered by the glass while all other wines are offered by the bottles. Although six white wines offered by the glass, I believe it covered all palettes of white wine that a person may be looking for. (Chardonnay, Pinot Noir Blanc, Riesling, Albarino, and Sauvignon Blanc.)

Table Service - We were seated at the bar and the service was okay. The bartender did a nice job of keeping our beverages full. Other kitchen staff / servers brought out each of our plates efficiently. However, the delivery of the plates felt as if they were just throwing the plates down on the counter and running off before we could even say thank you. Things seemed a bit rushed. We really only felt the hospitality with the hostess and for a restaurant of this caliber (with many accolades) we expected more of an upscale experience in terms of customer service.

My expectations for Tatiana (based on the many reviews) were high and with all due respect to Pete Wells, I did not have an experience that would justify Tatiana being ranked New York Times number 1 restaurant in NYC for two years in a row. I left Tatiana still pondering the 'why' behind Pete's decision and behind the hype. I wish Chef Kwame Onwuachi much success, but we will not be returning.

Had the best meal ever with my fav coworkers ever. We literally manifested this like hardest reservation in nyc yet the second time we tried Alexa got the resy!!! Y'all this place was PROFOUNDLY incredible.

We shared everything so heres a breakdown of each dish:

Curried goat patties. STELLAR. Tied for my fav dish. The pastry was crunchy af and the spiced goat had such great flavor. Paired with this beautifully sweet mango chutney, and a mystery white sauce, what a perfect bite.

The other dish tied for my fav was the black bean hummus. Y'all I never had hummus like this omfg this was beyond any hummus ever and it had some lamb on it too... the bread it came with was so crispy too but my only gripe is it came with so little, like we ended up having to eat most of the hummus with our forks (and yet it was still THAT good that way)

Next we had the egusi dumplings. YUPPPP. I been dying to try egusi soup with fufu and after trying these dumplings I only want it so much more. Will be visiting a Nigerian restaurant soon.

Final small plate was the jerk lamb rib. It was cooked to perfection, fell off the bone, and putting it on the piece of bread with the cucumber was another perfect bite.

Onto the large dishes, first we tried the fried branzino. This was pretty good, there were a couple bones but it was ok bc the sauce on top of the fish was so freaking good. Came with a brown rice too that was great.

Next we had the take out mushrooms which the mushrooms on its own were fine, but it came with scallion pancakes and this un freaking believable freaking plum freaking sauce what the actual flipping flip y'all this plum sauce made me tear tf up. So yeah putting the mushrooms on the scallion pancake and then drizzling the plum sauce on top... one of the most perfect perfect bites of the night. Bonus points to this dish being my fav presentation of the night too.

Lastly we had the eggplant schnitzel, which was my fav of the large plates. A fried whole eggplant in a green curry sauce STOPPP IT STFUUUUU that was like pure ecstasy guys literally wtaf...

Ended with dessert and got the bodega special. Gourmet cosmic brownie with powdered donut ice cream. I didn't know you could make a cosmic brownie better than it already is but thats exactly what they did. And the powdered donut ice cream not only was shaped like a powdered donut but literally tasted exactly like it, consistency and everything despite it literally being ice cream!!! 

Wow what a special meal i'm so happy and also that i got to share it with my fav coworkers ive ever had i'm so grateful for :')

Arrived to wait in the walk-in line at 3:55, there were 4 people already in line. We were able to get a seat  at the back window around 5:15pm, which had such an amazing view. 

We ordered the egusi dumplings, fried okra, and goat curry patties for small plates. I highly recommend the fried okra, which were spicy and sweet and so flavorful. The goat patties were pretty good, slightly game-y still, but came with cilantro sauce and mango chutney and really added a lot. Unfortunately, they forgot to deliver our egusi dumplings so can't say much on that. 

Because of a long wait for the braised oxtail, we were given some jell-o shots on the house which were gorgeous and tasty, not very strong. 

The braised oxtail was so tender, very saucy, and was great with the coconut pea rice. They will pack up the leftover oxtail for you.

Lastly, we got the bodega cosmic brownie and powdered donut ice cream which was so cute and honestly delicious! 

Everything tasted high quality and was super exciting and creative, would definitely recommend if you are looking for a flavorful meal with African and Caribbean fusion flavors.

The service is great. Very attentive and warm environment. The music was great, but can be consider a bit loud. The food is divine. I've been 3 times and each  time was an amazing experience . I've also had the honor of trying a variety of their dishes.

The branzino fish is amazing, the only con Is that there are so many bones.

The okra is my favorite appetizer. It's a bit spicy so if you cannot handle spice I would not recommend it. Sometimes they make it crunchy, which I prefer, and sometimes it's a little more mushy. 

The shrimp dish is also another one of my faves. Whatever sauce they use is magnificent.

On Valentine's Day they had a few new items on the menu. I ordered the seafood guisado (a stew like dish) it was a bit too salty to me, I think if they paired it with some type of bread, it would have set the entire dish off. 

The Jell-O shots are such a vibe. I would definitely recommend ordering a round. They are so fun.

I refer the bodega dessert over the cheesecake because the cheesecake was a little too rich for me.

My go to drink is the coquito, it's sooo good. I wish it was larger.

Else else

I will definitely be back a few more times.

Overall, we had a great time at Tatiana.  Our reservation was actually on the same day as my birthday so it ended being a special celebration with my family.  

We tried a variety of different dishes.   Our table had the Cornbread, Ragoons, Cod, Oxtails, Branzino, Brown Stew Chicken, and Short Rib Pastrami.  Everything was tasty and good, though nothing blew me away. 

The dessert stole the show...it was freaking amazing!!! And the jello shots at the end were a nice treat.

Service was good.  The timing of when the food came out was interesting.  Although we weren't tracking the time, it actually made the dining experience longer than it likely needed to be.  One dish took so long we actually forgot we ordered it.

The restaurant is located on the main floor of the building and had nice vibes.

Making a reservation was a pain.  The slots never opened on Resy so I had to email the restaurant to make a reservation.  By the time I did that, I was only able to secure a reservation 5:30, which ended work out well.  

Putting aside the few hiccups, it's definitely worth checking out.  Enjoy!

The whole vibe of this place is ... interesting. The interior does not go well with the overall Lincoln Center architecture. The choice of music makes it feel like a club, and it's so loud you can barely hear the person across the table from you. 
The space is way too small and tables are arranged in rows with waiters walking back and forth the entire evening. I understand them wanting to be attentive but we also had 3 different waiters tending to our table of 2 throughout the evening, so didnt know who we should be flagging for the check. 

Corn bread: 5/5
Cosmic brownie: 5/5
Goat patties: 4/5 
Dumplings: 3/5 - the dough was good but nothing to write home about
Short rib: 2/5 - way too salty and odd combo of putting fresh mint on spiced ribs
Pastrami: 3/5 - decent portion but not worth $120 and also way too salty 

We had a reservation, but it is not worth the walk-in wait to those who want to try that.

Been trying to land a reservation for so long and finally managed to snag a spot! Was soo worth it.

The pastrami was heavenly--so juicy and full of flavor. The goat curry patties were also amazing; just the curry was worth writing home about, but the flaky crust  outside was also amazing. The bodega dessert was a perfect warm gooey brownie.

Now for the stuff that didn't hit: 3/4 of our party thought the rum cake had much too strong of a rum flavor (although our fourth member loved it!). The oxtail entree was okay--to be honest, I thought it tasted similar to the oxtail I get from Caribbean food trucks outside my office. I also thought the Jell-O shots were ok--they didn't taste too strongly of alcohol but also didn't have that much flavor in general (although my friends seemed to like it).

Decor is beautiful with the great view of Lincoln center, but like others have mentioned, the music was a bit loud.

Finally, have to also mention that there was a mix up with the reservation waitlist system, but in the end the team made it right and I was able to get a res eventually. I assume (but am not sure) the restaurant uses such a manual but more error-prone process to avoid bots snatching up the reservations. If that's the case, then I'm okay with going through that stressful process.

Definitely one of the best restaurants in the city and one of the few worth the hype. My wife and I eat all over the city and their pastrami dish is the best dish we've had so far out of any restaurant.

1000/10 worth the experience, I will most certainly be back our host Shay was Amazing!. We had a little hiccup in the beginning , Darnell made sure to come over to make sure we were okay. Back to the good stuff lol, the food!/ drinks!/ ambiance! was certainly everything and more. We had the pleasure of meeting the owner as well, everyone was so welcoming. Plz stop by if you can snag a res!

EVERYTHING pretty much was a standout. We went for all the star dishes and we loved them. I recommend the dumplings, oxtail and crab rangoons, curried goat patties.
The meat on the pastrami suraya was exceptionally tender. My absolute favorite dish of the night was the fried eggplant curry - it was so unique and flavorful and I had never had anything like it. Many dishes had some heat to them.
We loved the bodega special dessert. The golden rum cake was overpowering with rum which was off putting, but we loved the entire meal nonetheless.
The only other comment I'll make is that the ambiance is rather clubby with loud music, so it's not your traditional fine dining restaurant!

Suggestions to the restaurant: I would swap out the plating of the oxtail dish because everything was so dark and we needed to flag an overhead light to see what we needed to cut. Also, the goat patties, bodega special, and dumplings had things that came in 3's when we were 4 people, so I would suggest offering to customize dishes for both even and odd numbers.

This was such an amazing meal!! Fantastic food, fun vibes, and kind service. 

The food:
To start we ordered the Egusi Dumplings, Oxtail and Crab Rangoons, and the Curried Goat Patties. All sooo delicious and enjoyed by everyone. The patties and the rangoons were the favorites of the table.

For entrees we ordered the Crispy Eggplant Curry, the Pastrami Suya, and the Braised Oxtail. The eggplant was very crispy and the curry was delicious, although I will say because of the darkness I think I ended up biting into a bay leaf or two since I couldn't quite see what was on my fork, haha. The pastrami was soooo delicious, so incredibly tender and my favorite dish by far this entire experience!! The oxtail was tender and delicious, although I'm unsure if I would say it was more unique to other oxtail dishes. I will also note here some of the menu items are a little spicy, which is fine for me but something to keep in mind!

For dessert we got the bodega special and the rum cake. The cosmic brownie in the special was so chocolatey and had a great texture. The donuts.. were actually ice cream which we didn't realize haha! They were a bit hard to eat unfortunately but the presentation was very cute. I loved the rum cake, I thought the whipped cream paired so well with the cake and texture was so soft and tender. However! The rum flavor was quite strong, so if you're not a fan of that I'd caution against getting this.

The drinks:
We got the jell-o shots for fun and they were very beautiful! My favorite flavor was the yellow one, the name unfortunately escapes me. We also all got cocktails, which I think were mostly fine. I ordered the Tatiana Tonic, which I think was the most liked at our table.

The service and vibe:
Our waitress was friendly and kind and the food came out relatively fast! I also read reviews about people having to wait for their reservations, but we were seated immediately even though our party arrived a couple minutes early to our reservation (7:15pm on a Friday for a party of 4). The decor of the restaurant was really nice, but the music was a bit loud. Also this may depend on your table placement, but it was a bit dark so we had a little trouble seeing the food at times.

Overall a wonderful experience, definitely recommend, the food was so amazing and I'm grateful to my friend who got our res so we could eat here!!

Wowwwww! absolutely blown away by this Black owned Michelin starred gem. Supporting a Black business with this level of excellence makes the experience totally meaningful.

My partner somehow snagged a reservation here for my birthday last year and it was one of the best birthday dinners I've ever had.

I went with the oxtails, and let me tell you....it was the most unique and exquisite cut of meat I've ever tasted. Tender, flavorful, rich and beautifully presented.

And the dessert? Straight up artwork. I almost didn't want to eat it...it was that beautiful. The jelly like texture and eclectic flavors made it unforgettable. I hope that I can get a reservation for my next birthday!

I am a believer. This place is difficult to get into but totally worth the hype. We booked the private dining room for a birthday party, which let us enjoy with friends and try a little bit of everything! Note there are 6 walk-in spots every day for each seating so people line up. The Saturday we arrived in March, people had started lining up at 2:45 even though it doesn't open until 5 and by 430/445, the line was already insanely long. 

Now to the food. 
- The goat empanadas and the oxtail were out of this world. My two favorites of the night, hands down. 
- The lamb hummus and the pastrami were also amazing though, and very close seconds. 
- The fried Branzino also exceeded my expectations - some of our guests really loved it. 
- The egusi dumplings and hamachi were fine but didn't blow me away. 
- Some guests loved the mama dukes shrimp but my husband and I both found them overcooked. But nonetheless we're impressed by their massive size! 
- I found the cornbread a little hard but my husband enjoyed it and had two pieces. 
- The private dining also came with sides of rice and fried okra, which I didn't love but everything else was so amazing it didn't even matter.
- Dessert platter! I loved the cheesecake and found it very unique (wrapped in chocolate). Was less impressed by the brownie and rum cake (the rum in the rum cake is VERY strong as a warning).

As for drinks, I really loved the POG nutcracker. The Smoke break (a tequila based cocktail) was also good but the POG was definitely my favorite. 

Also as a heads up - it's very loud inside so not a place for a quiet intimate date night. But I loved the music they played and we were with a big rowdy group so it was all good

Over all, this place is OUTSTANDING. One of the best restaurants in NYC. Highly recommend finding a way to get here!

An amazing time at Tatiana's. 10/10 across the board. From the food to the amazing staff. Siria, Shayla and Christian made a phenomenal team creating an unmatched dining experience. Definitely will be back!!!

Overall I enjoyed my spontaneous dinner at Tatiana's. A reservation just happened to fall into our lap, and given how difficult they are to get, there was no way we weren't going. 

I came with a friend and in order of preference, we got the curried goat patties, braised oxtails, jerk lamb rib, and cornbread. I absolutely loved the goat patties as well as the chutneys that came with it. Unfortunately the oxtail and especially the lamb were too salty for my personal preference. The cornbread was not that noteworthy and pricey for the portion size.

The 3 small plates and 1 large plate was the perfect amount for the two of us--in fact, we were both pretty stuffed by the end of it. Our total post tax and tip came out to around $90pp, which is a little on the pricier side but that was to be expected going in. Service was attentive and the atmosphere was pretty classy, though strangely located within Lincoln Center. I'm glad I gave it a try but don't know if I'd be back again.
Amazing this oxtail is imprinted on my brain...I can't wait to come back. Turned my man from a hater to a believer he cant stop talking about Tatiana.

Lively ...great music...great vibes....Great food! Pierre was our server and he was wonderful! 
Curry goat patties
Branzino
Eggplant

We enjoyed it all!

Amazing service, delicious food, cool ambiance! The crab Rangoon and the dessert are my favorites but everything is very special - amazing mix of spices and very unique. Service is very attentive and kind. Advice is to order 2-3 appetizers for 2 people and 1 main. Highly recommend!
Best oxtail ive ever had in my life. Dipping the cornbread in the sauce was AMAZING... i cant wait to go back to nyc, this will be my fist stop
